text: Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.
note: Strength hidden in apparent weakness

tags.when_helps: A believer feeling weak or foolish by worldly standards, reminded that divine strength works differently.

display_text: Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.
plain: God's foolishness is wiser than human wisdom, and God's weakness is stronger than human strength.
core_idea: God's weakness outdoes human strength

text: Let no one deceive himself. If anyone thinks that he is wise among you in this world, let him become a fool, that he may become wise.
note: Humility, intellectual pride, self-deception

keywords: become a fool to be wise
tags.when_helps: Someone sure of their own cleverness who may need to unlearn before they can truly learn.

display_text: Let no one deceive himself. If anyone thinks that he is wise among you in this world, let him become a fool, that he may become wise.
plain: Do not fool yourself. If you think you are wise by this world's standards, become a fool so that you may become truly wise.
core_idea: Become a fool to become truly wise

text: But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you, or by man’s judgment. Yes, I don’t judge my own self. For I know nothing against myself. Yet I am not justified by this, but he who judges me is the Lord. Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and reveal the counsels of the hearts. Then each man will get his praise from God.
note: Freedom from others' judgment and harsh self-judgment

keywords: a very small thing to be judged by you
tags.when_helps: Someone stung by others' judgement, or harsh on themselves, freed from needing a human verdict.

display_text: But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you, or by man’s judgment. Yes, I don’t judge my own self. For I know nothing against myself. Yet I am not justified by this, but he who judges me is the Lord. Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and reveal the counsels of the hearts. Then each man will get his praise from God.
plain: It matters little to me if you or any human court judges me; I do not even judge myself. A clear conscience does not acquit me; the Lord judges. So judge nothing before he comes and reveals hearts.
core_idea: Leave judgment to the Lord, not people

plain_judge.issue: Drops the Lord exposing hidden things and each receiving praise from God.

text: For who makes you different? And what do you have that you didn’t receive? But if you did receive it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?
note: Pride, gratitude, everything we have is received

keywords: what do you have that you didn't receive
tags.when_helps: Someone proud of their gifts who is reminded that everything they have was received.

display_text: For who makes you different? And what do you have that you didn’t receive? But if you did receive it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?
plain: Who makes you better than anyone else? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why boast as if you had not?
core_idea: Everything you have was given; why boast?

plain_judge.issue: 'Makes you different' rendered as 'makes you better than anyone else', a slight shift.

text: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are expedient. “All things are lawful for me,” but I will not be brought under the power of anything.
note: Freedom without being mastered by habits or cravings

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
keywords: not brought under the power of anything
tags.when_helps: Someone justifying a habit because it's allowed, asked whether it is mastering them.

display_text: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are expedient. “All things are lawful for me,” but I will not be brought under the power of anything.
plain: Everything is permitted to me, but not everything is helpful. Everything is permitted to me, but I will not let anything master me.
core_idea: Not everything allowed is good for you

text: Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up. But if anyone thinks that he knows anything, he doesn’t yet know as he ought to know.
note: Intellectual pride versus love; humility about knowing

keywords: knowledge puffs up, love builds up
tags.when_helps: Someone who prides themselves on knowing, reminded that love builds what knowledge alone cannot.

display_text: Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up. But if anyone thinks that he knows anything, he doesn’t yet know as he ought to know.
plain: Knowledge makes people proud, but love builds them up. Anyone who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he should.
core_idea: Knowledge puffs up; love builds up

text: Don’t you know that those who run in a race all run, but one receives the prize? Run like that, that you may win. Every man who strives in the games exercises self-control in all things. Now they do it to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible.
note: Discipline, effort and purpose in striving

tags.when_helps: Someone in training or a long effort who needs motivation for discipline and focus.

display_text: Don’t you know that those who run in a race all run, but one receives the prize? Run like that, that you may win. Every man who strives in the games exercises self-control in all things. Now they do it to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible.
plain: In a race all runners run, but only one wins the prize, so run to win. Athletes train with strict self-control for a crown that fades; we do it for one that lasts forever.
core_idea: Run with discipline for a lasting prize

text: Therefore let him who thinks he stands be careful that he doesn’t fall. No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.
note: Temptation, overconfidence, strength to endure

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone facing temptation who feels it is unbearable, assured that it is common and a way through exists.

display_text: Therefore let him who thinks he stands be careful that he doesn’t fall. No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.
plain: If you think you stand firm, be careful not to fall. Every temptation you face is common to people. God is faithful: he will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear, and will provide a way out.
core_idea: God never lets temptation exceed what you can bear

text: Let no one seek his own, but each one his neighbor’s good.
note: Selfishness versus care for others

tags.when_helps: Someone caught up in their own interests who could find direction by seeking another's good.

display_text: Let no one seek his own, but each one his neighbor’s good.
plain: No one should look out only for themselves; each should seek the good of others.
core_idea: Seek others' good, not just your own

plain_judge.issue: Adds 'only', softening 'let no one seek his own' into a milder saying.

text: The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.” No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.
note: Feeling unneeded; the worth of the overlooked

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels weak or unneeded in their group, reminded that every member is necessary.

display_text: The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.” No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.
plain: The eye cannot tell the hand it does not need it, nor the head tell the feet. In fact, the parts of the body that seem weaker are essential.
core_idea: The parts that seem weakest are essential

text: When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. Or when one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
note: Shared suffering and joy in community

tags.when_helps: Someone suffering or celebrating who needs to know their community shares it with them.

display_text: When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. Or when one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
plain: When one part of the body suffers, every part suffers with it; when one part is honoured, every part rejoices with it.
core_idea: We suffer and rejoice together

text: If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but don’t have love, I have become sounding brass, or a clanging cymbal. If I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge; and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but don’t have love, I am nothing. If I give away all my goods to feed the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but don’t have love, it profits me nothing.
note: Achievement is empty without love

tags.when_helps: Someone proud of their gifts or good deeds who needs reminding that without love they count for nothing.

display_text: If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but don’t have love, I have become sounding brass, or a clanging cymbal. If I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge; and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but don’t have love, I am nothing. If I give away all my goods to feed the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but don’t have love, it profits me nothing.
plain: If I speak every human and angelic language but lack love, I am just a noisy gong. With prophecy, all knowledge and mountain-moving faith but no love, I am nothing. Giving everything away without love gains me nothing.
core_idea: Without love, every gift is worthless

plain_judge.issue: Drops giving one's body to be burned.

text: Love is patient and is kind; love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud, doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil; doesn’t rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never fails.
note: What love is: patience, kindness, endurance

tags.when_helps: Someone in a close relationship testing their patience who wants a picture of what love really asks.

display_text: Love is patient and is kind; love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud, doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil; doesn’t rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never fails.
plain: Love is patient and kind; it does not envy, boast or act proud. It is not rude, selfish or easily angered, and keeps no record of wrongs. It delights in truth and bears, hopes and endures everything. Love never fails.
core_idea: Love is patient and kind, and never fails

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'believes all things' and 'does not rejoice in unrighteousness'.

text: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I felt as a child, I thought as a child. Now that I have become a man, I have put away childish things. For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know fully, even as I was also fully known. But now faith, hope, and love remain—these three. The greatest of these is love.
note: Growing up, partial understanding, what remains

tags.when_helps: Someone growing up or changing who accepts they see only in part and wants to know what lasts.

display_text: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I felt as a child, I thought as a child. Now that I have become a man, I have put away childish things. For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know fully, even as I was also fully known. But now faith, hope, and love remain—these three. The greatest of these is love.
plain: As a child I spoke and thought like a child; grown up, I put childish ways aside. Now we see dimly, as in a mirror, then face to face. Faith, hope and love remain, and the greatest is love.
core_idea: Faith, hope and love remain; love is greatest

plain_judge.issue: Drops knowing in part now, fully then, as I am fully known.

text: But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
note: Unworthiness, past wrongs, accepting who you are

keywords: by the grace of God I am what I am
tags.when_helps: A believer unsure of their worth or troubled by their past who can rest in being what grace has made them.

display_text: But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
plain: By God's grace I am what I am. His grace toward me was not wasted; I worked harder than all the others, yet it was not I but God's grace working with me.
core_idea: By God's grace I am what I am

text: Don’t be deceived! “Evil companionships corrupt good morals.”
note: The influence of bad company

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone noticing that the people they spend time with are pulling them away from their values.

display_text: Don’t be deceived! “Evil companionships corrupt good morals.”
plain: Do not be fooled: bad company corrupts good character.
core_idea: Bad company corrupts good character

text: But when this perishable body will have become imperishable, and this mortal will have put on immortality, then what is written will happen: “Death is swallowed up in victory.” “Death, where is your sting? Hades, where is your victory?” The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law. But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
note: Grief and death; hope beyond mortality

tags.when_helps: A Christian afraid of death or grieving who needs the triumphant hope that death does not have the last word.

display_text: But when this perishable body will have become imperishable, and this mortal will have put on immortality, then what is written will happen: “Death is swallowed up in victory.” “Death, where is your sting? Hades, where is your victory?” The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law. But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
plain: When our mortal bodies become immortal, the saying comes true: death is swallowed up in victory. Death, where is your sting? Sin is death's sting, and the law gives sin power. Thank God for victory through Jesus Christ.
core_idea: Through Christ, death loses its sting

text: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
note: Perseverance when work feels futile

tags.when_helps: A believer wondering whether their work and effort matter who needs to hear it is not in vain.

display_text: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
plain: So, dear brothers and sisters, stand firm and unshakable, always giving yourselves fully to the Lord's work, knowing that your work in the Lord is never wasted.
core_idea: Stand firm; work for the Lord is never wasted

plain_judge.issue: Widens 'brothers' to 'brothers and sisters'.

text: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong! Let all that you do be done in love.
note: Courage and strength, tempered by love

tags.when_helps: A believer facing a challenge who needs a short rallying call to be strong while acting in love.

display_text: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong! Let all that you do be done in love.
plain: Stay alert, stand firm in the faith, be brave and strong. Do everything in love.
core_idea: Be brave and strong, and do everything in love

text: Then began the first, who had spoken of the strength of wine, and said thus, O sirs, how exceeding strong is wine! it causes all men to err that drink it: it makes the mind of the king and of the fatherless child to be all one; of the bondman and of the freeman, of the poor man and of the rich: it turns also every thought into jollity and mirth, so that a man remembers neither sorrow nor debt: and it makes every heart rich, so that a man remembers neither king nor satrap; and it makes to speak all things by talents: and when they are in their cups, they forget their love both to friends and kindred, and a little after draw their swords: but when they awake from their wine, they remember not what they have done. O sirs, is not wine the strongest, seeing that it enforces to do thus?
note: Drinking to forget sorrow; how alcohol overpowers people

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone reflecting on how drink takes hold and makes people forget themselves and those they love.

display_text: Then began the first, who had spoken of the strength of wine, and said thus, O sirs, how exceeding strong is wine! it causes all men to err that drink it: it makes the mind of the king and of the fatherless child to be all one; of the bondman and of the freeman, of the poor man and of the rich: it turns also every thought into jollity and mirth, so that a man remembers neither sorrow nor debt: and it makes every heart rich, so that a man remembers neither king nor satrap; and it makes to speak all things by talents: and when they are in their cups, they forget their love both to friends and kindred, and a little after draw their swords: but when they awake from their wine, they remember not what they have done. O sirs, is not wine the strongest, seeing that it enforces to do thus?
plain: The first speaker said: how strong wine is! It leads drinkers astray, makes king and orphan, rich and poor alike, drowns sorrow and debt, turns friends to drawn swords, and afterwards they remember nothing. Is wine not strongest?
core_idea: Wine overpowers everyone, making them forget and err

text: All the earth calls upon truth, and the heaven blesses her: all works shake and tremble, but with her is no unrighteous thing. Wine is unrighteous, the king is unrighteous, women are unrighteous, all the children of men are unrighteous, and unrighteous are all such their works; and there is no truth in them; in their unrighteousness also they shall perish. But truth remains, and is strong forever; she lives and conquers forevermore. With her there is no accepting of persons or rewards; but she does the things that are just, and refrains from all unrighteous and wicked things; and all men do well like of her works. Neither in her judgment is any unrighteousness; and she is the strength, and the kingdom, and the power, and the majesty, of all ages. Blessed be the God of truth.
note: Truth outlasting power, pleasure and wrongdoing

tags.when_helps: Someone disillusioned by everyone's failings who needs to hear that truth itself endures and prevails.

display_text: All the earth calls upon truth, and the heaven blesses her: all works shake and tremble, but with her is no unrighteous thing. Wine is unrighteous, the king is unrighteous, women are unrighteous, all the children of men are unrighteous, and unrighteous are all such their works; and there is no truth in them; in their unrighteousness also they shall perish. But truth remains, and is strong forever; she lives and conquers forevermore. With her there is no accepting of persons or rewards; but she does the things that are just, and refrains from all unrighteous and wicked things; and all men do well like of her works. Neither in her judgment is any unrighteousness; and she is the strength, and the kingdom, and the power, and the majesty, of all ages. Blessed be the God of truth.
plain: All the earth calls on truth and heaven blesses it. Wine, kings, women and all people are unjust and will perish, but truth stays strong forever, takes no bribes and does what is just. Blessed be the God of truth.
core_idea: Truth outlasts and outranks everything

plain_judge.issue: Drops truth as the strength, kingdom, power and majesty of all ages.

text: Also of the priests the Levites, and of the heads of their families, the ancients who had seen the former house came to the building of this with lamentation and great weeping. But many with trumpets and joy shouted with loud voice, insomuch that the people heard not the trumpets for the weeping of the people: for the multitude sounded marvelously, so that it was heard afar off.
note: Grief for what was lost mingled with joy at rebuilding

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling both joy at a new beginning and grief for what was, who sees both held together.

display_text: Also of the priests the Levites, and of the heads of their families, the ancients who had seen the former house came to the building of this with lamentation and great weeping. But many with trumpets and joy shouted with loud voice, insomuch that the people heard not the trumpets for the weeping of the people: for the multitude sounded marvelously, so that it was heard afar off.
plain: When the new temple was founded, old priests and elders who remembered the first one wept aloud, while many others shouted for joy with trumpets, so that weeping and joy could not be told apart, and the noise carried far.
core_idea: Weeping for the past mingled with joy for the new

text: I said, O Lord, I am ashamed and confounded before your face; for our sins are multiplied above our heads, and our errors have reached up to heaven, ever since the time of our fathers; and we are in great sin, even to this day.
note: Shame and confession over long-standing wrongdoing

tags.when_helps: A believer overwhelmed by a sense of long-accumulated wrongdoing, looking for words to confess it.

display_text: I said, O Lord, I am ashamed and confounded before your face; for our sins are multiplied above our heads, and our errors have reached up to heaven, ever since the time of our fathers; and we are in great sin, even to this day.
plain: I said: Lord, I am ashamed and confused before you, for our sins are piled above our heads and our wrongs reach up to heaven, from our ancestors' time until today.
core_idea: Ashamed before God of sins piled high

text: This day is holy to the Lord; (now they all wept when they heard the law:) go then, and eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions to those who have nothing; for the day is holy to the Lord: and be not sorrowful; for the Lord will bring you to honor.
note: Setting sorrow aside to celebrate and share with others

tags.when_helps: A believer weighed down by remorse on a day meant for celebration, invited to rejoice and share.

display_text: This day is holy to the Lord; (now they all wept when they heard the law:) go then, and eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions to those who have nothing; for the day is holy to the Lord: and be not sorrowful; for the Lord will bring you to honor.
plain: As the people wept on hearing the law, they were told: this day is holy to the Lord, so go and feast, send portions to those who have nothing, and do not grieve, for the Lord will bring you honour.
core_idea: On a holy day, feast, share and stop grieving

text: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
note: Guilt, honesty about failings, and forgiveness

tags.when_helps: A Christian aware of their wrongs who needs honesty about them and assurance of forgiveness.

display_text: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
plain: If we claim to have no sin, we fool ourselves and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, God is faithful and just, and will forgive us and cleanse us of all wrongdoing.
core_idea: Confess your sins and God will forgive

text: He who says he is in the light and hates his brother, is in the darkness even until now. He who loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no occasion for stumbling in him. But he who hates his brother is in the darkness, and walks in the darkness, and doesn’t know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.
note: Hatred and resentment blinding us

tags.when_helps: Someone holding hatred toward a brother or neighbour who needs to see how it blinds them.

display_text: He who says he is in the light and hates his brother, is in the darkness even until now. He who loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no occasion for stumbling in him. But he who hates his brother is in the darkness, and walks in the darkness, and doesn’t know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.
plain: Whoever claims to be in the light but hates a brother is still in darkness. Whoever loves a brother stays in the light and does not stumble; whoever hates walks blind in darkness, not knowing where he goes.
core_idea: Hatred blinds; love keeps you in the light

text: Don’t love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love isn’t in him. For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, isn’t the Father’s, but is the world’s. The world is passing away with its lusts, but he who does God’s will remains forever.
note: Desire, status and what lasts

keywords: lust of the eyes, pride of life
tags.when_helps: A believer pulled by worldly desires and status who needs reminding these pass away.

display_text: Don’t love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love isn’t in him. For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, isn’t the Father’s, but is the world’s. The world is passing away with its lusts, but he who does God’s will remains forever.
plain: Do not love the world or its things; whoever loves the world lacks the Father's love. Its lusts and pride do not come from the Father. The world and its desires are passing, but whoever does God's will lives forever.
core_idea: The world passes; doing God's will lasts forever

text: My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.
note: Love shown in action, not words

tags.when_helps: Someone who wants their love to show in actions rather than only words.

display_text: My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.
plain: Dear children, let us not love just with words or talk, but with actions and in truth.
core_idea: Love in deeds, not just words

text: Beloved, let us love one another, for love is of God; and everyone who loves has been born of God, and knows God. He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.
note: Love as the heart of faith

tags.when_helps: A believer reflecting on love as the heart of knowing God.

display_text: Beloved, let us love one another, for love is of God; and everyone who loves has been born of God, and knows God. He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.
plain: Dear friends, let us love one another, because love comes from God; everyone who loves is born of God and knows God. Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.
core_idea: God is love, so love one another

text: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love.
note: Fear and love

tags.when_helps: Someone gripped by fear of punishment or rejection who needs to hear that love drives out fear.

display_text: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love.
plain: There is no fear in love; perfect love drives out fear, because fear has to do with punishment. Whoever is afraid has not been made perfect in love.
core_idea: Perfect love drives out fear

text: If a man says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who doesn’t love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?
note: Hypocrisy, hating others while claiming faith

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
keywords: he who hates his brother is a liar
tags.when_helps: A believer holding hatred for someone who needs to face that love of God and of people cannot be separated.

display_text: If a man says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who doesn’t love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?
plain: Anyone who says "I love God" but hates his brother is a liar, for if he does not love the brother he can see, how can he love God, whom he has not seen?
core_idea: You cannot love God while hating others

text: Now the days of David came near that he should die; and he commanded Solomon his son, saying, “I am going the way of all the earth. You be strong therefore, and show yourself a man; and keep the instruction of Yahweh your God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, his commandments, his ordinances, and his testimonies, according to that which is written in the law of Moses, that you may prosper in all that you do, and wherever you turn yourself.
note: A dying parent's last counsel to a child

keywords: the way of all the earth
tags.when_helps: Someone receiving a dying parent's last charge, or stepping into a parent's role after them.

display_text: Now the days of David came near that he should die; and he commanded Solomon his son, saying, “I am going the way of all the earth. You be strong therefore, and show yourself a man; and keep the instruction of Yahweh your God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, his commandments, his ordinances, and his testimonies, according to that which is written in the law of Moses, that you may prosper in all that you do, and wherever you turn yourself.
plain: Dying, David told his son Solomon: I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong and act like a man; keep God's law and walk in his ways, so you prosper in all you do, wherever you go.
core_idea: Be strong and walk in God's ways

text: Now, Yahweh my God, you have made your servant king instead of David my father. I am just a little child. I don’t know how to go out or come in. Your servant is among your people which you have chosen, a great people, that can’t be numbered or counted for multitude. Give your servant therefore an understanding heart to judge your people, that I may discern between good and evil; for who is able to judge this great people of yours?”
note: Feeling inadequate to a new responsibility; asking for wisdom

situations: a career change or new job
keywords: I am just a little child
tags.when_helps: A believer newly given great responsibility who feels like a child and asks for wisdom.

display_text: Now, Yahweh my God, you have made your servant king instead of David my father. I am just a little child. I don’t know how to go out or come in. Your servant is among your people which you have chosen, a great people, that can’t be numbered or counted for multitude. Give your servant therefore an understanding heart to judge your people, that I may discern between good and evil; for who is able to judge this great people of yours?
plain: Solomon prayed: Lord my God, you made me king after my father, but I am like a little child who does not know how to lead. Give me an understanding heart to judge your people and tell good from evil.
core_idea: Ask God for an understanding heart

text: “Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of Yahweh, the God of Israel. But Yahweh said to David my father, ‘Whereas it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart. Nevertheless, you shall not build the house; but your son who shall come out of your body, he shall build the house for my name.’
note: A dream you won't fulfil yourself; good intentions still count

situations: loss of a dream or plan
keywords: you did well that it was in your heart
tags.when_helps: Someone whose cherished plan will not be fulfilled by them, consoled that the intention itself was good.

display_text: Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of Yahweh, the God of Israel. text: King Rehoboam took counsel with the old men, who had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, “What counsel do you give me to answer these people?” They replied, “If you will be a servant to this people today, and will serve them, and answer them with good words, then they will be your servants forever.”

situations: a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: A new leader deciding how to treat the people under them, advised to serve with kind words.

text: She said, “As Yahweh your God lives, I don’t have a cake, but a handful of meal in a jar, and a little oil in a jar. Behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and bake it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.” Elijah said to her, “Don’t be afraid. Go and do as you have said; but make me a little cake from it first, and bring it out to me, and afterward make some for you and for your son. For Yahweh, the God of Israel says, ‘The jar of meal will not run out, and the jar of oil will not fail, until the day that Yahweh sends rain on the earth.’”
note: Scarcity, despair, and trusting enough to give anyway

tags.when_helps: A believer down to their last resources, fearing for their family, who needs to trust provision will come.

text: Elijah came near to all the people, and said, “How long will you waver between the two sides? If Yahweh is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him.” The people didn’t say a word.

tags.when_helps: Someone wavering between two ways of life who needs to commit to one.

display_text: Elijah came near to all the people, and said, “How long will you waver between the two sides? If Yahweh is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him.” The people didn’t say a word.
plain: Elijah asked the people: how long will you keep wavering between two sides? If the Lord is God, follow him; if Baal is, follow Baal. The people said nothing.
core_idea: Stop wavering; choose whom you will follow

text: Behold, Yahweh passed by, and a great and strong wind tore the mountains, and broke in pieces the rocks before Yahweh; but Yahweh was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake; but Yahweh was not in the earthquake. After the earthquake a fire passed; but Yahweh was not in the fire. After the fire, there was a still small voice.
note: Finding the quiet voice amid turmoil

tags.when_helps: Someone seeking the sacred in dramatic events who may find it instead in quiet.

display_text: Behold, Yahweh passed by, and a great and strong wind tore the mountains, and broke in pieces the rocks before Yahweh; but Yahweh was not in the wind. plain: God passed by: a mighty wind tore the mountains and smashed rocks, but God was not in the wind. Nor was God in the earthquake that followed, nor in the fire. After the fire came a still, small voice.
core_idea: God came not in the storm but quietly

text: The messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, “See now, the prophets declare good to the king with one mouth. Please let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak good.” Micaiah said, “As Yahweh lives, what Yahweh says to me, that I will speak.”
note: Telling the truth under pressure to conform

tags.when_helps: Someone pressured to tell those in power only what they want to hear.

display_text: The messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, “See now, the prophets declare good to the king with one mouth. Please let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak good.” Micaiah said, “As Yahweh lives, what Yahweh says to me, that I will speak.”
plain: The messenger urged Micaiah to agree with the other prophets and tell the king good news. Micaiah answered: as the Lord lives, I will say whatever the Lord tells me.

text: And be not afraid of the words of a sinful man; for his glory shall be dung and worms. To-day he shall be lifted up, and to-morrow he shall in no wise be found, because he is returned to his dust, and his thought is perished.
note: Fear of a powerful or threatening person; their power passes

tags.when_helps: Someone intimidated by a powerful wrongdoer's words who needs reminding such power is passing.

display_text: And be not afraid of the words of a sinful man; for his glory shall be dung and worms. To-day he shall be lifted up, and to-morrow he shall in no wise be found, because he is returned to his dust, and his thought is perished.
plain: Do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory will end in dung and worms. Today he is raised up; tomorrow he is gone, returned to dust, and his plans have perished.
core_idea: Don't fear the boasting of the wicked; they pass

text: And Judas said, It is an easy thing for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with heaven it is all one, to save by many or by few: for victory in battle stands not in the multitude of an army; but strength is from heaven.
note: Feeling outnumbered or outmatched; courage against odds

tags.when_helps: A believer badly outnumbered or outmatched who needs courage that strength is not in numbers.

display_text: And Judas said, It is an easy thing for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with heaven it is all one, to save by many or by few: for victory in battle stands not in the multitude of an army; but strength is from heaven.

core_idea: Strength comes from heaven, not numbers

text: And Simon called his two oldest sons, Judas and John, and said to them, I and my kindred and my father’s house have fought the battles of Israel from our youth, even to this day; and things have prospered in our hands, that we should deliver Israel oftentimes. But now I am old, and you⌃ moreover, by his mercy, are of a sufficient age: be you⌃ instead of me and my brother, and go forth and fight for our nation; but let the help which is from heaven be with you.
note: Ageing; handing responsibility to the next generation

tags.when_helps: An older person handing on their life's work to the next generation and blessing them.

display_text: And Simon called his two oldest sons, Judas and John, and said to them, I and my kindred and my father’s house have fought the battles of Israel from our youth, even to this day; and things have prospered in our hands, that we should deliver Israel oftentimes. plain: Simon told his two eldest sons: my family and I have fought Israel's battles since youth and often won. Now I am old and you are grown; take our place and fight for our nation, and may heaven help you.
core_idea: The old hand on the struggle to the young

text: For, “All flesh is like grass, and all of man’s glory like the flower in the grass. The grass withers, and its flower falls; but the Lord’s word endures forever.”
note: transience of life and achievement

tags.when_helps: Someone reflecting on how quickly human glory fades and seeking what endures.

display_text: For, “All flesh is like grass, and all of man’s glory like the flower in the grass. The grass withers, and its flower falls; but the Lord’s word endures forever.”
plain: All people are like grass, and all human glory like a wildflower. The grass dries up and the flower falls, but the Lord's word lasts forever.
core_idea: Human glory fades; God's word endures

text: Let your beauty be not just the outward adorning of braiding the hair, and of wearing jewels of gold, or of putting on fine clothing; but in the hidden person of the heart, in the incorruptible adornment of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God very precious.

display_text: Let your beauty be not just the outward adorning of braiding the hair, and of wearing jewels of gold, or of putting on fine clothing; but in the hidden person of the heart, in the incorruptible adornment of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God very precious.

text: Finally, be all like-minded, compassionate, loving as brothers, tender hearted, courteous, not rendering evil for evil, or insult for insult; but instead blessing; knowing that to this were you called, that you may inherit a blessing. display_text: For man looks at the outward appearance, but Yahweh looks at the heart.

display_text: We exhort you, brothers, admonish the disorderly, encourage the faint-hearted, support the weak, be patient toward all. See that no one returns evil for evil to anyone, but always follow after that which is good, for one another, and for all. Rejoice always. Pray without ceasing. In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you.
plain: Paul urges correcting the unruly, encouraging the timid, helping the weak and being patient with everyone. Never repay wrong with wrong; always seek good. Rejoice always, pray constantly, and give thanks in everything, as God wills.
core_idea: Be patient, do good, rejoice, pray and give thanks.

plain_judge.issue: Reported as 'Paul urges' rather than direct exhortation; drops 'for one another, and for all'.

text: The saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief. However, for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first, Jesus Christ might display all his patience, for an example of those who were going to believe in him for eternal life.
note: guilt over past wrongs; mercy

tags.when_helps: A Christian who feels they are the worst of sinners and needs to see mercy shown to such a one.

display_text: The saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief. However, for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first, Jesus Christ might display all his patience, for an example of those who were going to believe in him for eternal life.
plain: It is true and worth accepting that Christ Jesus came to save sinners, and Paul counts himself the worst. He was shown mercy so Jesus could display his patience in him as an example for future believers.
core_idea: Even the worst sinner can receive mercy.

plain_judge.issue: Recast in third person; drops 'for eternal life'.

text: Let no man despise your youth; but be an example to those who believe, in word, in your way of life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.
note: being young and not taken seriously

situations: a career change or new job
keywords: let no one despise your youth
tags.when_helps: A young person not taken seriously because of their age who needs encouragement to lead by example.

display_text: Let no man despise your youth; but be an example to those who believe, in word, in your way of life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.
plain: Do not let anyone look down on you for being young. Instead, set an example for believers in how you speak, live, love, and in your spirit, faith and purity.
core_idea: Being young is no bar to setting an example.

text: But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can’t carry anything out. But having food and clothing, we will be content with that. But those who are determined to be rich fall into a temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful lusts, such as drown men in ruin and destruction. For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some have been led astray from the faith in their greed, and have pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
note: contentment, money, greed

keywords: we brought nothing into the world
tags.when_helps: Someone driven by the wish for more money who needs reminding that food, clothing and contentment are enough.

display_text: But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can’t carry anything out. But having food and clothing, we will be content with that. But those who are determined to be rich fall into a temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful lusts, such as drown men in ruin and destruction. For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some have been led astray from the faith in their greed, and have pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
plain: Living for God with contentment is real wealth. We bring nothing into the world and take nothing out, so food and clothing are enough. Chasing riches leads to ruin; loving money is a root of every kind of evil.
core_idea: Contentment is wealth; love of money brings ruin.

plain_judge.issue: Drops those led from the faith by greed, pierced with many sorrows.

text: Charge those who are rich in this present world that they not be haughty, nor have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on the living God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy; that they do good, that they be rich in good works, that they be ready to distribute, willing to share; laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold of eternal life.
note: wealth, generosity, uncertain riches

tags.when_helps: Someone with wealth tempted to rely on it who needs reminding to hold it lightly and share.

display_text: Charge those who are rich in this present world that they not be haughty, nor have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on the living God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy; that they do good, that they be rich in good works, that they be ready to distribute, willing to share; laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold of eternal life.
plain: Tell the rich not to be proud or trust uncertain wealth, but to trust the living God who gives everything to enjoy. They should do good, be generous and share, building a foundation for eternal life.
core_idea: The rich should trust God and be generous.

text: That night, God appeared to Solomon and said to him, “Ask for what you want me to give you.” Solomon said to God, “You have shown great loving kindness to David my father, and have made me king in his place. Now, Yahweh God, let your promise to David my father be established; for you have made me king over a people like the dust of the earth in multitude. Now give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people; for who can judge this great people of yours?”
note: Feeling unequal to a new responsibility; asking for wisdom

situations: a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: A believer facing a large new responsibility who chooses to ask for wisdom above all.

display_text: That night, God appeared to Solomon and said to him, “Ask for what you want me to give you.” Solomon said to God, “You have shown great loving kindness to David my father, and have made me king in his place. Now, Yahweh God, let your promise to David my father be established; for you have made me king over a people like the dust of the earth in multitude. Now give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people; for who can judge this great people of yours?”
plain: God tells Solomon to ask for anything. Solomon thanks God for his kindness to David and, feeling the weight of ruling a vast people, asks only for wisdom and knowledge to lead them.
core_idea: Asked for anything, Solomon asks for wisdom.

text: Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of Yahweh, the God of Israel. But Yahweh said to David my father, ‘Whereas it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart; nevertheless you shall not build the house; but your son who will come out of your body, he shall build the house for my name.’
note: A good intention you won't live to complete

situations: loss of a dream or plan
keywords: you did well that it was in your heart
tags.when_helps: Someone who will not see their life's hope fulfilled, consoled that the desire was good and others may complete it.

display_text: Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of Yahweh, the God of Israel. But Yahweh said to David my father, ‘Whereas it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart; nevertheless you shall not build the house; but your son who will come out of your body, he shall build the house for my name.’
plain: David wanted to build a temple for God. God told him it was good that he wanted to, but that his son, not he, would build it.
core_idea: A good intention matters even if another fulfils it.

text: “If I shut up the sky so that there is no rain, or if I command the locust to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among my people; if my people, who are called by my name, will humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then I will hear from heaven, will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.
note: Humility and turning back bring healing

tags.when_helps: A believer in hard times seeking a way back through humility, prayer and turning around.

display_text: If I shut up the sky so that there is no rain, or if I command the locust to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among my people; if my people, who are called by my name, will humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then I will hear from heaven, will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.
plain: God says that when he brings drought, locusts or plague, if his people humble themselves, pray, seek him and turn from their wrongdoing, he will hear them, forgive them and heal their land.
core_idea: Humility and turning from wrong bring God's healing.

text: King Rehoboam took counsel with the old men, who had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, “What counsel do you give me about how to answer these people?” They spoke to him, saying, “If you are kind to these people, please them, and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants forever.” But he abandoned the counsel of the old men which they had given him, and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
note: Choosing whose advice to heed; leading with kindness

situations: a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to ignore experienced advice in favour of what their peers want to hear.

display_text: King Rehoboam took counsel with the old men, who had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, “What counsel do you give me about how to answer these people?” They spoke to him, saying, “If you are kind to these people, please them, and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants forever.” But he abandoned the counsel of the old men which they had given him, and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
plain: King Rehoboam asked his father's old advisers what to do; they said that if he was kind to the people, they would serve him forever. But he rejected their advice and turned to the young men he grew up with.
core_idea: Rejecting wise elders' counsel for peers' approval.

text: Yahweh, there is no one besides you to help, between the mighty and him who has no strength. Help us, Yahweh our God; for we rely on you, and in your name are we come against this multitude. Yahweh, you are our God. Don’t let man prevail against you.
note: Feeling powerless against overwhelming odds; asking for help

keywords: no one besides you to help
tags.when_helps: A believer facing overwhelming odds who has nowhere left to turn but God.

display_text: Yahweh, there is no one besides you to help, between the mighty and him who has no strength. Help us, Yahweh our God; for we rely on you, and in your name are we come against this multitude. Yahweh, you are our God. Don’t let man prevail against you.
plain: A prayer to the Lord: only you can help the weak against the strong. Help us, for we rely on you and face this huge army in your name. Do not let mere people win against you.
core_idea: The weak rely on God against overwhelming odds.

text: But you be strong, and don’t let your hands be slack; for your work will be rewarded.
note: Discouragement in work; persevering

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to slacken because their effort seems to go nowhere.

display_text: But you be strong, and don’t let your hands be slack; for your work will be rewarded.
plain: Be strong and do not let your hands go limp, because your work will be rewarded.
core_idea: Keep going; your work will be rewarded.

text: As Yahweh lives, what my God says, that will I speak.
note: Pressure to tell people what they want to hear; integrity

tags.when_helps: A believer pressured to say what pleases others rather than what they know to be true.

display_text: As Yahweh lives, what my God says, that will I speak.
plain: I swear by the living Lord: I will say whatever my God tells me to say.
core_idea: Speak only what God says, whatever the pressure.

text: We don’t know what to do, but our eyes are on you.
note: Helplessness and not knowing what to do; trust

tags.when_helps: A believer who simply does not know what to do and needs words for turning to God.

display_text: We don’t know what to do, but our eyes are on you.
plain: We do not know what to do, but we are looking to you.
core_idea: When lost, look to God.

text: Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed because of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.
note: Overwhelmed by a struggle too big to carry alone

tags.when_helps: A believer facing overwhelming odds who can let go of carrying the whole fight themselves.

display_text: Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed because of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.
plain: Do not be afraid or discouraged by this huge army, because the fight is not yours; it is God's.
core_idea: The battle belongs to God, not you.

text: Amaziah said to the man of God, “But what shall we do for the hundred talents which I have given to the army of Israel?” The man of God answered, “Yahweh is able to give you much more than this.”
note: Letting go of a sunk cost to do the right thing

tags.when_helps: A believer reluctant to do right because of money already spent, reminded that more can be given.

display_text: Amaziah said to the man of God, “But what shall we do for the hundred talents which I have given to the army of Israel?” The man of God answered, “Yahweh is able to give you much more than this.”
plain: Amaziah worries about the large sum he already paid to hire an army. The man of God replies that the Lord can give him far more than that.
core_idea: God can give far more than what you lose.

text: May the good Yahweh pardon everyone who sets his heart to seek God, Yahweh, the God of his fathers, even if they aren’t clean according to the purification of the sanctuary.
note: Feeling not good enough; sincere heart over perfect form

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels not 'clean' enough for God but whose heart truly seeks.

display_text: May the good Yahweh pardon everyone who sets his heart to seek God, Yahweh, the God of his fathers, even if they aren’t clean according to the purification of the sanctuary.
plain: A prayer that the good Lord will forgive everyone who sincerely seeks God, even if they have not met the temple's purity rules.
core_idea: A heart seeking God matters more than ritual purity.

text: Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or dismayed because of the king of Assyria, nor for all the multitude who is with him; for there is a greater one with us than with him. An arm of flesh is with him, but Yahweh our God is with us to help us and to fight our battles.
note: Fear when facing a powerful opponent; courage

tags.when_helps: A believer afraid of a powerful opponent who needs to remember a greater one is with them.

display_text: Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or dismayed because of the king of Assyria, nor for all the multitude who is with him; for there is a greater one with us than with him. An arm of flesh is with him, but Yahweh our God is with us to help us and to fight our battles.
plain: Be strong and brave; do not fear the king of Assyria and his huge army. One greater is with us: he has only human strength, but the Lord our God is with us to help and fight for us.
core_idea: God with us outweighs any human power.

text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort; who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
note: Comfort received in suffering, passed on to others

situations: caring for a sick or ageing relative
tags.when_helps: A believer in affliction who wants comfort and to see how their own suffering can help them comfort others.

display_text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort; who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
plain: Praise to God, the Father of mercies and source of all comfort, who comforts us in every trouble so that we can comfort others in theirs with the comfort God gave us.
core_idea: Comfort received from God is meant to be passed on.

text: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God, and not from ourselves. We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair; pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed; always carrying in the body the putting to death of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
note: Fragility, pressure and resilience without despair

tags.when_helps: A believer pressed hard on every side who needs to hear that being struck down is not being destroyed.

display_text: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God, and not from ourselves. We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair; pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed; always carrying in the body the putting to death of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
plain: Our treasure is held in fragile clay jars, so the great power is shown to be God's, not ours. Pressed, confused, hunted and knocked down, we are never crushed, despairing, abandoned or destroyed, so Jesus' life shows in us.
core_idea: Fragile people, sustained by God's power, are not crushed.

plain_judge.issue: Drops carrying in the body the dying of Jesus.

text: Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day. For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory; while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.
note: Ageing body, inner renewal, perspective on hardship

keywords: inward man renewed day by day
tags.when_helps: A believer feeling their body decline or troubles wear on them who needs the hope of inner renewal.

display_text: Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day. For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory; while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.
plain: So we do not lose heart. Our bodies wear out, but inside we are renewed daily. Brief troubles produce lasting glory, as we look not at what is seen, which passes, but at what is unseen, which is eternal.
core_idea: Outer decay, inner renewal; the unseen is eternal.

plain_judge.issue: Loses 'light' affliction weighed against an eternal weight of glory.

text: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
note: Fresh start, leaving the past behind

tags.when_helps: A Christian wanting to leave their old self behind and believe a genuine new start is possible.

display_text: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
plain: Anyone who is in Christ is made new. The old has gone; everything has become new.
core_idea: In Christ, a person is made entirely new.

text: For godly sorrow produces repentance to salvation, which brings no regret. But the sorrow of the world produces death.
note: Guilt and regret that heal versus destroy

tags.when_helps: A believer sorry for a wrong who wants to tell sorrow that leads to change from sorrow that only crushes.

display_text: For godly sorrow produces repentance to salvation, which brings no regret. But the sorrow of the world produces death.
plain: Sorrow that comes from God leads to a change of heart and to salvation, with nothing to regret. But the world's kind of sorrow leads to death.
core_idea: Godly sorrow heals; worldly sorrow kills.

text: For if the readiness is there, it is acceptable according to what you have, not according to what you don’t have.
note: Giving what you can; enough is enough

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels what they can give is too little and needs to hear willingness counts by what they have.

display_text: For if the readiness is there, it is acceptable according to what you have, not according to what you don’t have.
plain: If you are willing, your gift is welcome for what you have, not judged by what you do not have.
core_idea: Willingness counts; give from what you have.

text: Remember this: he who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly. He who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully. Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart; not grudgingly, or under compulsion; for God loves a cheerful giver.
note: Generosity given freely and cheerfully

tags.when_helps: Someone deciding how generously to give who wants encouragement to give freely and gladly.

display_text: Remember this: he who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly. He who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully. Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart; not grudgingly, or under compulsion; for God loves a cheerful giver.
plain: Whoever sows little reaps little; whoever sows generously reaps generously. Each should give what they have decided in their heart, not reluctantly or under pressure, because God loves a cheerful giver.
core_idea: Give generously and gladly; God loves a cheerful giver.

text: For we are not bold to number or compare ourselves with some of those who commend themselves. But they themselves, measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves with themselves, are without understanding.
note: Comparing ourselves with others, self-promotion

tags.when_helps: Someone caught comparing themselves to others or to self-promoters who needs to see the folly of it.

display_text: For we are not bold to number or compare ourselves with some of those who commend themselves. But they themselves, measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves with themselves, are without understanding.
plain: Paul will not class or compare himself with those who praise themselves. People who measure themselves against themselves and compare themselves with each other show they lack understanding.
core_idea: Measuring yourself by yourself shows a lack of understanding.

text: He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me. Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then am I strong.
note: Living with weakness or affliction; strength in weakness

keywords: when I am weak, then am I strong
tags.when_helps: A believer ashamed of weakness or limitation who needs to hear that strength can show itself through it.

display_text: He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me. Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then am I strong.
plain: The Lord told Paul his grace is enough, because his power is made complete in weakness. So Paul gladly boasts of and takes pleasure in his weaknesses and hardships for Christ, because when he is weak, he is strong.
core_idea: God's power shows most in our weakness.

text: Finally, brothers, rejoice. Be perfected, be comforted, be of the same mind, live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with you.
note: Encouragement toward comfort, unity and peace

tags.when_helps: A believer who wants a short blessing of peace, comfort and harmony with others.

display_text: Finally, brothers, rejoice. Be perfected, be comforted, be of the same mind, live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with you.
plain: Finally, brothers, rejoice. Grow toward maturity, be comforted, agree with one another, live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with you.
core_idea: Live in peace; the God of peace is with you.

text: You⌃ have not as it were forsaken me, but your own selves, says the Lord.
note: Turning from what is good betrays your own self

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels God has abandoned them, prompted to ask whether they have abandoned themselves.

display_text: You have not as it were forsaken me, but your own selves, says the Lord.
plain: The Lord says: you have not really abandoned me; you have abandoned yourselves.
core_idea: Turning from God is abandoning yourself.

text: Do right to the widow, judge the fatherless, give to the poor, defend the orphan, clothe the naked, heal the broken and the weak, laugh not a lame man to scorn, defend the maimed, and let the blind man come to the sight of my glory. Keep the old and young within your walls.
note: Caring for the vulnerable, poor and weak

tags.when_helps: Someone wanting a concrete picture of what caring for the weak and forgotten looks like.

display_text: Do right to the widow, judge the fatherless, give to the poor, defend the orphan, clothe the naked, heal the broken and the weak, laugh not a lame man to scorn, defend the maimed, and let the blind man come to the sight of my glory. Keep the old and young within your walls.
plain: God commands: treat widows rightly, defend the fatherless and orphans, give to the poor, clothe the naked, heal the broken and weak, never mock the lame, protect the maimed, help the blind, and look after old and young.
core_idea: Care for the vulnerable is God's command.

plain_judge.issue: 'Let the blind come to the sight of my glory' reduced to 'help the blind'.

text: Abide still, O my people, and take your rest, for your quietness shall come.
note: Restlessness; waiting for peace to come

tags.when_helps: Someone worn out and agitated who needs permission to rest and trust that quiet will come.

display_text: Abide still, O my people, and take your rest, for your quietness shall come.
plain: Be still, my people, and rest, because your peace is coming.
core_idea: Rest; peace is coming.

text: Be not careful overmuch: for when the day of tribulation and anguish comes, others shall weep and be sorrowful, but you shall be merry and have abundance.
note: Over-worrying about hard times ahead

tags.when_helps: A believer worrying too much about hard times ahead.

display_text: Be not careful overmuch: for when the day of tribulation and anguish comes, others shall weep and be sorrowful, but you shall be merry and have abundance.
plain: Do not worry too much. When the time of trouble and anguish comes, others will weep and grieve, but you will be glad and have plenty.
core_idea: Do not overworry; God's people will be cared for.

text: And he answered me, and said, You do not hasten more than the Most High: for your haste is for your own self, but he that is above hastens on behalf of many.
note: Impatience for things to happen on your own timeline

tags.when_helps: A believer impatient for answers, reminded that their hurry serves only themselves.

display_text: And he answered me, and said, You do not hasten more than the Most High: for your haste is for your own self, but he that is above hastens on behalf of many.
plain: The angel answers that you cannot hurry ahead of the Most High: your haste is for yourself alone, but God's timing serves many.
core_idea: God's timing serves many; our haste serves ourselves.

plain_judge.issue: 'Hastens on behalf of many' recast as God's timing; loses that the Most High also hastens.

text: For what is gone I know, but what is for to come I know not.
note: Uncertainty about the future

tags.when_helps: Someone unsettled by not knowing what comes next, wanting their uncertainty named honestly.

display_text: For what is gone I know, but what is for to come I know not.
plain: I know what has already happened, but I do not know what is still to come.
core_idea: The past is known; the future is not.

text: Then I awaked, and an extreme trembling went through my body, and my mind was troubled, so that it fainted. So the angel that was come to talk with me held me, comforted me, and set me up upon my feet.
note: Overwhelming fear, then being held and comforted

keywords: held and set on one's feet
tags.when_helps: Someone shaken and trembling after a fright, needing to know that comfort and steadiness can come.

display_text: Then I awaked, and an extreme trembling went through my body, and my mind was troubled, so that it fainted. So the angel that was come to talk with me held me, comforted me, and set me up upon my feet.
plain: Waking from a vision, he shook all over and his mind was so troubled it gave way. The angel held him, comforted him and helped him back onto his feet.
core_idea: In terror, comfort lifts us back to our feet.

text: And I said, Wherefore, Lord, or whereunto was I born? or why was not my mother’s womb then my grave, that I might not have seen the travail of Jacob, and the wearisome toil of the stock of Israel?
note: Despair; asking why one was born at all

tags.safety_reason: Wishes the womb had been the speaker's grave, presenting never having lived as preferable to suffering.
tags.when_helps: A believer questioning why they were born amid long suffering, who needs to know others have cried out the same.

display_text: And I said, Wherefore, Lord, or whereunto was I born? or why was not my mother’s womb then my grave, that I might not have seen the travail of Jacob, and the wearisome toil of the stock of Israel?
plain: He asks the Lord why he was born at all, and why he did not die at birth, so he would not have to see the suffering and weary toil of Israel's people.
core_idea: Despair asks why one was born to see suffering.

text: And in the eighth night was my heart vexed within me again, and I began to speak before the Most High. For my spirit was greatly set on fire, and my soul was in distress.
note: Distress returning at night; pouring it out in prayer

tags.when_helps: A believer whose heart is agitated and distressed, needing permission to speak it before God.

display_text: And in the eighth night was my heart vexed within me again, and I began to speak before the Most High. For my spirit was greatly set on fire, and my soul was in distress.
plain: On the eighth night his heart was troubled again and he began to speak before the Most High, his spirit burning and his soul in distress.
core_idea: A troubled soul pours itself out before God.

text: Then he said to me, There is a sea set in a wide place, that it might be broad and vast. But the entrance thereof shall be set in a narrow place so as to be like a river; whoso then should desire to go into the sea to look upon it, or to rule it, if he went not through the narrow, how could he come into the broad?
note: Hardship as the narrow way into something larger

keywords: narrow entrance to a wide sea
tags.when_helps: Someone in a hard, narrow stretch who needs to see it as the way through to something wider.

display_text: Then he said to me, There is a sea set in a wide place, that it might be broad and vast. But the entrance thereof shall be set in a narrow place so as to be like a river; whoso then should desire to go into the sea to look upon it, or to rule it, if he went not through the narrow, how could he come into the broad?
plain: The angel compares it to a vast sea whose only entrance is narrow like a river: whoever wants to reach the open sea must first pass through the narrow way.
core_idea: The broad place is reached only through the narrow.

text: Now therefore why you disquiet yourself, seeing you are but a corruptible man? and why are you moved, whereas you are but mortal? and why have you not considered in your mind that which is to come, rather than that which is present?
note: Anxiety; looking beyond present troubles

tags.when_helps: Someone churning over present troubles, challenged to put them in proportion against what lasts.

display_text: Now therefore why you disquiet yourself, seeing you are but a corruptible man? and why are you moved, whereas you are but mortal? and why have you not considered in your mind that which is to come, rather than that which is present?
plain: Why are you so troubled, when you are only a mortal who will perish? Why have you not thought about what is to come rather than only about what is happening now?
core_idea: Mortals should look to what comes, not only now.

text: And I answered and said, O you earth, wherefore have you brought forth, if the mind is made out of dust, like as all other created things? For it were better that the dust itself had been unborn, so that the mind might not have been made therefrom. But now the mind grows with us, and by reason of this we are tormented, because we perish and know it.
note: The pain of knowing we will die

tags.safety_reason: Says it were better never to have been made, presenting non-existence as preferable to conscious mortality.
tags.when_helps: Someone tormented by awareness of their own mortality, wanting to know that the feeling is ancient.

display_text: And I answered and said, O you earth, wherefore have you brought forth, if the mind is made out of dust, like as all other created things? For it were better that the dust itself had been unborn, so that the mind might not have been made therefrom. But now the mind grows with us, and by reason of this we are tormented, because we perish and know it.
plain: He asks the earth why it brought forth a mind from dust. It would be better if the dust had never been, because the mind grows with us, and so we suffer: we die and we know it.
core_idea: Knowing we will die torments the human mind.

text: And I answered and said, Swallow down understanding then, O my soul, and let my heart devour wisdom. For you are come here without your will, and depart when you would not: for there is given you no longer space than only to live a short time.
note: Life is short; seek wisdom while you can

tags.when_helps: Someone drifting through life who needs a reminder that time is short and wisdom is worth seeking now.

display_text: And I answered and said, Swallow down understanding then, O my soul, and let my heart devour wisdom. For you are come here without your will, and depart when you would not: for there is given you no longer space than only to live a short time.
plain: He tells his soul to take in understanding and his heart to feed on wisdom, because we arrive without choosing it, leave when we do not wish to, and are given only a short time to live.
core_idea: Life is short; seek understanding while you can.

text: For what is man, that you should take displeasure at him? or what is a corruptible race, that you should be so bitter toward it? For in truth there is no man among those who are born, but he has dealt wickedly; and among them that have lived there is none which have not done amiss.
note: Everyone falls short; a plea for mercy

tags.when_helps: A person weighed down by their own wrongdoing who needs to see that every human has fallen short.

display_text: For what is man, that you should take displeasure at him? or what is a corruptible race, that you should be so bitter toward it? For in truth there is no man among those who are born, but he has dealt wickedly; and among them that have lived there is none which have not done amiss.
plain: He asks God why he should be so angry with frail, mortal humans, since truly no one ever born has not done wrong and fallen short.
core_idea: Every human does wrong; God, why such anger?

text: Now therefore keep your sorrow to yourself, and bear with a good courage the adversities which have befallen you.

display_text: Now therefore keep your sorrow to yourself, and bear with a good courage the adversities which have befallen you.
plain: So keep your grief to yourself, and face the misfortunes that have come to you with courage.
core_idea: Bear misfortune with courage.

text: You therefore shake off your great heaviness, and put away from you the multitude of sorrows, that the Mighty may be merciful to you again, and the Most High may give you rest, even ease from your travails.
note: setting down heavy sorrow; hope of rest

tags.when_helps: A believer weighed down by many sorrows, encouraged to shake off the heaviness and hope for rest.

display_text: You therefore shake off your great heaviness, and put away from you the multitude of sorrows, that the Mighty may be merciful to you again, and the Most High may give you rest, even ease from your travails.
plain: Shake off your heavy grief and set aside your many sorrows, so that the Mighty One may show you mercy again and the Most High may give you rest from your troubles.
core_idea: Letting go of sorrow opens the way to God's rest.

text: Behold, I am yet weary in my mind, and very weak in my spirit; nor is there the least strength in me, for the great fear wherewith I was affrighted this night.

text: Be of good comfort, O Israel; and be not sorrowful, you house of Jacob: for the Most High has you in remembrance, and the Mighty has not forgotten you forever.

plain: Take comfort, Israel, and do not grieve, people of Jacob: the Most High remembers you, and the Mighty One has not forgotten you forever.
core_idea: God has not forgotten his people.

text: Your life have you ordered in wisdom, and have called understanding your mother.
