tags.when_helps: Someone who has tried to live wisely and wants that effort affirmed.

display_text: Your life have you ordered in wisdom, and have called understanding your mother.
plain: You have ordered your life by wisdom, and have treated understanding as your mother.
core_idea: A life guided by wisdom and understanding.

text: For the world has lost its youth, and the times begin to wax old.

tags.when_helps: Someone sensing that an era or their own youth has passed, wanting that feeling named.

display_text: For the world has lost its youth, and the times begin to wax old.

text: Don’t be afraid of their imaginations against you, don’t let the unbelief of them that speak against you trouble you.

plain: Do not be afraid of what they plot against you, and do not let the disbelief of those who speak against you upset you.
core_idea: Do not let critics' disbelief trouble you.

text: Be you⌃ not afraid, neither doubt; for God is your guide: and you⌃ who keep my commandments and precepts, says the Lord God, don’t let your sins weigh you down, and don’t let your iniquities lift up themselves.

display_text: Be you not afraid, neither doubt; for God is your guide: and you who keep my commandments and precepts, says the Lord God, don’t let your sins weigh you down, and don’t let your iniquities lift up themselves.

core_idea: Do not fear; God guides; sins need not crush you.

text: Having many things to write to you, I don’t want to do so with paper and ink, but I hope to come to you, and to speak face to face, that our joy may be made full.

display_text: Having many things to write to you, I don’t want to do so with paper and ink, but I hope to come to you, and to speak face to face, that our joy may be made full.

core_idea: Joy is fullest face to face.

text: Elijah said to Elisha, “Please wait here, for Yahweh has sent me as far as Bethel.” Elisha said, “As Yahweh lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you.” So they went down to Bethel.
note: Staying beside someone you are about to lose

situations: caring for a sick or ageing relative
tags.when_helps: Someone staying close to a mentor or loved one near the end, refusing to leave their side.

display_text: Elijah said to Elisha, “Please wait here, for Yahweh has sent me as far as Bethel.” Elisha said, “As Yahweh lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you.” So they went down to Bethel.

text: But Naaman was angry, and went away, and said, “Behold, I thought, ‘He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of Yahweh his God, and wave his hand over the place, and heal the leper.’ Aren’t Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? text: When the servant of the man of God had risen early, and gone out, behold, an army with horses and chariots was around the city. His servant said to him, “Alas, my master! What shall we do?” He answered, “Don’t be afraid; for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.” Elisha prayed, and said, “Yahweh, please open his eyes, that he may see.” Yahweh opened the young man’s eyes; and he saw: and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha.
note: Fear when surrounded; unseen support

tags.when_helps: A believer surrounded by threats who needs to see they are not as outnumbered as they feel.

display_text: When the servant of the man of God had risen early, and gone out, behold, an army with horses and chariots was around the city. His servant said to him, “Alas, my master! text: Now there were four leprous men at the entrance of the gate. They said to one another, “Why do we sit here until we die? If we say, ‘We will enter into the city,’ then the famine is in the city, and we will die there. If we sit still here, we also die. Now therefore come, and let us surrender to the army of the Syrians. If they save us alive, we will live; and if they kill us, we will only die.”
note: Acting instead of waiting when every option is hard

tags.when_helps: Someone stuck in a hopeless situation who sees that acting is better than waiting.

display_text: Now there were four leprous men at the entrance of the gate. They said to one another, “Why do we sit here until we die? If we say, ‘We will enter into the city,’ then the famine is in the city, and we will die there. If we sit still here, we also die. Now therefore come, and let us surrender to the army of the Syrians. If they save us alive, we will live; and if they kill us, we will only die.”
plain: Four men with leprosy at the city gate reason that staying put or entering the starving city both mean death. So they decide to go to the enemy camp: if spared they live, and if killed they only die.
core_idea: When every option risks death, take the one with hope.

text: Jehoash the king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as wife. Then a wild animal that was in Lebanon passed by, and trampled down the thistle. You have indeed struck Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. note: Pride after success; knowing when to stop

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone puffed up by a success and tempted to pick a fight they cannot win.

Enjoy the glory of it, and stay at home; for why should you meddle to your harm, that you fall, even you, and Judah with you?’”
plain: King Jehoash warns Amaziah with a fable of a thistle that asked a cedar for a marriage and was trampled by a beast. Proud of beating Edom, Amaziah should enjoy his glory at home rather than invite ruin.

text: In those days Hezekiah was sick and dying. tags.when_helps: A believer given grave news about their health who turns to prayer and weeps.

text: For it becomes not our years to dissemble, said he, that through this many of the young should suppose that Eleazar, the man of fourscore years and ten, had gone over to an alien religion; and so they, by reason of my dissimulation, and for the sake of this brief and momentary life, should be led astray because of me, and thus I get to myself a pollution and a stain of my old age. For even if for the present time I shall remove from me the punishment of men, yet shall I not escape the hands of the Almighty, either living or dead. Wherefore, by manfully parting with my life now, I will show myself worthy of my old age, and leave behind a noble ensample to the young to die willingly and nobly a glorious death for the reverend and holy laws.

text: Yahweh sent Nathan to David. He came to him, and said to him, “There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor. tags.when_helps: Someone in hard times who values a friend's loyalty, or wants to pledge their own.

display_text: Ittai answered the king, and said, “As Yahweh lives, and as my lord the king lives, surely in what place my lord the king is, whether for death or for life, your servant will be there also.”
plain: Ittai swears by the Lord and by the king's life that wherever the king goes, in life or death, he will be there too.
core_idea: Loyalty that follows in life or death.

text: The king said to Zadok, “Carry God’s ark back into the city. If I find favor in Yahweh’s eyes, he will bring me again, and show me both it, and his habitation; but if he says, ‘I have no delight in you;’ behold, here am I. Let him do to me as seems good to him.”
note: Surrendering an uncertain outcome during a fall from power

tags.when_helps: A believer facing an uncertain outcome who wants to surrender it to God's will.

display_text: The king said to Zadok, “Carry God’s ark back into the city. If I find favor in Yahweh’s eyes, he will bring me again, and show me both it, and his habitation; but if he says, ‘I have no delight in you;’ behold, here am I. Let him do to me as seems good to him.”
plain: Fleeing, King David sends God's ark back to the city. If the Lord favours him, he will bring him back to see it; if not, David says, here I am, let God do with me what he thinks good.
core_idea: Surrendering one's fate to God's will.

text: The king was much moved, and went up to the room over the gate, and wept. As he went, he said, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I had died for you, Absalom, my son, my son!”
note: A parent's anguish at losing a child

tags.when_helps: A parent grieving a child, especially one estranged, who needs to know such anguish has been voiced before.

display_text: The king was much moved, and went up to the room over the gate, and wept. As he went, he said, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I had died for you, Absalom, my son, my son!”
plain: Deeply shaken, the king goes up to the room over the gate and weeps, crying out for his son Absalom and wishing he had died in his place.
core_idea: A father's grief, wishing to have died instead.

text: Barzillai said to the king, “How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem? I am eighty years old, today. Can I discern between good and bad? Can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Can I hear the voice of singing men and singing women any more? Why then should your servant be a burden to my lord the king?
note: Ageing, fading senses, and not wanting to be a burden

tags.when_helps: An older person feeling their senses fade and wondering whether they are now a burden.

display_text: Barzillai said to the king, “How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem? I am eighty years old, today. Can I discern between good and bad? Can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Can I hear the voice of singing men and singing women any more? Why then should your servant be a burden to my lord the king?
plain: Old Barzillai tells the king he is eighty and has few years left: he can no longer tell good from bad, taste food or drink, or hear singers. Why should he go to Jerusalem and be a burden?
core_idea: In old age, not wanting to be a burden.

text: Please let your servant turn back again, that I may die in my own city, by the grave of my father and my mother.
note: Old age and the wish to end life at home

tags.when_helps: An older person longing to spend their last years at home near their family roots.

display_text: Please let your servant turn back again, that I may die in my own city, by the grave of my father and my mother.
plain: Please let me go back home so I can die in my own town, near the grave of my father and mother.
core_idea: Wishing to die at home, near one's parents.

text: For the waves of death surrounded me. The floods of ungodliness made me afraid. The cords of Sheol were around me. The snares of death caught me. In my distress, I called on Yahweh. Yes, I called to my God. He heard my voice out of his temple. My cry came into his ears.
note: Crying out from overwhelming fear and distress

keywords: my cry came into his ears
tags.when_helps: A believer overwhelmed by danger or darkness who needs to know a cry for help is heard.

display_text: For the waves of death surrounded me. The floods of ungodliness made me afraid. The cords of Sheol were around me. The snares of death caught me. In my distress, I called on Yahweh. Yes, I called to my God. He heard my voice out of his temple. My cry came into his ears.
plain: Death and evil surrounded me like waves and floods, and its snares caught me. In my distress I called to the Lord, my God, and he heard my voice and my cry from his temple.
core_idea: In overwhelming distress, God hears our cry.

text: For you are my lamp, Yahweh. Yahweh will light up my darkness.
note: Hope of light in a dark time

tags.when_helps: A believer in a dark season who needs the image of God as a lamp.

display_text: For you are my lamp, Yahweh. Yahweh will light up my darkness.
plain: Lord, you are my lamp; the Lord will light up my darkness.
core_idea: God lights up our darkness.

text: The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spoke to me, ‘One who rules over men righteously, who rules in the fear of God, shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, when the tender grass springs out of the earth, through clear shining after rain.’
note: Just leadership and the good it brings to others

situations: a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: Someone taking on leadership who wants a picture of what ruling justly can be like.

display_text: The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spoke to me, ‘One who rules over men righteously, who rules in the fear of God, shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, when the tender grass springs out of the earth, through clear shining after rain.’
plain: God, the Rock of Israel, said that one who rules people justly and in awe of God is like morning light at sunrise on a cloudless day, like grass sprouting in the clear shine after rain.
core_idea: Just rule in awe of God is like morning light.

text: David’s heart struck him after he had counted the people. David said to Yahweh, “I have sinned greatly in that which I have done. But now, Yahweh, put away, I beg you, the iniquity of your servant; for I have done very foolishly.”
note: Conscience, guilt and asking forgiveness after a mistake

tags.when_helps: A believer whose conscience is troubling them after a foolish act, ready to ask for forgiveness.

display_text: David’s heart struck him after he had counted the people. David said to Yahweh, “I have sinned greatly in that which I have done. But now, Yahweh, put away, I beg you, the iniquity of your servant; for I have done very foolishly.”
plain: After taking a census, David's conscience strikes him. He tells the Lord he has sinned greatly and acted very foolishly, and begs him to take away his guilt.
core_idea: A troubled conscience confesses and asks forgiveness.

text: The king said to Araunah, “No; but I will most certainly buy it from you for a price. I will not offer burnt offerings to Yahweh my God which cost me nothing.”
note: Real giving costs something; integrity in devotion

tags.when_helps: A believer tempted to give only what costs them nothing, reminded that real devotion has a price.

display_text: The king said to Araunah, “No; but I will most certainly buy it from you for a price. I will not offer burnt offerings to Yahweh my God which cost me nothing.”
plain: The king refuses Araunah's gift and insists on paying, saying he will not offer the Lord his God sacrifices that cost him nothing.
core_idea: A true offering must cost you something.

text: But you, brothers, don’t be weary in doing what is right.
note: tiredness in doing good

keywords: don't be weary in doing right
tags.when_helps: Someone tired of doing the right thing without reward who needs a short word to keep going.

display_text: But you, brothers, don’t be weary in doing what is right.
plain: But you, brothers, do not grow tired of doing what is right.
core_idea: Do not tire of doing right.

text: Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways. The Lord be with you all.
note: longing for peace

keywords: peace at all times in all ways
tags.when_helps: A believer longing for peace in every part of life who wants a simple blessing.

display_text: Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways. The Lord be with you all.
plain: May the Lord of peace himself give you peace always and in every way. The Lord be with you all.
core_idea: May the Lord give you peace always.

text: For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
note: fear and timidity

tags.when_helps: A believer held back by fear who needs reminding of the power, love and self-control they have been given.

display_text: For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
plain: God did not give us a spirit of fear, but one of power, love and self-control.
core_idea: God gives power, love and self-control, not fear.

text: For I am already being offered, and the time of my departure has come. I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.
note: facing the end of life with peace

keywords: I have fought the good fight
tags.when_helps: Someone nearing the end of life or of a long work who wants to look back with a sense of having kept faith.

display_text: For I am already being offered, and the time of my departure has come. I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.
plain: My life is already being poured out, and the time for me to depart has come. I have fought the good fight, finished the race and kept the faith.
core_idea: Facing death having lived faithfully to the end.

text: At my first defense, no one came to help me, but all left me. May it not be held against them. But the Lord stood by me, and strengthened me, that through me the message might be fully proclaimed, and that all the Gentiles might hear; and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
note: abandoned by others; forgiving them

keywords: may it not be held against them
tags.when_helps: A believer deserted by others in a time of need who wants to forgive them and find strength in God.

display_text: At my first defense, no one came to help me, but all left me. May it not be held against them. But the Lord stood by me, and strengthened me, that through me the message might be fully proclaimed, and that all the Gentiles might hear; and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
plain: At my first trial everyone deserted me; may it not be held against them. But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so the message could be fully preached, and I was rescued from the lion's mouth.
core_idea: Deserted by all, but the Lord stood by me.

plain_judge.issue: Drops the purpose that all the Gentiles might hear.

text: Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be healthy, even as your soul prospers.
note: Wishing wellbeing for body and soul

tags.when_helps: Someone wishing wellbeing for a loved one, or wanting to receive such a blessing.

display_text: Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be healthy, even as your soul prospers.
plain: Dear friend, I pray that all goes well with you and that you are healthy, just as your soul is doing well.
core_idea: Wishing body and life to thrive as the soul does.

text: Beloved, don’t imitate that which is evil, but that which is good. He who does good is of God. He who does evil hasn’t seen God.
note: Choosing good examples, moral choices

tags.when_helps: A believer surrounded by bad examples, deciding whose behaviour to follow.

display_text: Beloved, don’t imitate that which is evil, but that which is good. He who does good is of God. He who does evil hasn’t seen God.
plain: Dear friend, do not copy what is evil, but what is good. Whoever does good is from God; whoever does evil has not seen God.
core_idea: Imitate good; doing good shows you are of God.

text: Blot out our iniquities, and do away with our errors, and show forth your compassion in this hour. Let your mercies quickly go before us. Grant us peace, that the cast down and broken hearted may praise you with their mouth.
note: A plea for mercy and peace when broken-hearted

tags.when_helps: A broken-hearted believer asking for mercy and peace after wrongdoing.

display_text: Blot out our iniquities, and do away with our errors, and show forth your compassion in this hour. Let your mercies quickly go before us. Grant us peace, that the cast down and broken hearted may praise you with their mouth.
plain: A prayer asking God to wipe out our sins and mistakes, to show compassion now, to send mercy quickly ahead of us, and to grant peace so that the downcast and broken-hearted may praise him.
core_idea: Plea for mercy and peace for the broken-hearted.

text: When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster, you did look upon him, O Father, and recover him to the sight of his own.
note: Being seen and rescued from the depths of despair

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels swallowed up and unseen, needing to remember that rescue came even from the depths.

display_text: When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster, you did look upon him, O Father, and recover him to the sight of his own.
plain: A prayer recalling that when Jonah was wasting away inside the sea monster, God the Father watched over him and brought him back to his own people.
core_idea: God sees and rescues even from the depths.

text: One may not be able to root out anger from the soul, but it is possible to withstand anger. Any one of you may not be able to eradicate malice, but reasoning has force to work with you to prevent you yielding to malice. For reasoning is not an eradicator, but an antagonist of the passions.
note: anger and resentment; not acting on strong feelings

keywords: reason as antagonist of the passions
tags.when_helps: Someone who can't stop feeling anger but wants to know they can still refuse to act on it.

display_text: One may not be able to root out anger from the soul, but it is possible to withstand anger. Any one of you may not be able to eradicate malice, but reasoning has force to work with you to prevent you yielding to malice. For reasoning is not an eradicator, but an antagonist of the passions.
plain: You may not be able to remove anger or malice from your soul, but you can resist them. Reason does not wipe out the passions; it stands against them and helps you not give in.
core_idea: Reason cannot erase passions, but can resist them.

text: Before pleasure is lust; and after pleasure, joy. And before pain is fear; and after pain is sorrow.
note: understanding desire, fear and sorrow

tags.when_helps: Someone caught in fear before pain, reflecting on how feelings follow one another.

display_text: Before pleasure is lust; and after pleasure, joy. And before pain is fear; and after pain is sorrow.
plain: Desire comes before pleasure, and joy after it. Fear comes before pain, and sorrow after it.
core_idea: Pleasure and pain each have feelings before and after.

text: For the wise and brave man only is lord over his passions.
note: self-mastery over strong emotions

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone ruled by their impulses who wants a picture of what mastering them takes.

display_text: For the wise and brave man only is lord over his passions.
plain: Only the wise and brave person is master of their passions.
core_idea: Only the wise and brave master their passions.

text: The tame birds frequenting the roofs of our houses, defend their fledglings. Others build their nests, and hatch their young, in the tops of mountains and in the precipices of valleys, and the holes and tops of trees, and keep off the intruder. And if not able to do this, they fly circling round them in agony of affection, calling out in their own note, and save their offspring in whatever manner they are able.
note: a parent's protective love and helplessness

tags.when_helps: A parent anxious to protect their child, seeing that fierce instinct mirrored in nature.

display_text: The tame birds frequenting the roofs of our houses, defend their fledglings. Others build their nests, and hatch their young, in the tops of mountains and in the precipices of valleys, and the holes and tops of trees, and keep off the intruder. And if not able to do this, they fly circling round them in agony of affection, calling out in their own note, and save their offspring in whatever manner they are able.
plain: Birds on our rooftops defend their chicks; others nest on mountaintops, cliffs and trees and drive off intruders. If they cannot, they circle overhead crying out in anguished love, saving their young however they can.
core_idea: Even birds fight with love to protect their young.

text: All who believed were together, and had all things in common. They sold their possessions and goods, and distributed them to all, according as anyone had need. Day by day, continuing steadfastly with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread at home, they took their food with gladness and singleness of heart, praising God, and having favor with all the people.
note: community, sharing, and simple gladness

tags.when_helps: Someone longing for a community that shares and eats together with gladness.

display_text: All who believed were together, and had all things in common. They sold their possessions and goods, and distributed them to all, according as anyone had need. Day by day, continuing steadfastly with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread at home, they took their food with gladness and singleness of heart, praising God, and having favor with all the people.
plain: All the believers lived together and shared everything, selling their property to give to anyone in need. Every day they met in the temple, ate together at home with glad, sincere hearts, praised God, and were liked by everyone.
core_idea: Early believers shared everything with glad hearts.

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'with one accord' and steadfast continuance; small loss of nuance.

text: For if this counsel or this work is of men, it will be overthrown. But if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow it, and you would be found even to be fighting against God!
note: letting time test what lasts; not forcing outcomes

tags.when_helps: A believer anxious about opposing or defending a cause, trusting time to show what is of God.

display_text: For if this counsel or this work is of men, it will be overthrown. But if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow it, and you would be found even to be fighting against God!
plain: If this plan or movement is merely human, it will fail. But if it comes from God, you will not be able to stop it, and you may even find yourselves fighting against God.
core_idea: What is from God cannot be overthrown.

text: Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism; but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.
note: belonging; feeling an outsider; prejudice

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels an outsider by birth or nation, needing to hear that God shows no favouritism.

display_text: Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism; but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.
plain: I now truly see that God has no favourites; in every nation, anyone who reveres him and does what is right is accepted by him.
core_idea: God accepts the upright of every nation.

text: The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands, neither is he served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath, and all things. He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons, and the boundaries of their dwellings, that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us. ‘For in him we live, and move, and have our being.’
note: Seeking God, feeling far from the divine, shared humanity

keywords: in him we live and move
tags.when_helps: A seeker who feels God is distant, reminded that the divine is not far from anyone.

display_text: The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands, neither is he served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath, and all things. He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons, and the boundaries of their dwellings, that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us. ‘For in him we live, and move, and have our being.’
plain: God, who made the world, does not live in temples or need anything; he gives all life and breath. He made every nation to seek and find him, though he is near each of us, for in him we live.
core_idea: God is near us; in him we live and move.

plain_judge.issue: Compresses heavily: drops 'one blood', appointed seasons, 'move and have our being'.

text: Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there; except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me. But these things don’t count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.
note: Facing an uncertain, hard future with purpose and courage

tags.when_helps: A believer heading into likely hardship, wanting the resolve to finish their calling with joy.

display_text: Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there; except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me. But these things don’t count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.
plain: Paul says the Spirit compels him to Jerusalem; he knows only that prison and hardship await. He does not value his life, if only he can joyfully finish his race and the work Jesus gave him.
core_idea: Finishing one's calling matters more than one's life.

plain_judge.issue: Drops testifying to the Good News of God's grace; looser on 'bound by the Spirit'.

text: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’
note: Generosity, helping others through one's work

tags.when_helps: Someone weighing whether to give their time or money to people weaker than themselves.

display_text: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’
plain: Paul says his life showed them that, by working hard, we should help the weak and remember Jesus' words: giving brings more blessing than receiving.
core_idea: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

text: Do two walk together, unless they have agreed?
note: partnership and shared purpose in relationships

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone in a strained partnership or friendship wondering whether they truly share a direction.

display_text: Do two walk together, unless they have agreed?
plain: Can two people walk together unless they have agreed to?
core_idea: Walking together requires agreement.

text: Seek good, and not evil, that you may live; and so Yahweh, the God of Armies, will be with you, as you say. Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the courts.
note: choosing goodness and justice as a way to live

tags.when_helps: A believer wanting a clear rule for living rightly and standing up for fairness.

display_text: Seek good, and not evil, that you may live; and so Yahweh, the God of Armies, will be with you, as you say. Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the courts.
plain: Seek good and not evil so that you may live, and then the Lord, the God of Armies, will truly be with you, as you claim. Hate evil, love good, and make sure there is justice in the courts.
core_idea: Seek good, hate evil, establish justice.

text: But let justice roll on like rivers, and righteousness like a mighty stream.
note: longing for justice and right living

tags.when_helps: Someone angered by injustice who needs a vision of fairness flowing freely and unstoppably.

display_text: But let justice roll on like rivers, and righteousness like a mighty stream.
plain: Let justice flow like rivers, and right living like a mighty stream that never stops.
core_idea: Let justice flow like a river.

plain_judge.issue: Adds 'that never stops', not in this translation.

text: Behold, the days come,” says the Lord Yahweh, “that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing Yahweh’s words. They will wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east; they will run back and forth to seek Yahweh’s word, and will not find it.
note: spiritual hunger and searching for meaning

tags.when_helps: A believer feeling spiritually starved, searching everywhere for meaning and finding none.

display_text: Behold, the days come,” says the Lord Yahweh, “that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing Yahweh’s words. They will wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east; they will run back and forth to seek Yahweh’s word, and will not find it.
plain: The Lord says a time is coming when he will send a famine, not of food or water, but of hearing his words. People will wander everywhere searching for the Lord's word and will not find it.
core_idea: A famine of hearing God's word.

text: O Lord Almighty, you God of Israel, the soul in anguish, the troubled spirit, cries to you.
note: anguish and a troubled spirit crying out

tags.when_helps: A believer in anguish who needs simple words to cry out with, knowing others have prayed the same.

display_text: O Lord Almighty, you God of Israel, the soul in anguish, the troubled spirit, cries to you.
plain: Lord Almighty, God of Israel, a soul in anguish and a troubled spirit cries out to you.
core_idea: A soul in anguish cries out to God.

text: Learn where is wisdom, where is strength, where is understanding; that you may know also where is length of days, and life, where is the light of the eyes, and peace.
note: seeking wisdom, strength and peace

tags.when_helps: Someone searching for direction who is invited to seek wisdom, strength and peace.

display_text: Learn where is wisdom, where is strength, where is understanding; that you may know also where is length of days, and life, where is the light of the eyes, and peace.
plain: Learn where wisdom, strength and understanding are found, so you also know where to find long life, the light of the eyes, and peace.
core_idea: Seek wisdom, and with it life and peace.

text: Where are the princes of the heathen, and such as ruled the beasts that are upon the earth; those who had their pastime with the fowls of the air, and those who hoarded up silver and gold, wherein men trust; and of whose getting there is no end? For those who wrought in silver, and were so careful, and whose works are past finding out, they are vanished and gone down to the grave, and others are come up in their steads.
note: wealth and power pass away; ambition and mortality

tags.when_helps: Someone consumed by wealth or status who needs to remember that the mighty have all vanished.

display_text: Where are the princes of the heathen, and such as ruled the beasts that are upon the earth; those who had their pastime with the fowls of the air, and those who hoarded up silver and gold, wherein men trust; and of whose getting there is no end? For those who wrought in silver, and were so careful, and whose works are past finding out, they are vanished and gone down to the grave, and others are come up in their steads.
plain: Where are the rulers of nations, those who mastered beasts and birds, those who hoarded endless silver and gold that people trust in, and the skilled craftsmen? They have vanished into the grave, and others have taken their place.
core_idea: The powerful and rich all pass into the grave.

text: Go your way, O my children, go your way: for I am left desolate. I have put off the garment of peace, and put upon me the sackcloth of my petition: I will cry to the Everlasting as long as I live.
note: parent's grief at children leaving; desolation

tags.when_helps: A parent left desolate as their children go, who turns their sorrow into lifelong prayer.

display_text: Go your way, O my children, go your way: for I am left desolate. I have put off the garment of peace, and put upon me the sackcloth of my petition: I will cry to the Everlasting as long as I live.
plain: Jerusalem, as a mother, tells her children to go on their way, since she is left desolate. She has taken off the clothes of peace and put on sackcloth, and will cry to the Everlasting as long as she lives.
core_idea: In desolation, crying to God for life.

plain_judge.issue: Adds Jerusalem-as-mother speaker, which the passage itself does not name.

text: Set your mind on the things that are above, not on the things that are on the earth.
note: lifting attention above daily worries

tags.when_helps: A believer preoccupied with earthly worries or wants who needs to lift their focus.

display_text: Set your mind on the things that are above, not on the things that are on the earth.
plain: Fix your thoughts on the things above, not on earthly things.
core_idea: Set your mind on things above.

text: Put on therefore, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance; bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do. Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection. And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body; and be thankful.
note: forgiveness, compassion, patience with others

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: A Christian with a complaint against someone who needs to put on patience, forgive and walk in love.

display_text: Put on therefore, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance; bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do. Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection. And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body; and be thankful.
plain: As God's chosen, loved people, clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility and patience. Bear with and forgive one another as Christ forgave you. Above all, love, which binds everything together; let God's peace rule your hearts; be thankful.
core_idea: Clothe yourself in compassion, forgiveness and love.

plain_judge.issue: Drops lowliness, the complaint condition and 'called in one body'.

text: Fathers, don’t provoke your children, so that they won’t be discouraged.
note: parenting without discouraging children

tags.when_helps: A parent whose irritation may be discouraging their child and who needs reminding to be gentle.

display_text: Fathers, don’t provoke your children, so that they won’t be discouraged.
plain: Fathers, do not provoke your children, so that they do not lose heart.
core_idea: Don't provoke your children into discouragement.

text: And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance; for you serve the Lord Christ.
note: meaning in work, working wholeheartedly

keywords: work heartily, as for the Lord
tags.when_helps: A believer whose work goes unappreciated who needs a reason to work wholeheartedly anyway.

display_text: And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance; for you serve the Lord Christ.
plain: Whatever you do, put your whole heart into it, as working for the Lord rather than for people, knowing the Lord will reward you, since it is Christ you serve.
core_idea: Work wholeheartedly, as for the Lord.

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'inheritance' from the reward.

text: Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time. Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer each one.
note: gracious speech, wise use of time

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone unsure how to speak to people who see things differently who wants to answer with grace.

display_text: Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time. Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer each one.
plain: Act wisely toward outsiders, making the most of your time. Let your speech always be gracious and flavoured with salt, so you know how to answer each person.
core_idea: Speak with grace and use time wisely.

text: Daniel answered, “Blessed be the name of God forever and ever; for wisdom and might are his. He changes the times and the seasons. He removes kings, and sets up kings. He gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to those who have understanding. He reveals the deep and secret things. He knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells with him.
note: Change and uncertainty; light present even in darkness

tags.when_helps: A believer unsettled by change or uncertainty who finds steadiness in praising a God who knows the hidden things.

display_text: Daniel answered, “Blessed be the name of God forever and ever; for wisdom and might are his. He changes the times and the seasons. He removes kings, and sets up kings. He gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to those who have understanding. He reveals the deep and secret things. He knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells with him.
plain: Daniel praises God forever, for wisdom and power are his. He changes times and seasons, removes and sets up kings, gives wisdom to the wise, reveals deep secrets, and knows what lies in darkness, for light lives with him.
core_idea: God holds wisdom, power and the course of history.

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'knowledge to those who have understanding'.

text: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered the king, “Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter. If it happens, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; and he will deliver us out of your hand, O king. But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image which you have set up.”
note: Standing by conviction under pressure, whatever the outcome

tags.when_helps: A believer pressured to betray their convictions who needs courage to stand firm whatever the outcome.

display_text: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered the king, “Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter. If it happens, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; and he will deliver us out of your hand, O king. But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image which you have set up.”
plain: Three young men tell King Nebuchadnezzar their God can save them from the blazing furnace and will rescue them. But even if he does not, they will never serve the king's gods or worship his golden statue.
core_idea: Faithful even if God does not rescue.

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'we have no need to answer you' and the conditional 'if it happens'.

text: Then one like the appearance of a man touched me again, and he strengthened me. He said, “Greatly beloved man, don’t be afraid. Peace be to you. Be strong. Yes, be strong.” When he spoke to me, I was strengthened, and said, “Let my lord speak; for you have strengthened me.”
note: Fear and exhaustion met with reassurance; regaining strength

tags.when_helps: Someone frightened and drained who needs a gentle word of strength and to hear they are beloved.

display_text: Then one like the appearance of a man touched me again, and he strengthened me. He said, “Greatly beloved man, don’t be afraid. Peace be to you. Be strong. Yes, be strong.” When he spoke to me, I was strengthened, and said, “Let my lord speak; for you have strengthened me.”
plain: A figure like a man touched Daniel again and strengthened him, saying: greatly loved one, do not fear; peace be with you; be strong, be strong. As he spoke, Daniel was strengthened and told him to speak.
core_idea: Be strong, you are loved; peace be with you.

text: Those who are wise will shine as the brightness of the expanse. Those who turn many to righteousness will shine as the stars forever and ever.
note: Lasting worth of wisdom and helping others do good

tags.when_helps: Someone who works quietly to help others find their way and wonders whether it matters.

display_text: Those who are wise will shine as the brightness of the expanse. Those who turn many to righteousness will shine as the stars forever and ever.
plain: The wise will shine like the bright sky, and those who lead many to do right will shine like the stars forever.
core_idea: The wise and those who lead others rightly will shine.

text: How can I myself alone bear your problems, your burdens, and your strife?
note: Overwhelm from carrying others' burdens alone

situations: caring for a sick or ageing relative
tags.when_helps: Someone carrying everyone else's problems alone who feels the load has become too much for one person.

display_text: How can I myself alone bear your problems, your burdens, and your strife?
plain: How can I carry all your problems, burdens and quarrels on my own?
core_idea: No one can carry everyone's burdens alone.

text: You shall not show partiality in judgment; you shall hear the small and the great alike. You shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God’s.
note: Fairness; not fearing others' opinion when deciding

tags.when_helps: Someone who must judge fairly between people and is afraid of displeasing the powerful.

display_text: You shall not show partiality in judgment; you shall hear the small and the great alike. You shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God’s.
plain: Do not take sides when judging; hear the humble and the powerful the same. Do not be afraid of anyone, because judgment belongs to God.
core_idea: Judge fairly and fear no one; judgment is God's.

text: For Yahweh your God has blessed you in all the work of your hand. He has known your walking through this great wilderness. These forty years, Yahweh your God has been with you. You have lacked nothing.
note: Looking back on long hardship with gratitude

tags.when_helps: A believer looking back on a long hard stretch who needs to see they were provided for throughout.

display_text: For Yahweh your God has blessed you in all the work of your hand. He has known your walking through this great wilderness. These forty years, Yahweh your God has been with you. You have lacked nothing.
plain: The Lord your God has blessed all your work and watched over your journey through this vast wilderness. For forty years he has been with you, and you have not lacked anything.
core_idea: God was with you through the wilderness; you lacked nothing.

text: Hear, Israel: Yahweh is our God. Yahweh is one. You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
note: Wholehearted devotion; loving with all of oneself

tags.when_helps: A believer wanting to recommit wholeheartedly to loving God with everything they have.

display_text: Hear, Israel: Yahweh is our God. Yahweh is one. You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
plain: Listen, Israel: the Lord is our God, the Lord alone. Love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul and all your strength.
core_idea: Love the one God with everything you have.

text: You shall remember all the way which Yahweh your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble you, to prove you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments, or not. He humbled you, and allowed you to be hungry, and fed you with manna, which you didn’t know, neither did your fathers know; that he might teach you that man does not live by bread only, but man lives by every word that proceeds out of Yahweh’s mouth.
note: Hard seasons as teachers; meaning beyond material need

tags.when_helps: A believer in a long lean season who wants to see hardship as a time of being led and taught.

display_text: You shall remember all the way which Yahweh your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble you, to prove you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments, or not. He humbled you, and allowed you to be hungry, and fed you with manna, which you didn’t know, neither did your fathers know; that he might teach you that man does not live by bread only, but man lives by every word that proceeds out of Yahweh’s mouth.
plain: Remember how the Lord led you forty years in the wilderness to humble and test you. He let you hunger, then fed you manna, to teach that people live not by bread alone but by every word from the Lord.
core_idea: People live not by bread alone but by God's word.

plain_judge.issue: Drops testing what was in their heart, whether they would keep commandments.

text: You shall consider in your heart that as a man disciplines his son, so Yahweh your God disciplines you.
note: Hardship understood as loving correction

keywords: as a man disciplines his son
tags.when_helps: A believer going through hardship who could understand it as loving correction rather than abandonment.

display_text: You shall consider in your heart that as a man disciplines his son, so Yahweh your God disciplines you.
plain: Take it to heart that the Lord your God disciplines you just as a parent disciplines a child.
core_idea: God disciplines us as a parent does a child.

text: Now, Israel, what does Yahweh your God require of you, but to fear Yahweh your God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul, to keep Yahweh’s commandments and statutes, which I command you today for your good?
note: What a faithful life asks; purpose and devotion

tags.when_helps: A believer unsure what is asked of them who wants a simple summary of a faithful life.

display_text: Now, Israel, what does Yahweh your God require of you, but to fear Yahweh your God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul, to keep Yahweh’s commandments and statutes, which I command you today for your good?
plain: Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you? Only to revere him, follow all his ways, love him, serve him with all your heart and soul, and keep his commands, which are for your own good.
core_idea: God asks for reverence, love and wholehearted service.

text: For Yahweh your God, he is God of gods, and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty, and the awesome, who doesn’t respect persons, nor takes reward. He does execute justice for the fatherless and widow, and loves the foreigner, in giving him food and clothing. Therefore love the foreigner; for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
note: Compassion for outsiders, remembering one's own displacement

tags.when_helps: A believer who is a stranger or widow, or cares for one, wanting assurance that God defends the vulnerable.

display_text: For Yahweh your God, he is God of gods, and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty, and the awesome, who doesn’t respect persons, nor takes reward. He does execute justice for the fatherless and widow, and loves the foreigner, in giving him food and clothing. Therefore love the foreigner; for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
plain: The Lord your God is the great, mighty, awesome God of gods. He takes no bribes and plays no favourites; he defends orphans and widows and loves foreigners, feeding and clothing them. So love foreigners; you were foreigners in Egypt.
core_idea: Love the foreigner, as God does; you were one too.

text: If a poor man, one of your brothers, is with you within any of your gates in your land which Yahweh your God gives you, you shall not harden your heart, nor shut your hand from your poor brother; but you shall surely open your hand to him, and shall surely lend him sufficient for his need, which he lacks.
note: Generosity toward someone in need; not hardening the heart

tags.when_helps: A believer tempted to shut their hand to someone in need who needs a call to open-handed generosity.

display_text: If a poor man, one of your brothers, is with you within any of your gates in your land which Yahweh your God gives you, you shall not harden your heart, nor shut your hand from your poor brother; but you shall surely open your hand to him, and shall surely lend him sufficient for his need, which he lacks.
plain: If any of your fellow people in your land is poor, do not harden your heart or close your hand to them. Open your hand freely and lend them enough for whatever they need.
core_idea: Don't harden your heart; open your hand to the poor.

text: You shall surely give, and your heart shall not be grieved when you give to him; because that for this thing Yahweh your God will bless you in all your work, and in all that you put your hand to. For the poor will never cease out of the land. Therefore I command you to surely open your hand to your brother, to your needy, and to your poor, in your land.
note: Giving freely without resentment

tags.when_helps: A believer who gives grudgingly and wants to learn to give gladly, without a grieving heart.

display_text: You shall surely give, and your heart shall not be grieved when you give to him; because that for this thing Yahweh your God will bless you in all your work, and in all that you put your hand to. For the poor will never cease out of the land. Therefore I command you to surely open your hand to your brother, to your needy, and to your poor, in your land.
plain: Give freely and without resentment, and the Lord your God will bless all your work. There will always be poor people in the land, so I command you to be open-handed toward the needy and poor among you.
core_idea: Give freely and gladly to the poor.

text: You shall not pervert justice. You shall not show partiality. You shall not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise, and perverts the words of the righteous. You shall follow that which is altogether just, that you may live, and inherit the land which Yahweh your God gives you.
note: Integrity, fairness, resisting corruption

tags.when_helps: Someone with power to judge others who is tempted toward favouritism and needs a firm call to fairness.

display_text: You shall not pervert justice. You shall not show partiality. You shall not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise, and perverts the words of the righteous. You shall follow that which is altogether just, that you may live, and inherit the land which Yahweh your God gives you.
plain: Do not twist justice or play favourites. Do not take bribes, because a bribe blinds the wise and corrupts the words of the righteous. Pursue justice and only justice, so you may live in the land God gives you.
core_idea: Pursue justice; bribes blind even the wise.

text: When you go out to battle against your enemies, and see horses, chariots, and a people more than you, you shall not be afraid of them; for Yahweh your God is with you, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.
note: Facing overwhelming odds without fear

tags.when_helps: A believer facing a confrontation where they feel badly outnumbered, needing courage that God is with them.

display_text: When you go out to battle against your enemies, and see horses, chariots, and a people more than you, you shall not be afraid of them; for Yahweh your God is with you, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.
plain: When you go to war and face horses, chariots and an army larger than yours, do not be afraid of them, because the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, is with you.
core_idea: Facing greater forces, do not fear; God is with you.

text: You shall not see your brother’s donkey or his ox fallen down by the way, and hide yourself from them. You shall surely help him to lift them up again.
note: Not looking away when someone needs help

tags.when_helps: Someone hesitating to get involved when a neighbour or relative is struggling, needing a nudge to help.

display_text: You shall not see your brother’s donkey or his ox fallen down by the way, and hide yourself from them. You shall surely help him to lift them up again.
plain: If you see your neighbour's donkey or ox fallen on the road, do not look away. You must help him get it back on its feet.
core_idea: Don't look away; help your neighbour up.

text: You shall observe and do that which has gone out of your lips. Whatever you have vowed to Yahweh your God as a freewill offering, which you have promised with your mouth, you must do.
note: Keeping one's word and promises

tags.when_helps: A believer wavering on a promise made to God who needs reminding to keep their word.

display_text: You shall observe and do that which has gone out of your lips. Whatever you have vowed to Yahweh your God as a freewill offering, which you have promised with your mouth, you must do.
plain: Be careful to do what you have said. Whatever you freely vowed to the Lord your God with your own mouth, you must carry out.
core_idea: Keep the promises you make.

text: You shall not oppress a hired servant who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers, or one of the foreigners who are in your land within your gates. In his day you shall give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down on it; for he is poor, and sets his heart on it; lest he cry against you to Yahweh, and it be sin to you.
note: Fair treatment of workers; paying people promptly

tags.when_helps: A worker treated unfairly over pay, or an employer tempted to delay it, who needs a clear word on justice.

display_text: You shall not oppress a hired servant who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers, or one of the foreigners who are in your land within your gates. In his day you shall give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down on it; for he is poor, and sets his heart on it; lest he cry against you to Yahweh, and it be sin to you.
plain: Do not exploit a poor hired worker, whether Israelite or foreigner. Pay them each day before sunset, since they are poor and counting on it; otherwise they may cry to the Lord against you, and you will be guilty.
core_idea: Pay the poor worker promptly and fairly.

text: When you reap your harvest in your field, and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, you shall not go again to get it. It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow; that Yahweh your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
note: Leaving room for others; generosity from abundance

tags.when_helps: A grateful believer with plenty who wants a practical image of leaving something for those in need.

display_text: When you reap your harvest in your field, and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, you shall not go again to get it. It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow; that Yahweh your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
plain: When you harvest and forget a bundle of grain in the field, do not go back for it. Leave it for foreigners, orphans and widows, so the Lord your God will bless all your work.
core_idea: Leave something for the poor and the stranger.

text: Your life will hang in doubt before you. You will be afraid night and day, and will have no assurance of your life. In the morning you will say, “I wish it were evening!” and at evening you will say, “I wish it were morning!” for the fear of your heart which you will fear, and for the sights which your eyes will see.
note: Restless anxiety and dread; part of a curse list

tags.when_helps: Someone living in constant fear, wishing each day and night away, who needs to know this state has been described before.

display_text: Your life will hang in doubt before you. You will be afraid night and day, and will have no assurance of your life. In the morning you will say, “I wish it were evening!” and at evening you will say, “I wish it were morning!” for the fear of your heart which you will fear, and for the sights which your eyes will see.
plain: Your life will hang in doubt; you will be afraid day and night, never sure you will live. In the morning you will wish for evening, and at evening for morning, because of the dread in your heart.
core_idea: Constant dread makes every hour unbearable.

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'the sights which your eyes will see'.

text: The secret things belong to Yahweh our God; but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, that we may do all the words of this law.
note: Accepting what cannot be known; acting on what is clear

tags.when_helps: Someone tormented by unanswerable questions who could rest in doing what is known and leaving the unknown alone.

display_text: The secret things belong to Yahweh our God; but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, that we may do all the words of this law.
plain: Hidden things belong to the Lord our God, but what has been revealed belongs to us and our children forever, so that we may live by all the words of this law.
core_idea: Leave the hidden to God; live by what is revealed.

text: For this commandment which I command you today is not too hard for you or too distant. It is not in heaven, that you should say, “Who will go up for us to heaven, and bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?” Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, “Who will go over the sea for us, and bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?” But the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, that you may do it.
note: What is right is within reach, not far away

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels the right path is out of reach, needing reminding it is already within them.

display_text: For this commandment which I command you today is not too hard for you or too distant. It is not in heaven, that you should say, “Who will go up for us to heaven, and bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?” Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, “Who will go over the sea for us, and bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?” But the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, that you may do it.
plain: This command is not too hard or out of reach. It is not in heaven or across the sea for someone to fetch. The word is very near you, in your mouth and heart, so you can do it.
core_idea: God's word is near, in your mouth and heart.

text: I call heaven and earth to witness against you today, that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your descendants; to love Yahweh your God, to obey his voice, and to cling to him; for he is your life, and the length of your days; that you may dwell in the land which Yahweh swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.
note: Decisions; choosing life and what sustains it

tags.when_helps: A believer at a crossroads between ways of living who needs a clear call to choose life.

display_text: I call heaven and earth to witness against you today, that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your descendants; to love Yahweh your God, to obey his voice, and to cling to him; for he is your life, and the length of your days; that you may dwell in the land which Yahweh swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.
plain: With heaven and earth as witnesses, Moses sets before the people life and death, blessing and curse. So choose life, for you and your children, by loving the Lord, obeying him and clinging to him, for he is your life.
core_idea: Choose life by loving and holding to God.

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'length of days' and the promised land sworn to the fathers.

text: Yahweh himself is who goes before you. He will be with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged.
note: Facing the unknown; not being alone in fear

tags.when_helps: A believer facing something new and frightening who needs assurance they will not be abandoned.

display_text: Yahweh himself is who goes before you. He will be with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged.
plain: The Lord himself goes ahead of you and will be with you. He will never fail or abandon you. Do not be afraid or discouraged.
core_idea: God goes ahead and will never abandon you.

text: The eternal God is your dwelling place. Underneath are the everlasting arms.
note: Being held and supported in weakness or grief

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels unsupported and needs the image of being held from beneath.

display_text: The eternal God is your dwelling place. Underneath are the everlasting arms.
plain: The eternal God is your home, and his everlasting arms are underneath you.
core_idea: God's everlasting arms hold you up.

text: As your days, so your strength will be.
note: Strength given equal to each day's demands

tags.when_helps: Someone afraid they will not have strength for what lies ahead, reminded that strength comes day by day.

display_text: As your days, so your strength will be.
plain: Your strength will last as long as your days.
core_idea: You will have strength for each day.

text: All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing. That which has been is that which shall be; and that which has been done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.
note: weariness, restlessness, feeling nothing ever changes

tags.when_helps: Someone weary of sameness and never feeling satisfied, who wants that weariness named honestly.

display_text: All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing. That which has been is that which shall be; and that which has been done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.
plain: Everything is wearisome beyond words. The eye never has enough of seeing, nor the ear of hearing. What has been will be again, and what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.
core_idea: Nothing is new; desire is never satisfied.

text: That which is crooked can’t be made straight; and that which is lacking can’t be counted.
note: accepting what cannot be fixed

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone straining to fix what cannot be fixed, needing to accept limits.

display_text: That which is crooked can’t be made straight; and that which is lacking can’t be counted.
plain: What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is missing cannot be counted.
core_idea: Some things simply cannot be fixed.

text: I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind. For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
note: knowledge bringing sorrow, overthinking

tags.when_helps: Someone whose learning has brought more sorrow than peace, feeling the weight of seeing too much.

display_text: I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind. For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
plain: I set my mind to understand wisdom as well as madness and folly, and saw that this too was chasing the wind. For with much wisdom comes much grief; whoever increases knowledge increases sorrow.
core_idea: More knowledge brings more sorrow.

text: Whatever my eyes desired, I didn’t keep from them. I didn’t withhold my heart from any joy, for my heart rejoiced because of all my labor, and this was my portion from all my labor. Then I looked at all the works that my hands had worked, and at the labor that I had labored to do; and behold, all was vanity and a chasing after wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
note: emptiness after success and achievement

tags.when_helps: Someone who got what they worked and wished for and finds it hollow.

display_text: Whatever my eyes desired, I didn’t keep from them. I didn’t withhold my heart from any joy, for my heart rejoiced because of all my labor, and this was my portion from all my labor. Then I looked at all the works that my hands had worked, and at the labor that I had labored to do; and behold, all was vanity and a chasing after wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
plain: I denied myself nothing my eyes wanted and no pleasure, and enjoyed my work as my reward. But when I looked at all I had done, it was all empty, chasing the wind, with no real gain under the sun.
core_idea: Getting everything you want still leaves you empty.

text: There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.
note: finding contentment in simple pleasures and work

tags.when_helps: Someone grinding through work who could let themselves enjoy simple pleasures as a gift.

display_text: There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.
plain: Nothing is better for a person than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in their work. I saw that this too comes from God's hand.
core_idea: Enjoying simple things and work is God's gift.

text: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted; a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up; a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance; a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing; a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away; a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak; a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
note: change, seasons of life, grief and joy

tags.when_helps: Someone in a painful season of life, reminded that every season, sorrowful or joyful, has its time.

display_text: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted; a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up; a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance; a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing; a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away; a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak; a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
plain: There is a right time for everything under heaven: to be born and to die, to plant and uproot, to weep and laugh, to mourn and dance, to be silent and speak, to love and hate, for war and peace.
core_idea: Everything in life has its season.

plain_judge.issue: Drops several pairs, including the hard 'time to kill, time to heal'.

text: Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labor and chasing after wind.
note: overwork, ambition versus peace

tags.when_helps: Someone overworked and chasing more, invited to choose less with peace.

display_text: Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labor and chasing after wind.
plain: One handful with peace and quiet is better than two handfuls with toil and chasing the wind.
core_idea: Less with peace beats more with toil.

text: There is one who is alone, and he has neither son nor brother. There is no end to all of his labor, neither are his eyes satisfied with wealth. “For whom then, do I labor, and deprive my soul of enjoyment?” This also is vanity. Yes, it is a miserable business.
note: loneliness and endless work without purpose

tags.when_helps: Someone working endlessly and alone, starting to ask who all this effort is for.

display_text: There is one who is alone, and he has neither son nor brother. There is no end to all of his labor, neither are his eyes satisfied with wealth. “For whom then, do I labor, and deprive my soul of enjoyment?” This also is vanity. Yes, it is a miserable business.
plain: Someone alone, with no son or brother, works without end and is never satisfied with his wealth. He never asks who he is working for, depriving himself of enjoyment. This too is empty, a miserable business.
core_idea: Endless toil for no one is empty and miserable.

plain_judge.issue: Says he never asks whom he works for; in the passage he does ask.

text: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one keep warm alone? If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
note: friendship, companionship, loneliness

tags.when_helps: Someone trying to go it alone who needs a reminder of the strength of companionship.

display_text: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one keep warm alone? If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
plain: Two are better than one; they gain more from their work. If one falls, the other lifts them up; pity the one who falls alone. Two keep warm and resist attackers; a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
core_idea: Companions lift, warm and defend each other.

text: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he who loves abundance, with increase: this also is vanity. When goods increase, those who eat them are increased; and what advantage is there to its owner, except to feast on them with his eyes? The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not allow him to sleep.
note: money, greed, restlessness of wealth

keywords: the sleep of a laboring man
tags.when_helps: Someone always wanting more money, noticing that more never satisfies or brings rest.

display_text: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he who loves abundance, with increase: this also is vanity. When goods increase, those who eat them are increased; and what advantage is there to its owner, except to feast on them with his eyes? The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not allow him to sleep.
plain: Whoever loves money never has enough, and whoever loves wealth is never satisfied; this too is empty. More goods bring more mouths to feed. A worker sleeps soundly, but the rich man's plenty keeps him awake.
core_idea: Love of wealth never satisfies and costs sleep.

plain_judge.issue: Drops owner only feasting his eyes, and 'whether he eats little or much'.

text: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
note: contentment with what is in front of you

tags.when_helps: Someone always wanting what they do not have, invited to value what is before them.

display_text: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
plain: It is better to enjoy what is in front of your eyes than to let your desires roam. Yet this too is empty, a chasing of the wind.
core_idea: Enjoy what you have rather than craving more.

text: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men, and the living should take this to heart. Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good. The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
note: grief and mortality deepening the heart

tags.when_helps: Someone attending a funeral or sitting with sorrow, finding that it can deepen and teach them.

display_text: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men, and the living should take this to heart. Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good. The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
plain: Better to visit a house of mourning than a feast, since death is everyone's end and the living should take it to heart. Sorrow is better than laughter; it improves the heart. The wise think on mourning, fools on fun.
core_idea: Facing death and sorrow makes the heart wiser.

text: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning. The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit. Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools. Don’t say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you do not ask wisely about this.
note: patience, anger, nostalgia for the past

tags.when_helps: Someone pining for the good old days or quick to anger, urged toward patience.

display_text: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning. The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit. Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools. Don’t say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you do not ask wisely about this.
plain: The end of a matter is better than its beginning, and patience better than pride. Do not be quick to anger; anger lives in fools. Do not ask why the old days were better; that is not wise.
core_idea: Be patient, slow to anger, and don't idealise the past.

text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yes, God has made the one side by side with the other, to the end that man should not find out anything after him.
note: good times and hard times side by side

keywords: day of prosperity, day of adversity
tags.when_helps: Someone in a hard stretch, or a good one, reminded that both come side by side.

display_text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yes, God has made the one side by side with the other, to the end that man should not find out anything after him.
plain: When times are good, be glad; when times are bad, reflect. God has made both, side by side, so that no one can discover what lies ahead.
core_idea: Enjoy good days; reflect in bad ones; God made both.
