text: Surely there is not a righteous man on earth, who does good and doesn’t sin. Also don’t take heed to all words that are spoken, lest you hear your servant curse you; for often your own heart knows that you yourself have likewise cursed others.
note: imperfection, criticism, gossip about you

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone stung by what someone said behind their back, reminded that they have done the same.

display_text: Surely there is not a righteous man on earth, who does good and doesn’t sin. Also don’t take heed to all words that are spoken, lest you hear your servant curse you; for often your own heart knows that you yourself have likewise cursed others.
plain: No one on earth is so righteous that they do only good and never sin. So do not listen to everything people say, or you may hear your servant curse you; you know you have often cursed others yourself.
core_idea: Everyone sins; don't take every word to heart.

plain_judge.issue: Adds a causal 'So' linking universal sin to not heeding gossip.

text: Go your way—eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for God has already accepted your works. Let your garments be always white, and don’t let your head lack oil. Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of your life of vanity, which he has given you under the sun, all your days of vanity: for that is your portion in life, and in your labor in which you labor under the sun. Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.
note: enjoying life and love while you have it

tags.when_helps: Someone hesitant to enjoy life, encouraged to savour food, love and work wholeheartedly while they can.

display_text: Go your way—eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for God has already accepted your works. Let your garments be always white, and don’t let your head lack oil. Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of your life of vanity, which he has given you under the sun, all your days of vanity: for that is your portion in life, and in your labor in which you labor under the sun. Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.
plain: Eat and drink with joy, for God already approves what you do. Enjoy life with the wife you love through your fleeting days. Do everything with all your might; in the grave there is no work or wisdom.
core_idea: Enjoy life and work fully; the grave ends all.

plain_judge.issue: Drops white garments, oil, 'your portion', and Sheol 'where you are going'.

text: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.
note: unfairness, luck, effort not rewarded

keywords: the race is not to the swift
tags.when_helps: Someone who did everything right and still lost out, recognising the role of time and chance.

display_text: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.
plain: I saw that the race is not won by the fastest, nor the battle by the strongest; food does not always go to the wise, wealth to the clever, or favour to the skilled. Time and chance happen to everyone.
core_idea: Time and chance happen to everyone.

text: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.
note: an angry boss, gentleness in conflict

tags.when_helps: Someone whose boss or authority figure is angry at them, tempted to walk out.

display_text: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.
plain: If a ruler becomes angry with you, do not leave your post, because calmness can put great offences to rest.
core_idea: Calmness can settle great offences.

text: He who observes the wind won’t sow; and he who regards the clouds won’t reap. As you don’t know what is the way of the wind, nor how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child; even so you don’t know the work of God who does all. In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening don’t withhold your hand; for you don’t know which will prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both will be equally good.
note: indecision, waiting for certainty, acting anyway

tags.when_helps: Someone waiting for perfect conditions before acting, urged to sow now without knowing the outcome.

display_text: He who observes the wind won’t sow; and he who regards the clouds won’t reap. As you don’t know what is the way of the wind, nor how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child; even so you don’t know the work of God who does all. In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening don’t withhold your hand; for you don’t know which will prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both will be equally good.
plain: Whoever waits for perfect weather will never sow or reap. You cannot know how the wind moves or a baby grows, nor God's work. So sow morning and evening; you do not know which will succeed, or whether both.
core_idea: Don't wait for certainty; act, since outcomes are unknown.

text: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to see the sun. Yes, if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.
note: savouring life, ageing, remembering hard days

tags.when_helps: Someone enjoying a good stretch of life, mindful that darker days also come.

display_text: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to see the sun. Yes, if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.
plain: Light is sweet and seeing the sun is good. However many years a person lives, they should enjoy them all, yet remember that dark days will be many, and everything that comes passes away.
core_idea: Enjoy every year, but remember dark days will come

text: “Be angry, and don’t sin.” Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath, and don’t give place to the devil.
note: anger that is not let fester

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
keywords: don't let the sun go down on your wrath
tags.when_helps: Someone angry tonight who needs to deal with it before it hardens into a grudge.

display_text: “Be angry, and don’t sin.” Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath, and don’t give place to the devil.
plain: You may be angry, but do not let it lead you into sin. Settle your anger before the day ends, and give the devil no foothold.
core_idea: Do not let anger last past sundown

text: Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to those who hear.
note: speaking kindly, words that build up

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to speak harshly who wants to choose words that build others up instead.

display_text: Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to those who hear.
plain: Say nothing harmful. Speak only words that build others up when they need it, so that your words are a gift to those who hear them.
core_idea: Speak only words that build others up

text: Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, outcry, and slander, be put away from you, with all malice. And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
note: letting go of bitterness; forgiveness

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: A Christian holding bitterness or anger toward someone who needs the call to put it away and forgive.

display_text: Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, outcry, and slander, be put away from you, with all malice. And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
plain: Get rid of all bitterness, rage, anger, shouting, slander and malice. Be kind and tender-hearted to one another, and forgive each other just as God forgave you in Christ.
core_idea: Drop bitterness; forgive as God forgave you

text: You fathers, don’t provoke your children to wrath, but nurture them in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.
note: parenting with patience

tags.when_helps: A parent frustrated with their children who needs reminding to guide without provoking them.

display_text: You fathers, don’t provoke your children to wrath, but nurture them in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.
plain: Fathers, do not push your children into anger; raise them with the discipline and teaching of the Lord.
core_idea: Do not provoke children; raise them in the Lord

text: O my Lord, you alone are our king: help me who am destitute, and have no helper but you, for my danger is near at hand.
note: alone and in danger; prayer for help

tags.when_helps: A believer facing danger alone who wants words of prayer for when there is no one else to turn to.

display_text: O my Lord, you alone are our king: help me who am destitute, and have no helper but you, for my danger is near at hand.
plain: Lord, you alone are our king. Help me: I am alone, with no one to help me but you, and danger is close.
core_idea: A plea to God when alone and in danger

text: O god, who has power over all, hearken to the voice of the desperate, and deliver us from the hand of them that devise mischief; and deliver me from my fear.
note: desperation and fear; prayer for deliverance

tags.when_helps: A frightened believer facing people who mean them harm, who needs a prayer to voice their fear.

display_text: O god, who has power over all, hearken to the voice of the desperate, and deliver us from the hand of them that devise mischief; and deliver me from my fear.
plain: God who rules over all, hear those who have lost hope. Save us from those plotting harm, and free me from my fear.
core_idea: A prayer to God for rescue from fear

text: Who knows if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
note: Purpose and courage; this moment may be why you're here

keywords: for such a time as this
tags.when_helps: Someone hesitating before a hard moment who wonders whether their place in it might be exactly where they are needed.

display_text: Who knows if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
plain: Who knows whether you came to your position for exactly this moment?
core_idea: You may be where you are for this moment

text: The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah, and he said, “When you perform the duty of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them on the birth stool; if it is a son, then you shall kill him; but if it is a daughter, then she shall live.” But the midwives feared God, and didn’t do what the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the baby boys alive.
note: Courage to refuse an unjust order from power

tags.when_helps: A believer ordered by someone powerful to do wrong, who needs an example of quiet, courageous refusal.

display_text: The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah, and he said, “When you perform the duty of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them on the birth stool; if it is a son, then you shall kill him; but if it is a daughter, then she shall live.” But the midwives feared God, and didn’t do what the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the baby boys alive.
plain: The king of Egypt ordered the Hebrew midwives to kill every baby boy at birth. But the midwives feared God more than the king, refused the order, and let the boys live.
core_idea: Fear of God gave the midwives courage to disobey

text: Moses said to Yahweh, “O Lord, I am not eloquent, neither before now, nor since you have spoken to your servant; for I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.” Yahweh said to him, “Who made man’s mouth? Or who makes one mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Isn’t it I, Yahweh? Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth, and teach you what you shall speak.”
note: Feeling inadequate for a task you are called to

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels unqualified for a task, especially speaking, and needs reassurance they will be helped.

display_text: Moses said to Yahweh, “O Lord, I am not eloquent, neither before now, nor since you have spoken to your servant; for I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.” Yahweh said to him, “Who made man’s mouth? Or who makes one mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Isn’t it I, Yahweh? Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth, and teach you what you shall speak.”
plain: Moses told God he was a poor speaker. God replied that he made every human mouth, and told Moses to go, promising to be with his mouth and teach him what to say.
core_idea: God helps the one who feels unable to speak

plain_judge.issue: Drops God's claim to make people mute, deaf, seeing or blind.

text: Moses returned to Yahweh, and said, “Lord, why have you brought trouble on this people? Why is it that you have sent me? For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has brought trouble on this people; and you have not rescued your people at all.”
note: Doing the right thing and seeing it make matters worse

tags.when_helps: A believer who did what they felt called to and saw things get worse, needing permission to complain to God.

display_text: Moses returned to Yahweh, and said, “Lord, why have you brought trouble on this people? Why is it that you have sent me? For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has brought trouble on this people; and you have not rescued your people at all.”
plain: Moses went back to God and complained: why have you brought trouble on this people and sent me? Since I spoke to Pharaoh for you, things have got worse, and you have not rescued them.
core_idea: Moses honestly complains to God when things worsen

text: Yahweh will fight for you, and you shall be still.”
note: Fear and overwhelm; trusting rather than struggling

tags.when_helps: An anxious believer facing something too big for them who needs permission to be still and trust.

display_text: Yahweh will fight for you, and you shall be still.
plain: God will fight for you; you only need to be still.
core_idea: God will fight for you; be still

text: Yah is my strength and song. He has become my salvation. This is my God, and I will praise him; my father’s God, and I will exalt him.
note: Gratitude and strength after deliverance from danger

tags.when_helps: A believer who has come through a trial and wants words to give thanks and praise.

display_text: Yah is my strength and song. He has become my salvation. This is my God, and I will praise him; my father’s God, and I will exalt him.
plain: God is my strength and my song, and has saved me. He is my God and my father's God, and I will praise him.
core_idea: God is my strength, song and salvation

text: Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “The thing that you do is not good. You will surely wear away, both you, and this people that is with you; for the thing is too heavy for you. You are not able to perform it yourself alone.
note: Burnout; carrying too much alone, needing to share the load

tags.when_helps: Someone carrying every responsibility alone and wearing out, who needs to hear they must share the load.

display_text: Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “The thing that you do is not good. You will surely wear away, both you, and this people that is with you; for the thing is too heavy for you. You are not able to perform it yourself alone.
plain: Moses' father-in-law told him that what he was doing was not good: he would wear out himself and the people, because the load was too heavy to carry alone.
core_idea: The load is too heavy to carry alone

text: “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor’s.”
note: Envy of what others have

tags.when_helps: Someone eaten up wanting what a neighbour or friend has, who needs a plain call to stop.

display_text: “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor’s.”
plain: Do not crave what belongs to your neighbour: not their house, their spouse, their workers, their animals, or anything else that is theirs.
core_idea: Do not crave what belongs to others

text: “You shall not follow a crowd to do evil. You shall not testify in court to side with a multitude to pervert justice.
note: Peer pressure; standing apart from the crowd for what's right

tags.when_helps: Someone under pressure to go along with the majority in something unjust, needing resolve to stand apart.

display_text: You shall not follow a crowd to do evil. You shall not testify in court to side with a multitude to pervert justice.
plain: Do not join a crowd in doing wrong. In court, do not go along with the majority to twist justice.
core_idea: Do not follow the crowd into wrongdoing

text: “If you meet your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, you shall surely bring it back to him again. If you see the donkey of him who hates you fallen down under his burden, don’t leave him, you shall surely help him with it.
note: Kindness toward someone who dislikes you; enmity

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone holding a grudge who sees their adversary in trouble and is weighing whether to help anyway.

display_text: If you meet your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, you shall surely bring it back to him again. If you see the donkey of him who hates you fallen down under his burden, don’t leave him, you shall surely help him with it.
plain: If you find your enemy's animal wandering, take it back to him. If you see the donkey of someone who hates you collapsed under its load, do not walk away; help him with it.
core_idea: Help even your enemy when he is in trouble

text: “You shall take no bribe, for a bribe blinds those who have sight and perverts the words of the righteous.
note: Integrity; temptation of personal gain clouding judgment

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted by a favour or payment that would compromise their judgement.

display_text: You shall take no bribe, for a bribe blinds those who have sight and perverts the words of the righteous.
plain: Do not take bribes: a bribe blinds people who can see and twists the words of honest people.
core_idea: Bribes blind and corrupt even the honest

text: “You shall not oppress an alien, for you know the heart of an alien, since you were aliens in the land of Egypt.
note: Empathy for outsiders from remembering your own hardship

tags.when_helps: Someone who knows what being an outsider feels like and is reflecting on how to treat newcomers.

display_text: You shall not oppress an alien, for you know the heart of an alien, since you were aliens in the land of Egypt.
plain: Do not mistreat a foreigner. You know how a foreigner feels, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
core_idea: Do not mistreat foreigners; you were one

text: Yahweh passed by before him, and proclaimed, “Yahweh! Yahweh, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth, keeping loving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity and disobedience and sin; and who will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, and on the children’s children, on the third and on the fourth generation.”
note: Guilt and forgiveness; mercy alongside accountability

tags.when_helps: A believer burdened by wrongdoing who wants to know God's mercy while taking their actions seriously.

display_text: Yahweh passed by before him, and proclaimed, “Yahweh! Yahweh, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth, keeping loving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity and disobedience and sin; and who will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, and on the children’s children, on the third and on the fourth generation.”
plain: God proclaims his own name: merciful, gracious, slow to anger, full of steadfast love and truth, forgiving wrongdoing, yet not letting the guilty go unpunished, with consequences reaching to later generations.
core_idea: God is merciful and forgiving, yet holds guilt accountable

plain_judge.issue: Softens visiting fathers' iniquity on children to third and fourth generation into vague 'consequences'.

text: I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them a heart of flesh; that they may walk in my statutes, and keep my ordinances, and do them. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
note: Hardened heart made new; inner renewal and change

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels hardened or numb inside and longs for a renewed, softer heart.

display_text: I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them a heart of flesh; that they may walk in my statutes, and keep my ordinances, and do them. They will be my people, and I will be their God.

text: Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there. He washed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, “Serve the meal.”
note: Hiding tears and composing oneself in front of others

tags.when_helps: Someone holding back tears on seeing a long-separated relative, who needs to know such hidden weeping is human.

display_text: Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there. He washed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, “Serve the meal.”
plain: Overcome with love for his brother, Joseph hurried away to find somewhere to cry. He wept in his room, washed his face, steadied himself, came back and ordered the meal served.
core_idea: Joseph wept privately, then composed himself

text: Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” They came near. “He said, I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt. Now don’t be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
note: Forgiving family who betrayed you

tags.when_helps: Someone who wronged a family member and dreads facing them, needing to see forgiveness offered freely.

display_text: Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” They came near. “He said, I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt. Now don’t be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
plain: Joseph told his brothers who he was, the brother they had sold into Egypt. He said not to be upset or angry with themselves, because God had sent him ahead to save lives.
core_idea: God used the wrong done to me to save lives

text: Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How many are the days of the years of your life?” Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The days of the years of my pilgrimage are one hundred thirty years. Few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.”
note: Old age looking back on a hard life

tags.when_helps: An older person looking back on a hard life, who feels their years were few and troubled.

display_text: Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How many are the days of the years of your life?” Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The days of the years of my pilgrimage are one hundred thirty years. Few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.”
plain: Asked his age, Jacob told Pharaoh his life's journey had lasted 130 years, and that his days had been few and hard, shorter than the lives of his ancestors.
core_idea: My days have been few and hard

text: Israel said to Joseph, “I didn’t think I would see your face, and behold, God has let me see your offspring also.”
note: Joy beyond hope after long loss

tags.when_helps: A believing grandparent overjoyed at a reunion or new grandchild beyond what they ever hoped.

display_text: Israel said to Joseph, “I didn’t think I would see your face, and behold, God has let me see your offspring also.”
plain: Israel told Joseph he never expected to see his face again, and now God had let him see Joseph's children too.
core_idea: I never thought I'd see you; now your children too

text: Joseph fell on his father’s face, wept on him, and kissed him.
note: Grief at a parent's death

tags.when_helps: Someone who has just lost a parent and needs to see the raw tenderness of mourning simply witnessed.

display_text: Joseph fell on his father’s face, wept on him, and kissed him.
plain: Joseph threw himself on his dead father's face, wept over him and kissed him.
core_idea: A son weeps over his dead father

plain_judge.issue: Adds 'dead' father, context the passage itself does not state.

text: Joseph said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for am I in the place of God? As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is today, to save many people alive. Now therefore don’t be afraid. I will nourish you and your little ones.” He comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.
note: Forgiveness; harm done to you turned toward good

keywords: you meant evil, God meant it for good
tags.when_helps: A believer wronged by family, or fearing the one they wronged, who wants a picture of kindness after harm.

display_text: Joseph said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for am I in the place of God? As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is today, to save many people alive. Now therefore don’t be afraid. I will nourish you and your little ones.” He comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.
plain: Joseph told his brothers not to fear, since he was not God. They meant to harm him, but God meant it for good, to save many lives. He promised to provide for them, and spoke kindly to them.
core_idea: You meant harm, but God meant it for good

plain_judge.issue: 'Am I in the place of God?' flattened to 'he was not God'; loses the point about judging.

text: Yahweh, how long will I cry, and you will not hear? I cry out to you “Violence!” and will you not save? Why do you show me iniquity, and look at perversity? For destruction and violence are before me. There is strife, and contention rises up.
note: Unanswered prayer; anguish at injustice and violence

tags.when_helps: A believer who has prayed for help against violence and injustice and feels unheard.

display_text: Yahweh, how long will I cry, and you will not hear? I cry out to you “Violence!” and will you not save? Why do you show me iniquity, and look at perversity? For destruction and violence are before me. There is strife, and contention rises up.
plain: How long, God, must I cry out before you listen? I shout about violence and you do not save. Why make me watch wrongdoing, destruction and conflict all around?
core_idea: How long, God, must I cry unheard?

text: Yahweh answered me, “Write the vision, and make it plain on tablets, that he who runs may read it. For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
note: Patience while waiting for a hope to be fulfilled

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone tired of waiting for a hoped-for vision to come true who needs encouragement to write it down and wait.

display_text: Yahweh answered me, “Write the vision, and make it plain on tablets, that he who runs may read it. For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
plain: God told the prophet to write the vision clearly so anyone could read it quickly. It is for a set time and will not fail; though it seems slow, wait for it, because it will surely come.
core_idea: Though it seems slow, wait; it will come

text: For though the fig tree doesn’t flourish, nor fruit be in the vines; the labor of the olive fails, the fields yield no food; the flocks are cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls: yet I will rejoice in Yahweh. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation! Yahweh, the Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet like deer’s feet, and enables me to go in high places.
note: Finding joy and strength when everything has failed

situations: loss of a dream or plan
keywords: though the fig tree doesn't flourish
tags.when_helps: A believer whose livelihood has failed on every side and who wants to find joy and strength in God anyway.

display_text: For though the fig tree doesn’t flourish, nor fruit be in the vines; the labor of the olive fails, the fields yield no food; the flocks are cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls: yet I will rejoice in Yahweh. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation! Yahweh, the Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet like deer’s feet, and enables me to go in high places.
plain: Even if the fig trees, vines, olives and fields all fail, and the flocks and herds are gone, I will still rejoice in God my saviour. The Lord is my strength and makes me sure-footed on the heights.
core_idea: Even when everything fails, I will rejoice in God

text: Consider your ways. You have sown much, and bring in little. You eat, but you don’t have enough. You drink, but you aren’t filled with drink. You clothe yourselves, but no one is warm, and he who earns wages earns wages to put them into a bag with holes in it.”
note: never feeling satisfied despite effort; reflecting on priorities

tags.when_helps: Someone working hard but never feeling it is enough, prompted to examine where their effort goes.

display_text: Consider your ways. You have sown much, and bring in little. You eat, but you don’t have enough. You drink, but you aren’t filled with drink. You clothe yourselves, but no one is warm, and he who earns wages earns wages to put them into a bag with holes in it.
plain: Think about how you are living. You plant much but harvest little; you eat and drink but are never satisfied; you dress but are never warm; and your wages vanish as if into a bag with holes.
core_idea: Look at your ways: much effort, little satisfaction

text: For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who has been in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy, and may find grace for help in time of need.
note: Weakness, temptation, and seeking help in need

keywords: touched with the feeling of our infirmities
tags.when_helps: A Christian who fears God cannot understand their weakness and needs encouragement to approach for mercy.

display_text: For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who has been in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy, and may find grace for help in time of need.
plain: Our high priest understands our weaknesses, because he was tempted in every way as we are, yet did not sin. So let us come boldly to God's throne of grace to receive mercy and help when we need it.
core_idea: Jesus understands our weakness; approach God boldly

text: Therefore don’t throw away your boldness, which has a great reward. For you need endurance so that, having done the will of God, you may receive the promise.
note: Perseverance when tempted to give up

tags.when_helps: A believer tempted to give up who needs encouragement to keep their confidence and endure.

display_text: Therefore don’t throw away your boldness, which has a great reward. For you need endurance so that, having done the will of God, you may receive the promise.
plain: So do not throw away your confidence; it will be richly rewarded. You need endurance, so that after doing God's will you receive what he promised.
core_idea: Keep your confidence; endurance brings the promise

text: Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.
note: Hope and faith in what is unseen

tags.when_helps: A believer reflecting on what faith is, especially while waiting for what they cannot yet see.

display_text: Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.
plain: Faith is being sure of what we hope for and convinced of what we cannot see.
core_idea: Faith is confidence in the hoped-for and unseen

text: By faith, Abraham, when he was called, obeyed to go out to the place which he was to receive for an inheritance. He went out, not knowing where he went.
note: Stepping into an uncertain future

tags.when_helps: A believer stepping into a new chapter without knowing where it leads who needs the example of faithful going.

display_text: By faith, Abraham, when he was called, obeyed to go out to the place which he was to receive for an inheritance. He went out, not knowing where he went.
plain: By faith Abraham obeyed when God called him to go to the land he would inherit; he set out without knowing where he was going.
core_idea: Faith sets out without knowing where

text: Therefore let us also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
note: Perseverance, laying down burdens

tags.when_helps: A Christian weighed down and flagging in a long struggle who needs to feel surrounded by others who endured.

display_text: Therefore let us also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
plain: Since so many faithful witnesses surround us, let us drop every burden and the sin that trips us, and run our race with endurance, eyes on Jesus, who endured the cross for the joy ahead.
core_idea: Drop every weight and run with endurance

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'despising its shame', 'author and perfecter of faith', and Jesus seated at God's right hand.

text: All chastening seems for the present to be not joyous but grievous; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been exercised thereby. Therefore lift up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees, and make straight paths for your feet, so what is lame may not be dislocated, but rather be healed.
note: Hardship that grows us; taking heart again

keywords: lift up the hands that hang down
tags.when_helps: Someone going through painful discipline or hardship who needs to see it can bear peaceful fruit later.

display_text: All chastening seems for the present to be not joyous but grievous; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been exercised thereby. Therefore lift up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees, and make straight paths for your feet, so what is lame may not be dislocated, but rather be healed.
plain: Discipline feels painful, not pleasant, at the time, but later it brings the peace of right living to those trained by it. So strengthen your tired hands and weak knees, and walk straight paths so injuries can heal.
core_idea: Painful discipline later yields peace

text: Let brotherly love continue. Don’t forget to show hospitality to strangers, for in doing so, some have entertained angels without knowing it. Remember those who are in bonds, as bound with them; and those who are ill-treated, since you are also in the body.
note: Kindness to strangers and those who suffer

tags.when_helps: Someone wanting to live more kindly, welcoming strangers and remembering those who suffer.

display_text: Let brotherly love continue. Don’t forget to show hospitality to strangers, for in doing so, some have entertained angels without knowing it. Remember those who are in bonds, as bound with them; and those who are ill-treated, since you are also in the body.
plain: Keep loving each other as family. Welcome strangers, because some have hosted angels without knowing it. Remember prisoners as if you were in prison with them, and those who are mistreated, since you have a body too.
core_idea: Love, welcome strangers, remember those who suffer

text: Be free from the love of money, content with such things as you have, for he has said, “I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you.” So that with good courage we say, “The Lord is my helper. I will not fear. What can man do to me?”
note: Contentment, money worries, and courage

keywords: what can man do to me
tags.when_helps: A believer anxious about money or afraid of others who needs reminding they are not forsaken.

display_text: Be free from the love of money, content with such things as you have, for he has said, “I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you.” So that with good courage we say, “The Lord is my helper. I will not fear. What can man do to me?”
plain: Do not love money; be content with what you have, because God has promised never to leave or abandon you. So we can say boldly that the Lord helps us and we will not fear what anyone can do.
core_idea: Be content; God will never leave you

text: “Come, and let us return to Yahweh; for he has torn us to pieces, and he will heal us; he has injured us, and he will bind up our wounds. After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him. Let us acknowledge Yahweh. Let us press on to know Yahweh. As surely as the sun rises, Yahweh will appear. He will come to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.”
note: Hope of healing and renewal after being broken

tags.when_helps: A believer wounded by hard times who needs trust that healing and renewal will come.

display_text: “Come, and let us return to Yahweh; for he has torn us to pieces, and he will heal us; he has injured us, and he will bind up our wounds. After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him. Let us acknowledge Yahweh. Let us press on to know Yahweh. As surely as the sun rises, Yahweh will appear. He will come to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.”
plain: Let us return to God. He has torn and wounded us, but he will heal us and soon raise us to live before him. Let us strive to know him; he will come as surely as sunrise, like spring rain.
core_idea: Return to God; he will heal what he wounded

plain_judge.issue: Drops the 'two days... third day' revival and 'let us acknowledge Yahweh'.

text: For I desire mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
note: Compassion matters more than outward ritual

tags.when_helps: A believer caught up in ritual or duty who needs reminding that mercy matters more.

display_text: For I desire mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
plain: God wants mercy, not sacrifice; he wants people to know him more than he wants burnt offerings.
core_idea: God wants mercy more than ritual

text: Sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap according to kindness. Break up your fallow ground; for it is time to seek Yahweh, until he comes and rains righteousness on you.
note: Fresh start; cultivating goodness and kindness

tags.when_helps: A believer feeling stagnant who senses it is time to turn the soil and begin again.

display_text: Sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap according to kindness. Break up your fallow ground; for it is time to seek Yahweh, until he comes and rains righteousness on you.
plain: Sow what is right and you will reap kindness. Break up your hard, unplowed ground, because it is time to seek God until he comes and showers righteousness on you.
core_idea: Break up hard ground and seek God

text: Wash yourselves, make yourself clean. Put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes. Cease to do evil. Learn to do well. Seek justice. Relieve the oppressed. Judge the fatherless. Plead for the widow.”
note: turning from wrong to doing good

tags.when_helps: Someone ready to turn from wrongdoing and wanting concrete ways to do good for the vulnerable.

display_text: Wash yourselves, make yourself clean. Put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes. Cease to do evil. Learn to do well. Seek justice. Relieve the oppressed. Judge the fatherless. Plead for the widow.
plain: Wash yourselves clean and put your evil deeds out of God's sight. Stop doing wrong and learn to do right: seek justice, help the oppressed, defend orphans and stand up for widows.
core_idea: Stop doing wrong; learn to do right

text: “Come now, and let us reason together,” says Yahweh: “Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
note: guilt and forgiveness, a clean start

tags.when_helps: Someone weighed down by past wrongs who needs to hear that they can be made clean.

display_text: Come now, and let us reason together,” says Yahweh: “Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
plain: God invites the people to talk things through: even if their sins are bright red like scarlet, they will become white as snow and wool.
core_idea: Though sins are scarlet, they can be white as snow

text: Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.
note: hope for peace

tags.when_helps: Someone disheartened by war and conflict who wants to hold on to a vision of peace.

display_text: Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.
plain: Nations will no longer raise swords against one another, and they will not train for war any more.
core_idea: Nations will stop learning war

text: Stop trusting in man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for of what account is he?
note: misplaced trust in people

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone let down by people they relied on, reminded not to stake everything on human approval.

display_text: Stop trusting in man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for of what account is he?
plain: Stop putting your trust in human beings; their life is only a breath, so what are they really worth?
core_idea: Do not rely on mere mortals

text: Woe to those who join house to house, who lay field to field, until there is no room, and you are made to dwell alone in the middle of the land!
note: greed that leaves you alone

tags.when_helps: Someone caught up in accumulating more property or wealth, warned it can leave them isolated.

display_text: Woe to those who join house to house, who lay field to field, until there is no room, and you are made to dwell alone in the middle of the land!
plain: Shame on those who keep buying up house after house and field after field until there is no room left for anyone, and they end up living alone in the land.
core_idea: Endless acquiring leaves you alone

text: Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil; who put darkness for light, and light for darkness; who put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter! Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!
note: self-deception and arrogance

tags.when_helps: Someone troubled by a world that twists right and wrong, or tempted to trust only their own cleverness.

display_text: Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil; who put darkness for light, and light for darkness; who put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter! Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!
plain: Shame on those who call evil good and good evil, who swap darkness for light and bitter for sweet. Shame on those who think themselves wise and clever.
core_idea: Woe to those who call evil good

text: Then I said, “Woe is me! For I am undone, because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips: for my eyes have seen the King, Yahweh of Armies!”
note: feeling unworthy before something greater

tags.when_helps: Someone suddenly aware of their own unworthiness before something holy.

display_text: Then I said, “Woe is me! For I am undone, because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips: for my eyes have seen the King, Yahweh of Armies!”
plain: The prophet cried out that he was ruined, a man with unclean lips living among people with unclean lips, because he had seen God, the King.
core_idea: Seeing God, I see my own unworthiness

text: I heard the Lord’s voice, saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here I am. Send me!”
note: answering a call, stepping forward

situations: a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: Someone sensing a calling and gathering the courage to answer it.

display_text: I heard the Lord’s voice, saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here I am. Send me!”
plain: I heard the Lord ask whom he should send and who would go. I answered: here I am, send me.
core_idea: Here I am; send me

text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. Those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, on them the light has shined.
note: light after a long darkness

tags.when_helps: Someone who has walked long in darkness and needs to believe light can break through.

display_text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. Those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, on them the light has shined.
plain: People who walked in darkness have seen a great light; light has shone on those living in the shadow of death.
core_idea: Light has dawned on those in darkness

text: “The bricks have fallen, but we will build with cut stone. The sycamore fig trees have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place.”
note: rebuilding after loss, defiance or pride

situations: loss of a dream or plan
loss of a home or something valued
tags.when_helps: Someone whose plans have collapsed and who wants resolve to rebuild something stronger.

display_text: “The bricks have fallen, but we will build with cut stone. The sycamore fig trees have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place.”
plain: The people boasted: the brick buildings have fallen, but we will rebuild in cut stone; the fig trees are cut down, but we will plant cedars instead.
core_idea: Proud boast: we will rebuild bigger

plain_judge.issue: Adds 'the people boasted', a framing the passage itself does not state.

text: Should an ax brag against him who chops with it? Should a saw exalt itself above him who saws with it? As if a rod should lift those who lift it up, or as if a staff should lift up someone who is not wood.
note: arrogance, forgetting what made your success possible

tags.when_helps: Someone taking full credit for success, reminded they are a tool in larger hands.

display_text: Should an ax brag against him who chops with it? Should a saw exalt itself above him who saws with it? As if a rod should lift those who lift it up, or as if a staff should lift up someone who is not wood.
plain: Can an axe boast against the one who swings it, or a saw against the one who uses it? That would be like a stick trying to lift the person holding it.
core_idea: A tool cannot boast against its user

text: The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat; The calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf together; and a little child will lead them.
note: hope for peace between enemies

tags.when_helps: Someone weary of conflict who wants an image of enemies living together in peace.

display_text: The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat; The calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf together; and a little child will lead them.
plain: The wolf will live with the lamb and the leopard lie down with the young goat; calf and lion will be together, and a little child will lead them.
core_idea: Enemies at peace, led by a child

text: Behold, God is my salvation. I will trust, and will not be afraid; for Yah, Yahweh, is my strength and song; and he has become my salvation.”
note: trust overcoming fear

keywords: I will trust, and will not be afraid
tags.when_helps: A believer facing fear who wants to lean on God as their strength.

display_text: Behold, God is my salvation. I will trust, and will not be afraid; for Yah, Yahweh, is my strength and song; and he has become my salvation.
plain: God is my salvation; I will trust him and not be afraid, because the Lord is my strength and my song and has saved me.
core_idea: I trust God and will not be afraid

text: How you have fallen from heaven, morning star, son of the dawn! How you are cut down to the ground, who laid the nations low! You said in your heart, “I will ascend into heaven! note: pride and ambition before a fall

tags.when_helps: Someone driven by soaring ambition, shown how overreaching pride ends in a fall.

display_text: How you have fallen from heaven, morning star, son of the dawn! How you are cut down to the ground, who laid the nations low! You said in your heart, “I will ascend into heaven! I will exalt my throne above the stars of God! I will sit on the mountain of assembly, in the far north! I will ascend above the heights of the clouds! I will make myself like the Most High!” Yet you shall be brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit.
plain: The proud one who planned to climb above the stars and make himself like the Most High has fallen from heaven like the morning star, and will be brought down to the depths of the grave.
core_idea: Pride that reaches for heaven falls to the pit

text: Give counsel! Execute justice! Make your shade like the night in the middle of the noonday! Hide the outcasts! Don’t betray the fugitive!
note: sheltering outcasts and the vulnerable

tags.when_helps: Someone moved to protect outcasts and refugees, urged to act justly and not betray them.

display_text: Give counsel! Execute justice! Make your shade like the night in the middle of the noonday! Hide the outcasts! Don’t betray the fugitive!
plain: Give advice and do justice. Shelter the outcasts like shade at midday; hide them, and do not betray those who are fleeing.
core_idea: Shelter outcasts; do not betray the fugitive

text: My heart flutters. Horror has frightened me. The twilight that I desired has been turned into trembling for me.
note: anxiety, rest turned to dread

tags.when_helps: Someone gripped by panic where they hoped for rest, who needs to know others have felt this.

display_text: My heart flutters. Horror has frightened me. The twilight that I desired has been turned into trembling for me.
plain: My heart is racing and horror has seized me; the evening I longed for has turned to trembling.
core_idea: The evening I longed for became dread

text: One calls to me out of Seir, “Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?” The watchman said, “The morning comes, and also the night. If you will inquire, inquire. Come back again.”
note: Waiting through a dark time; asking when it ends

tags.when_helps: Someone waiting through a dark time and asking how long it will last.

display_text: One calls to me out of Seir, “Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?” The watchman said, “The morning comes, and also the night. If you will inquire, inquire. Come back again.”
plain: Someone calls to the watchman asking how much of the night is left. The watchman answers that morning is coming, but night too; ask again if you wish, and come back.
core_idea: Morning comes, and night too

text: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.
note: Grief and hope that tears will be wiped away

tags.when_helps: A believer in grief who needs the promise that death will not have the last word.

display_text: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.
plain: God will swallow up death for ever and wipe the tears from every face, and remove his people's disgrace from the whole earth, because God has said so.
core_idea: God will end death and wipe away all tears

text: You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you. Trust in Yahweh forever; for in Yah, Yahweh, is an everlasting Rock.
note: Anxiety; finding peace through steady trust

tags.when_helps: A believer whose mind is restless who wants to anchor it in trust.

display_text: You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you. Trust in Yahweh forever; for in Yah, Yahweh, is an everlasting Rock.
plain: God keeps in perfect peace those whose minds stay fixed on him because they trust him. So trust God for ever; he is a rock that lasts for ever.
core_idea: Trust in God keeps the mind in perfect peace

text: With my soul I have desired you in the night. Yes, with my spirit within me will I seek you earnestly; for when your judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
note: Spiritual longing and seeking in the night

tags.when_helps: A believer awake at night with a deep longing for God.

display_text: With my soul I have desired you in the night. Yes, with my spirit within me will I seek you earnestly; for when your judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
plain: I long for you, God, through the night, and seek you with all my spirit, because when your judgements are seen on earth, people learn what is right.
core_idea: I long for God in the night

text: Just as a woman with child, who draws near the time of her delivery, is in pain and cries out in her pangs; so we have been before you, Yahweh. We have been with child. We have been in pain. We gave birth, it seems, only to wind. We have not worked any deliverance in the earth; neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen.
note: Painful effort that seems to come to nothing

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone who laboured hard and painfully only to produce nothing, needing that disappointment voiced.

display_text: Just as a woman with child, who draws near the time of her delivery, is in pain and cries out in her pangs; so we have been before you, Yahweh. We have been with child. We have been in pain. We gave birth, it seems, only to wind. We have not worked any deliverance in the earth; neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen.
plain: Like a woman in labour crying out in pain, we have suffered before you, God, but have given birth only to wind; we have achieved no rescue on the earth.
core_idea: We laboured in pain and produced only wind

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen'.

text: Come, my people, enter into your rooms, and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourself for a little moment, until the indignation is past.
note: Withdrawing to wait out a storm

keywords: hide yourself for a little moment
tags.when_helps: Someone caught in a storm who could withdraw and shelter until it passes.

display_text: Come, my people, enter into your rooms, and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourself for a little moment, until the indignation is past.
plain: Go into your rooms, my people, and shut the doors. Hide for a little while until the anger has passed.
core_idea: Shelter a little while until it passes

text: For thus said the Lord Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.”
note: Restlessness; strength found in quiet and rest

tags.when_helps: Someone frantically trying to fix everything who needs to hear that strength lies in rest and quiet.

display_text: For thus said the Lord Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.”
plain: God says you will be saved by turning back and resting; your strength will come from quietness and trust.
core_idea: Strength lies in quietness and trust

text: Though the Lord may give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your teachers won’t be hidden any more, but your eyes will see your teachers; and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way. Walk in it.”
note: Adversity and indecision; finding guidance on the path

keywords: this is the way, walk in it
tags.when_helps: A believer in adversity unsure which way to turn who needs the promise of guidance.

display_text: Though the Lord may give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your teachers won’t be hidden any more, but your eyes will see your teachers; and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way. Walk in it.”
plain: Even if God gives you hardship and suffering to live on, your teachers will no longer be hidden; whichever way you turn, you will hear a voice behind you saying, this is the way, walk in it.
core_idea: Even in hardship you will hear: this is the way

text: A man shall be as a hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the storm, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a large rock in a weary land.
note: Being a shelter for others in hard times

situations: caring for a sick or ageing relative
tags.when_helps: Someone worn down who needs shelter, or who wants to be shelter for another.

display_text: A man shall be as a hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the storm, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a large rock in a weary land.
plain: Each person will be like a shelter from the wind and storm, like streams in a dry land, like the shade of a great rock in a weary country.
core_idea: A person can be shelter for others

plain_judge.issue: 'A man' generalised to 'each person', loosening who is meant.

text: The work of righteousness will be peace; and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever. My people will live in a peaceful habitation, in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting places.
note: Doing right as the path to inner peace

tags.when_helps: Someone longing for a settled, peaceful life who is reminded peace grows from doing right.

display_text: The work of righteousness will be peace; and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever. My people will live in a peaceful habitation, in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting places.
plain: Doing right will bring peace, and its result will be quiet and confidence for ever. God's people will live in peaceful homes, safe and quietly at rest.
core_idea: Righteousness brings peace, quiet and safety

text: Yahweh, be gracious to us. We have waited for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
note: Prayer for daily strength in trouble

tags.when_helps: A believer who has waited long in trouble and asks for strength each morning.

display_text: Yahweh, be gracious to us. We have waited for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
plain: Lord, be kind to us; we have waited for you. Be our strength every morning and our rescue in times of trouble.
core_idea: God, be our strength every morning

text: The wilderness and the dry land will be glad. The desert will rejoice and blossom like a rose.
note: Hope after a barren, dry season

tags.when_helps: Someone in a barren, dry season who needs an image of life returning.

display_text: The wilderness and the dry land will be glad. The desert will rejoice and blossom like a rose.
plain: The wilderness and dry land will be glad; the desert will rejoice and bloom like a rose.
core_idea: The desert will bloom

text: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees. Tell those who have a fearful heart, “Be strong. Don’t be afraid. Behold, your God will come with vengeance, God’s retribution. He will come and save you.
note: Fear and weakness; encouraging the fearful

tags.when_helps: A believer with a fearful heart, or someone supporting one, who needs strengthening.

display_text: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees. Tell those who have a fearful heart, “Be strong. Don’t be afraid. Behold, your God will come with vengeance, God’s retribution. He will come and save you.
plain: Strengthen tired hands and weak knees. Tell the frightened to be strong and not afraid, because their God is coming to set things right and save them.
core_idea: Be strong, do not fear; God will save you

plain_judge.issue: Softens 'God will come with vengeance, God's retribution' to 'set things right'.

text: I said, “In the middle of my life I go into the gates of Sheol. I am deprived of the residue of my years.” I said, “I won’t see Yah, Yah in the land of the living. I will see man no more with the inhabitants of the world. My dwelling is removed, and is carried away from me like a shepherd’s tent. I have rolled up, like a weaver, my life. He will cut me off from the loom. From day even to night you will make an end of me.
note: Facing serious illness and death in mid-life

keywords: in the middle of my life
tags.when_helps: Someone facing serious illness in mid-life who grieves the years they may lose.

display_text: I said, “In the middle of my life I go into the gates of Sheol. I am deprived of the residue of my years.” I said, “I won’t see Yah, Yah in the land of the living. I will see man no more with the inhabitants of the world. My dwelling is removed, and is carried away from me like a shepherd’s tent. I have rolled up, like a weaver, my life. He will cut me off from the loom. From day even to night you will make an end of me.

plain_judge.issue: Adds Hezekiah's illness as context; drops shepherd's tent and 'you will make an end of me'.

text: Behold, for peace I had great anguish, but you have in love for my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption; for you have cast all my sins behind your back.
note: Relief and forgiveness after anguish

tags.when_helps: A believer emerging from anguish who feels rescued and forgiven.

display_text: Behold, for peace I had great anguish, but you have in love for my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption; for you have cast all my sins behind your back.
plain: I suffered bitterly instead of having peace, but in your love you saved my life from the pit and threw all my sins behind your back.
core_idea: God in love saved me and cast my sins away

text: “Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God. “Speak comfortably to Jerusalem; and call out to her that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received of Yahweh’s hand double for all her sins.”
note: Comfort after a long struggle is over

tags.when_helps: A believer after a long ordeal who needs to hear that the struggle is over and they are pardoned.

display_text: “Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God. “Speak comfortably to Jerusalem; and call out to her that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received of Yahweh’s hand double for all her sins.”
plain: God tells his messengers to comfort his people. Speak tenderly to Jerusalem: her hard service is over, her guilt is forgiven, and she has paid twice over for her sins.
core_idea: Comfort my people: their hardship is over

text: The voice of one saying, “Cry!” One said, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field. The grass withers, the flower fades, because Yahweh’s breath blows on it. Surely the people are like grass. The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”
note: Mortality and the fleeting nature of life

tags.when_helps: Someone confronting how fleeting human glory is and looking for something that lasts.

display_text: The voice of one saying, “Cry!” One said, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field. The grass withers, the flower fades, because Yahweh’s breath blows on it. Surely the people are like grass. The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”
plain: A voice is told to cry out a message: all people are like grass, and their glory like wild flowers. The grass withers and the flower fades when God's breath blows, but God's word lasts for ever.
core_idea: People fade like grass; God's word endures

text: Behold, the Lord Yahweh will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him. He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young.
note: Being gently cared for; tenderness for the vulnerable

tags.when_helps: A believer, perhaps a weary parent, who needs the image of being gently carried.

display_text: Behold, the Lord Yahweh will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him. He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young.
plain: God will come in power and rule. Yet he will care for his flock like a shepherd: he gathers the lambs in his arms, carries them close, and gently leads the mothers with young.
core_idea: God carries his lambs like a gentle shepherd

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'his reward is with him, and his recompense before him'.

text: Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? The everlasting God, Yahweh, The Creator of the ends of the earth, doesn’t faint. He isn’t weary. His understanding is unsearchable. He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might. Even the youths faint and get weary, and the young men utterly fall; But those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
note: Exhaustion and weariness; renewed strength

tags.when_helps: A believer utterly worn out who needs the promise of renewed strength.

display_text: Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? The everlasting God, Yahweh, The Creator of the ends of the earth, doesn’t faint. He isn’t weary. His understanding is unsearchable. He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might. Even the youths faint and get weary, and the young men utterly fall; But those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
plain: The eternal God, creator of the earth, never tires, and his understanding has no limit. He strengthens the weak. Even the young grow tired and fall, but those who wait for God will renew their strength and soar like eagles.
core_idea: Those who wait for God renew their strength

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'run and not be weary, walk and not faint' and strength to the mightless.

text: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
note: Fear and feeling alone; being upheld

tags.when_helps: A believer gripped by fear who needs to hear they are held and helped.

display_text: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
plain: Do not be afraid, because I am with you; do not lose heart, because I am your God. I will strengthen you, help you, and hold you up with my righteous right hand.
core_idea: Do not fear; God is with you and upholds you

text: “Behold, my servant, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delights— I have put my Spirit on him. He will bring justice to the nations. He will not shout, nor raise his voice, nor cause it to be heard in the street. He won’t break a bruised reed. He won’t quench a dimly burning wick. He will faithfully bring justice.
note: Quiet gentleness toward the fragile and hurting

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels bruised and barely flickering, needing to know they will be handled gently.

display_text: Behold, my servant, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delights— I have put my Spirit on him. He will bring justice to the nations. plain: God presents his chosen servant, filled with his Spirit, who will bring justice to the nations. He will not shout or make a show; he will not break a bruised reed or snuff out a faint flame.
core_idea: God's servant is gentle with the bruised and faint

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'in whom my soul delights' and 'he will faithfully bring justice'.

text: I will bring the blind by a way that they don’t know. I will lead them in paths that they don’t know. I will make darkness light before them, and crooked places straight. I will do these things, and I will not forsake them.
note: Uncertainty about the way ahead; not forsaken

tags.when_helps: A believer walking an unknown path in the dark who needs assurance they will not be forsaken.

display_text: I will bring the blind by a way that they don’t know. I will lead them in paths that they don’t know. I will make darkness light before them, and crooked places straight. I will do these things, and I will not forsake them.
plain: God says he will lead the blind along roads and paths they do not know, turn their darkness into light and their crooked places straight, and never abandon them.
core_idea: God leads the blind on unknown paths

text: But now Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
note: Belonging and being known; fear eased

tags.when_helps: A believer afraid and doubting their worth who needs to hear they are known by name and belong.

display_text: But now Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
plain: God, who created and formed his people, says: do not be afraid, because I have rescued you. I have called you by name; you are mine.
core_idea: Do not fear; God called you by name

note: Going through overwhelming trials; not alone

tags.when_helps: Someone going through an ordeal who needs assurance they will not be overwhelmed or alone.

display_text: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they will not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, and flame will not scorch you.
plain: When you go through deep waters, I will be with you, and the rivers will not sweep you away. When you walk through fire, you will not be burned, and the flames will not hurt you.
core_idea: Through water and fire, God is with you

text: “Don’t remember the former things, and don’t consider the things of old. Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
note: Letting go of the past; a new beginning

tags.when_helps: Someone stuck on the past who needs to look for a new beginning now emerging.

display_text: Don’t remember the former things, and don’t consider the things of old. Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
plain: Do not dwell on the past or what happened long ago. God is doing something new; it is springing up now. He will make a road through the wilderness and rivers in the desert.
core_idea: Forget the past; God is doing a new thing

text: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions, and, as a cloud, your sins. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.
note: Guilt and forgiveness; invitation to return

tags.when_helps: A believer who has drifted and fears their wrongs, invited to return and be forgiven.

display_text: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions, and, as a cloud, your sins. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.
plain: God says he has wiped away your wrongdoings and sins like a thick cloud; come back to him, because he has rescued you.
core_idea: Your sins are wiped away; return to God

text: “Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, that have been carried from their birth, that have been carried from the womb. Even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver.
note: Ageing; being carried through every stage of life

keywords: even to gray hairs I will carry you
tags.when_helps: Someone growing old or weary who needs to hear they will be carried to the end.

display_text: Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, that have been carried from their birth, that have been carried from the womb. Even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver.

display_text: Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver. I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
plain: God says he has refined his people, though not the way silver is refined; he chose them in the furnace of suffering.
core_idea: Chosen in the furnace of suffering

text: Oh that you had listened to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
note: Regret over ignored advice; peace lost

display_text: Oh that you had listened to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.

text: But I said, “I have labored in vain. I have spent my strength in vain for nothing; yet surely the justice due to me is with Yahweh, and my reward with my God.”
note: Feeling one's work has been in vain

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels their hard work came to nothing and needs to trust it is still seen.

text: But Zion said, “Yahweh has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me.” “Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? display_text: But Zion said, “Yahweh has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me.” “Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? display_text: The Lord Yahweh has given me the tongue of those who are taught, that I may know how to sustain with words him who is weary. He wakens morning by morning, he wakens my ear to hear as those who are taught.

text: Who among you fears Yahweh, and obeys the voice of his servant? He who walks in darkness, and has no light, let him trust in Yahweh’s name, and rely on his God.

core_idea: In darkness without light, trust God

display_text: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look on the earth beneath; for the heavens will vanish away like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment; and its inhabitants will die in the same way: but my salvation will be forever, and my righteousness will not be abolished.

display_text: “Listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law: Don’t fear the reproach of men, and don’t be dismayed at their insults.
