tags.when_helps: Someone living in constant fear of a powerful oppressor, helped to see them in proportion.

display_text: I, even I, am he who comforts you. Who are you, that you are afraid of man who shall die, and of the son of man who will be made as grass? Have you forgotten Yahweh your Maker, who stretched out the heavens, and laid the foundations of the earth? Do you live in fear continually all day because of the fury of the oppressor, when he prepares to destroy? Where is the fury of the oppressor?
plain: God says: I am the one who comforts you. Why fear mortals who wither like grass, and forget God your Maker who spread out the heavens? Why live in constant fear of the oppressor's fury? Where is that fury now?
core_idea: Why fear mortals when God comforts you?

text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
note: The gift of bringing good news and peace

tags.when_helps: A believer celebrating good news or the joy of bringing peace to others.

display_text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
plain: How beautiful is the arrival of the messenger crossing the mountains with good news of peace and salvation, telling Zion that its God reigns.
core_idea: Beautiful are those who bring good news

text: “For a small moment I have forsaken you; but with great mercies will I gather you. In overflowing wrath I hid my face from you for a moment; but with everlasting loving kindness I will have mercy on you,” says Yahweh your Redeemer.
note: Feeling abandoned for a time; mercy returns

keywords: for a small moment I have forsaken you
tags.when_helps: A believer feeling abandoned by God who needs hope that the absence is brief and mercy returns.

display_text: “For a small moment I have forsaken you; but with great mercies will I gather you. In overflowing wrath I hid my face from you for a moment; but with everlasting loving kindness I will have mercy on you,” says Yahweh your Redeemer.
plain: God says he abandoned his people for a brief moment, but will gather them back with great mercy; in a flash of anger he hid his face, but his everlasting love will have mercy on them.
core_idea: Brief abandonment, everlasting mercy

text: For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed; but my loving kindness will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be removed,” says Yahweh who has mercy on you.
note: When everything shifts; love that stays

tags.when_helps: Someone whose world is shaking who needs a love that will not be removed.

display_text: For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed; but my loving kindness will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be removed,” says Yahweh who has mercy on you.
plain: Even if the mountains are moved and the hills shaken, God's steadfast love will not leave you, and his promise of peace will not be taken away.
core_idea: God's love outlasts the mountains

text: “Hey! Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price. Why do you spend money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which doesn’t satisfy? Listen diligently to me, and eat that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in richness.
note: Chasing things that don't satisfy; spiritual hunger

tags.when_helps: Someone spending themselves on things that never satisfy, invited to what truly nourishes.

display_text: Hey! Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price. Why do you spend money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which doesn’t satisfy? Listen diligently to me, and eat that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in richness.
plain: Come, all who are thirsty, come to the water; even with no money, come and eat for free. Why spend money on what is not food, and work for what never satisfies? Listen to God and feed your soul.
core_idea: Why spend yourself on what does not satisfy?

text: “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways,” says Yahweh. “For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
note: Not understanding why things happen

tags.when_helps: A believer unable to understand why things happen, invited to trust a larger view.

display_text: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways,” says Yahweh. “For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
plain: God says his thoughts and ways are not like ours: as the heavens are higher than the earth, so his ways and thoughts are higher than ours.
core_idea: God's ways are higher than our ways

text: For you shall go out with joy, and be led out with peace. The mountains and the hills will break out before you into singing; and all the trees of the fields will clap their hands.
note: Joy and peace at a new departure

tags.when_helps: Someone setting out on a new chapter with gladness, wanting the world to sing along.

display_text: For you shall go out with joy, and be led out with peace. The mountains and the hills will break out before you into singing; and all the trees of the fields will clap their hands.
plain: You will go out with joy and be led in peace. The mountains and hills will burst into song before you, and all the trees will clap their hands.
core_idea: You will go out in joy and peace

text: The righteous perish, and no one lays it to heart. Merciful men are taken away, and no one considers that the righteous is taken away from the evil. He enters into peace. They rest in their beds, each one who walks in his uprightness.
note: Grief when good people die; they rest in peace

tags.safety_reason: Presents the death of the righteous as being taken from evil into peace and rest.
tags.when_helps: Someone grieving a good person who died, wanting to believe they have found peace.

display_text: The righteous perish, and no one lays it to heart. Merciful men are taken away, and no one considers that the righteous is taken away from the evil. He enters into peace. They rest in their beds, each one who walks in his uprightness.
plain: Good people die and no one takes it to heart; the kind are taken away and no one realises they are spared from coming evil. They enter peace and rest, those who lived upright lives.
core_idea: The righteous who die enter peace

text: For thus says the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.
note: Humility and remorse; being revived

tags.when_helps: Someone humbled and sorry who needs to hear that the holy dwells with the contrite and revives them.

display_text: For thus says the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.
plain: The high and holy God, who lives for ever, says he lives in the high and holy place, and also with those who are crushed and humble in spirit, to revive them.
core_idea: God dwells with the humble and crushed in spirit

text: “Isn’t this the fast that I have chosen: to release the bonds of wickedness, to undo the straps of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and that you break every yoke? Isn’t it to distribute your bread to the hungry, and that you bring the poor who are cast out to your house? When you see the naked, that you cover him; and that you not hide yourself from your own flesh? Then your light will break out as the morning, and your healing will appear quickly; then your righteousness shall go before you; and Yahweh’s glory will be your rear guard.
note: True devotion as helping others; purpose through service

tags.when_helps: Someone whose religious practice feels hollow, shown that true devotion is freeing and feeding others.

display_text: Isn’t this the fast that I have chosen: to release the bonds of wickedness, to undo the straps of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and that you break every yoke? Isn’t it to distribute your bread to the hungry, and that you bring the poor who are cast out to your house? When you see the naked, that you cover him; and that you not hide yourself from your own flesh? Then your light will break out as the morning, and your healing will appear quickly; then your righteousness shall go before you; and Yahweh’s glory will be your rear guard.
plain: The fast God wants is this: break the chains of injustice and free the oppressed; feed the hungry, shelter the homeless poor, clothe the naked, and do not turn from your own. Then your light will break out like dawn.
core_idea: True devotion is freeing the oppressed and feeding the hungry

plain_judge.issue: Drops the promised healing, righteousness going before, and God's glory as rear guard.

text: We look for light, but see darkness; for brightness, but we walk in obscurity. We grope for the wall like the blind. Yes, we grope as those who have no eyes. We stumble at noon as if it were twilight. Among those who are strong, we are like dead men.
note: Feeling lost and groping in darkness

keywords: grope for the wall like the blind
tags.when_helps: Someone looking for light and finding only confusion, who needs to know others have groped in the dark.

display_text: We look for light, but see darkness; for brightness, but we walk in obscurity. We grope for the wall like the blind. Yes, we grope as those who have no eyes. We stumble at noon as if it were twilight. Among those who are strong, we are like dead men.
plain: We hope for light but find darkness, for brightness but walk in gloom. We feel along the wall like the blind and stumble at noon as if it were dusk; among the strong we are like the dead.
core_idea: We look for light but walk in darkness

text: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory has risen on you. For, behold, darkness will cover the earth, and thick darkness the peoples; but Yahweh will arise on you, and his glory shall be seen on you.
note: Rising from darkness; hope and renewal

tags.when_helps: A believer in a dark time called to rise up because light has come to them.

display_text: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory has risen on you. For, behold, darkness will cover the earth, and thick darkness the peoples; but Yahweh will arise on you, and his glory shall be seen on you.
plain: Get up and shine, because your light has come and God's glory has risen on you. Darkness will cover the earth and its peoples, but God will rise on you and his glory will be seen on you.
core_idea: Arise, shine: your light has come

text: The sun will be no more your light by day; nor will the brightness of the moon give light to you, but Yahweh will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory. Your sun will not go down any more, nor will your moon withdraw itself; for Yahweh will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will end.
note: Mourning coming to an end

tags.when_helps: A grieving believer who needs hope that their days of mourning will one day end.

display_text: The sun will be no more your light by day; nor will the brightness of the moon give light to you, but Yahweh will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory. Your sun will not go down any more, nor will your moon withdraw itself; for Yahweh will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will end.
plain: You will no longer need the sun or moon for light, because God will be your everlasting light and your glory. Your sun will never set again, and your days of mourning will be over.
core_idea: God will be your light; mourning will end

text: The Lord Yahweh’s Spirit is on me; because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to those who are bound; to proclaim the year of Yahweh’s favor, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all who mourn; to provide for those who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh, that he may be glorified.
note: Heartbreak and mourning; joy given for ashes

tags.when_helps: Someone heartbroken or mourning who needs a promise of comfort, freedom and joy restored.

display_text: The Lord Yahweh’s Spirit is on me; because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to those who are bound; to proclaim the year of Yahweh’s favor, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all who mourn; to provide for those who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh, that he may be glorified.
plain: The speaker says God's Spirit has anointed him to bring good news to the humble, heal the broken-hearted, free captives, and comfort all who mourn, giving them beauty for ashes, joy for mourning and praise for despair.
core_idea: Sent to heal the broken-hearted and comfort mourners

plain_judge.issue: Drops "the day of vengeance of our God", softening the hard saying.

text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh! My soul will be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation. He has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
note: Overflowing joy and gratitude

tags.when_helps: A believer overflowing with gratitude and joy who wants words to rejoice in God.

display_text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh! My soul will be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation. He has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
plain: I will rejoice greatly in God, and my soul will be glad, because he has dressed me in salvation and righteousness, like a groom in his garland or a bride in her jewels.
core_idea: I rejoice: God has clothed me in salvation

text: You will not be called Forsaken any more; nor will your land be called Desolate any more: but you will be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah; for Yahweh delights in you, and your land will be married.
note: Feeling forsaken; being delighted in again

tags.when_helps: Someone who has felt forsaken or desolate and needs to hear they are delighted in.

display_text: You will not be called Forsaken any more; nor will your land be called Desolate any more: but you will be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah; for Yahweh delights in you, and your land will be married.
plain: You will no longer be called Forsaken, nor your land Desolate. You will be called My Delight, and your land Married, because God delights in you.
core_idea: No longer forsaken: God delights in you

text: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and in his pity he redeemed them. He bore them, and carried them all the days of old.
note: Not suffering alone; being carried in love

keywords: in all their affliction he was afflicted
tags.when_helps: A believer suffering who needs to know God shares their pain and carries them.

display_text: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and in his pity he redeemed them. He bore them, and carried them all the days of old.
plain: In all their suffering God suffered too, and his presence saved them. In love and pity he rescued them, and lifted and carried them through all the years of old.
core_idea: God suffers with his people and carries them

text: For we have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteousness is like a polluted garment. We all fade like a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away.
note: Guilt and a sense of one's own frailty

tags.when_helps: Someone confronting their own failings who finds honesty in a shared confession of human frailty.

display_text: For we have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteousness is like a polluted garment. We all fade like a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away.
plain: We have all become unclean, and even our good deeds are like filthy rags. We all wither like leaves, and our sins sweep us away like the wind.
core_idea: Our sins sweep us away like leaves

text: But now, Yahweh, you are our Father. We are the clay, and you our potter. We all are the work of your hand.
note: Surrender; being shaped by a greater hand

tags.when_helps: A believer unsure who they are, finding rest in being shaped by God's hands.

display_text: But now, Yahweh, you are our Father. We are the clay, and you our potter. We all are the work of your hand.
plain: Yet, God, you are our Father. We are the clay and you are the potter; we are all the work of your hands.
core_idea: We are clay; God is the potter

text: “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things will not be remembered, nor come into mind. But be glad and rejoice forever in that which I create; for, behold, I create Jerusalem to be a delight, and her people a joy. I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and delight in my people; and the voice of weeping and the voice of crying will be heard in her no more.
note: A fresh start; weeping comes to an end

keywords: new heavens and a new earth
tags.when_helps: A believer worn by sorrow who longs for a renewed world where weeping ends.

display_text: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things will not be remembered, nor come into mind. But be glad and rejoice forever in that which I create; for, behold, I create Jerusalem to be a delight, and her people a joy. I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and delight in my people; and the voice of weeping and the voice of crying will be heard in her no more.
plain: God says he is creating new heavens and a new earth, and the past will be forgotten. Rejoice for ever in what he creates. He will delight in his people, and weeping will never be heard in Jerusalem again.
core_idea: God makes all things new; weeping will end

text: It will happen that, before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.
note: Being heard before you even ask

keywords: before they call, I will answer
tags.when_helps: A believer wondering whether their prayers are heard.

display_text: It will happen that, before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.
plain: God says that before people call he will answer, and while they are still speaking he will hear.
core_idea: God answers before we call

text: As one whom his mother comforts, so will I comfort you. You will be comforted in Jerusalem.”
note: Needing comfort like a child from a mother

tags.when_helps: Someone hurting who longs for tender, motherly comfort.

display_text: As one whom his mother comforts, so will I comfort you. You will be comforted in Jerusalem.
plain: God says he will comfort you as a mother comforts her child.
core_idea: God comforts like a mother

text: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations, knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance. Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.
note: hardship as a way to grow endurance

tags.when_helps: A believer in a season of trials who needs to see hardship as building endurance and maturity.

display_text: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations, knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance. Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.
plain: When you face all kinds of trials, consider it pure joy, because testing your faith builds endurance. Let endurance finish its work, so that you become mature and complete, lacking nothing.
core_idea: Trials build endurance; welcome them with joy

text: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach; and it will be given to him. But let him ask in faith, without any doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed. For that man shouldn’t think that he will receive anything from the Lord. He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
note: indecision, doubt, seeking wisdom

tags.when_helps: A believer unsure what to do who needs encouragement to ask God for wisdom and stop wavering.

display_text: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach; and it will be given to him. But let him ask in faith, without any doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed. For that man shouldn’t think that he will receive anything from the Lord. He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
plain: If you lack wisdom, ask God, who gives generously to all without scolding, and you will receive it. But ask in faith without doubting; a doubter is like a wind-tossed wave, unstable, and should expect nothing from the Lord.
core_idea: Ask God for wisdom, in faith without doubting

text: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger; for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.
note: anger, listening before speaking

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
keywords: swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger
tags.when_helps: Someone about to react in anger who needs reminding to listen first and speak slowly.

display_text: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger; for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.
plain: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to get angry, because human anger does not produce the goodness God wants.
core_idea: Quick to listen, slow to speak and anger

text: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves. For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror; for he sees himself, and goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was. But he who looks into the perfect law of freedom, and continues, not being a hearer who forgets, but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed in what he does.
note: acting on what we know, not just knowing

tags.when_helps: Someone who keeps learning good ideas but not acting on them and needs a push to practise.

display_text: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves. For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror; for he sees himself, and goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was. But he who looks into the perfect law of freedom, and continues, not being a hearer who forgets, but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed in what he does.
plain: Do what God's word says; just listening fools you. A mere listener is like someone who sees their face in a mirror and forgets it at once. Whoever keeps to the law of freedom and acts will be blessed.
core_idea: Do what you hear, not only listen

text: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
note: caring for those who suffer

tags.when_helps: A believer wondering what genuine faith looks like who needs the plain answer of care for the vulnerable.

display_text: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
plain: Pure religion in God's eyes is this: caring for orphans and widows in their distress, and keeping yourself from being corrupted by the world.
core_idea: True religion: care for the vulnerable, stay unstained

text: What good is it, my brothers, if a man says he has faith, but has no works? Can faith save him? And if a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food, and one of you tells them, “Go in peace, be warmed and filled”; and yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs, what good is it? Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.
note: empty words versus real help

tags.when_helps: A believer whose faith has stayed in words who needs a challenge to meet others' real needs.

display_text: What good is it, my brothers, if a man says he has faith, but has no works? Can faith save him? And if a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food, and one of you tells them, “Go in peace, be warmed and filled”; and yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs, what good is it? Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.
plain: What use is saying you have faith if you do nothing? If someone lacks clothes and food and you just wish them well without giving what they need, what good is that? Faith without action is dead.
core_idea: Faith without action is dead

text: Indeed, we put bits into the horses’ mouths so that they may obey us, and we guide their whole body. Behold, the ships also, though they are so big and are driven by fierce winds, are yet guided by a very small rudder, wherever the pilot desires. So the tongue is also a little member, and boasts great things. See how a small fire can spread to a large forest!
note: the power of words, careless speech

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
keywords: the tongue is a small rudder
tags.when_helps: Someone who has said something they regret, or is about to, who needs to see how much small words can do.

display_text: Indeed, we put bits into the horses’ mouths so that they may obey us, and we guide their whole body. Behold, the ships also, though they are so big and are driven by fierce winds, are yet guided by a very small rudder, wherever the pilot desires. So the tongue is also a little member, and boasts great things. See how a small fire can spread to a large forest!
plain: A small bit steers a horse, and a small rudder steers a huge ship through strong winds. The tongue is small too, yet it boasts of great things. Think how a tiny spark sets a whole forest on fire.
core_idea: The small tongue has huge power

text: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good conduct that his deeds are done in gentleness of wisdom. But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, don’t boast and don’t lie against the truth. This wisdom is not that which comes down from above, but is earthly, sensual, and demonic. For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion and every evil deed. But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy. Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.
note: jealousy, ambition, true wisdom

tags.when_helps: Someone caught in rivalry or ambition who needs to tell worldly cleverness from wisdom that is gentle and peaceable.

display_text: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good conduct that his deeds are done in gentleness of wisdom. But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, don’t boast and don’t lie against the truth. This wisdom is not that which comes down from above, but is earthly, sensual, and demonic. For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion and every evil deed. plain: If you are wise, show it by good deeds done gently. Bitter jealousy and selfish ambition are not wisdom from above; they bring disorder and evil. Wisdom from above is pure, peaceful, gentle, merciful and sincere, and peacemakers reap righteousness.
core_idea: True wisdom is gentle and peaceful, not envious

plain_judge.issue: Drops "earthly, sensual, and demonic" and the command not to boast or lie; softens.

text: Where do wars and fightings among you come from? Don’t they come from your pleasures that war in your members? You lust, and don’t have. You murder and covet, and can’t obtain. note: where conflict and craving come from

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
keywords: pleasures that war in your members
tags.when_helps: Someone in repeated conflict who needs to see how their own unmet wants are fuelling it.

display_text: Where do wars and fightings among you come from? Don’t they come from your pleasures that war in your members? You lust, and don’t have. You murder and covet, and can’t obtain. plain_judge.issue: Drops "you murder and covet", softening the accusation.

note: judging and criticising others

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
keywords: who are you to judge another
tags.when_helps: Someone quick to criticise or judge others who needs to question their right to do so.

display_text: Don’t speak against one another, brothers. He who speaks against a brother and judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law, but a judge. Only one is the lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy. But who are you to judge another?

text: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow let’s go into this city, and spend a year there, trade, and make a profit.” Whereas you don’t know what your life will be like tomorrow. note: uncertainty of the future, brevity of life

situations: a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: Someone making confident plans, or anxious about them, who needs reminding how uncertain tomorrow is.

display_text: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow let’s go into this city, and spend a year there, trade, and make a profit.” Whereas you don’t know what your life will be like tomorrow. For what is your life? For you are a vapor, that appears for a little time, and then vanishes away. For you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will both live, and do this or that.”
plain: You plan next year's business as if sure of it, yet you don't know what tomorrow brings, for your life is a passing mist. Say instead, "If the Lord wills, we will live and do this."
core_idea: Life is brief; make plans subject to God's will

text: Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it, until it receives the early and late rain. You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.
note: patience while waiting

tags.when_helps: Someone impatient for results who needs the image of a farmer waiting patiently for the rain.

display_text: Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it, until it receives the early and late rain. You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.
plain: Be patient until the Lord comes. A farmer waits patiently for the rains and the harvest; be patient like that too, and steady your hearts, because the Lord's coming is near.
core_idea: Wait patiently, like a farmer, for the Lord

text: Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises.
note: responding to suffering and to joy

tags.when_helps: A believer who wants a simple word on how to meet both suffering and gladness.

display_text: Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises.
plain: If you are suffering, pray. If you are happy, sing praise.
core_idea: Pray in suffering; sing praise in joy

text: Confess your offenses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.
note: guilt, confession, healing together

keywords: confess your offenses to one another
tags.when_helps: A believer carrying a hidden wrong who needs encouragement to confess it to others and pray together.

display_text: Confess your offenses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.
plain: Admit your wrongs to each other and pray for each other so you can be healed. A good person's earnest prayer has great power.
core_idea: Confession and prayer for one another bring healing

text: “Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you. Before you were born, I sanctified you. I have appointed you a prophet to the nations.” Then I said, “Ah, Lord Yahweh! Behold, I don’t know how to speak; for I am a child.” But Yahweh said to me, “Don’t say, ‘I am a child;’ for you must go to whomever I send you, and you must say whatever I command you. Don’t be afraid because of them, for I am with you to rescue you,” says Yahweh.
note: Feeling too young or inadequate for a calling

situations: a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: A believer who feels too young or unqualified for a task they have been called to and fears others' reaction.

display_text: “Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you. Before you were born, I sanctified you. I have appointed you a prophet to the nations.” Then I said, “Ah, Lord Yahweh! Behold, I don’t know how to speak; for I am a child.” But Yahweh said to me, “Don’t say, ‘I am a child;’ for you must go to whomever I send you, and you must say whatever I command you. Don’t be afraid because of them, for I am with you to rescue you,” says Yahweh.
plain: God tells Jeremiah he knew and chose him before birth. Jeremiah protests that he is too young to speak; God says not to plead youth, to go and speak, and not to fear, for God is with him.
core_idea: God chose you before birth and goes with you

plain_judge.issue: Compresses God's command to say whatever he commands; drops promise to rescue.

text: “For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of living waters, and cut them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.
note: Chasing things that cannot satisfy

tags.when_helps: A believer who senses they have sought fulfilment in things that cannot hold it and has drifted from God.

display_text: For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of living waters, and cut them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.
plain: God says his people have done two wrongs: they left him, the source of living water, and dug their own cracked tanks that cannot hold water.
core_idea: Leaving God for empty substitutes that hold nothing

text: My anguish, my anguish! I am pained at my very heart! My heart trembles within me. I can’t hold my peace, because you have heard, O my soul, the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war.
note: Overwhelming anguish and dread

tags.when_helps: Someone whose heart is pounding with distress at news of violence or conflict and who needs to know others have felt it.

display_text: My anguish, my anguish! I am pained at my very heart! My heart trembles within me. I can’t hold my peace, because you have heard, O my soul, the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war.
plain: I am in agony, my heart pounding and trembling inside me. I cannot stay quiet, because I have heard the trumpet and the alarm of war.
core_idea: Anguish of heart at the sound of war

text: Yahweh says, “Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths, ‘Where is the good way?’ and walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls.
note: At a crossroads, seeking the good way

tags.when_helps: Someone at a crossroads, unsure which way to go, who needs a reminder to pause, look for tried paths and find rest.

display_text: Yahweh says, “Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths, ‘Where is the good way?’ and walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls.
plain: God says: stop at the crossroads and look; ask for the old, proven paths and which is the good way. Walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls.
core_idea: Seek the old good way and find rest

text: Oh that I could comfort myself against sorrow! My heart is faint within me.
note: Sorrow that will not be comforted

tags.when_helps: Someone weighed down by sorrow they cannot shake off who needs to hear the feeling named by someone long ago.

display_text: Oh that I could comfort myself against sorrow! My heart is faint within me.
plain: If only I could find comfort in my sorrow! My heart is weak inside me.
core_idea: Longing for comfort in deep sorrow

text: For the hurt of the daughter of my people, I am hurt. I mourn. Dismay has taken hold of me. Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Why then isn’t the health of the daughter of my people recovered? Oh that my head were waters, and my eyes a spring of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!
note: Grieving others' suffering; longing for healing

tags.when_helps: Someone grieving loss and suffering among their own people who longs for healing and wants their tears understood.

display_text: For the hurt of the daughter of my people, I am hurt. I mourn. Dismay has taken hold of me. Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Why then isn’t the health of the daughter of my people recovered? Oh that my head were waters, and my eyes a spring of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!
plain: I am wounded by my people's wound and mourn: is there no healing balm, no doctor, so why aren't they healed? I wish my eyes were a spring of tears to weep day and night for the dead.
core_idea: Grieving for others' suffering, longing for healing

text: Yahweh says, “Don’t let the wise man glory in his wisdom. Don’t let the mighty man glory in his might. Don’t let the rich man glory in his riches. But let him who glories glory in this, that he has understanding, and knows me, that I am Yahweh who exercises loving kindness, justice, and righteousness, in the earth; for I delight in these things,” says Yahweh.
note: Pride in wealth, strength and cleverness

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to rest their worth on cleverness, strength or wealth who needs reminding what truly matters.

display_text: Yahweh says, “Don’t let the wise man glory in his wisdom. Don’t let the mighty man glory in his might. Don’t let the rich man glory in his riches. But let him who glories glory in this, that he has understanding, and knows me, that I am Yahweh who exercises loving kindness, justice, and righteousness, in the earth; for I delight in these things,” says Yahweh.
plain: God says the wise, the strong and the rich should not boast of what they have. If anyone boasts, let it be in knowing God, who acts with kindness, justice and right, which he delights in.
core_idea: Boast only in knowing God, not wisdom, strength, wealth

text: Woe is me because of my injury! My wound is serious; but I said, “Truly this is my grief, and I must bear it.” My tent has been destroyed, and all my cords are broken. My children have gone away from me, and they are no more. There is no one to spread my tent any more, to set up my curtains.
note: Bearing grief and loss of home and family

situations: loss of a home or something valued
keywords: this is my grief, and I must bear it
tags.when_helps: Someone whose home and family have been torn away and who is learning to carry a grief that will not lift.

display_text: Woe is me because of my injury! My wound is serious; but I said, “Truly this is my grief, and I must bear it.” My tent has been destroyed, and all my cords are broken. My children have gone away from me, and they are no more. There is no one to spread my tent any more, to set up my curtains.
plain: My wound is grave, but I said, "This is my grief, and I must carry it." My home is torn down, my children are gone, and there is no one left to help me rebuild.
core_idea: Accepting a grief that must be carried

text: Yahweh, I know that the way of man is not in himself. It is not in man who walks to direct his steps. Yahweh, correct me, but gently; not in your anger, lest you reduce me to nothing.
note: Not being in control; asking for gentleness

tags.when_helps: A believer aware they cannot steer their own life well, who asks for correction but fears being crushed by it.

display_text: Yahweh, I know that the way of man is not in himself. It is not in man who walks to direct his steps. Yahweh, correct me, but gently; not in your anger, lest you reduce me to nothing.
plain: Lord, I know people cannot steer their own lives. Correct me, God, but gently, not in anger, or you will crush me to nothing.
core_idea: We cannot direct our steps; correct me gently

text: You are righteous, Yahweh, when I contend with you; yet I would like to reason the cause with you. Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why are they all at ease who deal very treacherously? You have planted them. Yes, they have taken root. They grow. Yes, they produce fruit. You are near in their mouth, and far from their heart.
note: Unfairness: why do wrongdoers thrive?

tags.when_helps: A believer troubled that dishonest people seem to thrive, who wants permission to argue honestly with God.

display_text: You are righteous, Yahweh, when I contend with you; yet I would like to reason the cause with you. Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why are they all at ease who deal very treacherously? You have planted them. Yes, they have taken root. They grow. Yes, they produce fruit. You are near in their mouth, and far from their heart.
plain: God, you are just, yet let me ask why the wicked prosper and traitors live at ease. You planted them and they flourish; they speak of you, but their hearts are far from you.
core_idea: Why do the wicked prosper?

text: “If you have run with the footmen, and they have wearied you, then how can you contend with horses? Though in a land of peace you are secure, yet how will you do in the pride of the Jordan?
note: Worn out by small trials, facing bigger ones

keywords: run with footmen, contend with horses
tags.when_helps: Someone worn out by small troubles who needs a bracing reminder that harder tests may come and strength must grow.

display_text: If you have run with the footmen, and they have wearied you, then how can you contend with horses? Though in a land of peace you are secure, yet how will you do in the pride of the Jordan?
plain: If racing men on foot has worn you out, how will you race horses? If you only feel safe in peaceful country, how will you cope in the wild Jordan thickets?
core_idea: If small trials tire you, harder ones await

text: Woe is me, my mother, that you have borne me, a man of strife, and a man of contention to the whole earth! I have not lent, neither have men lent to me; yet every one of them curses me.
note: Feeling hated and at odds with everyone

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels everyone is against them despite doing no harm and wishes they had never been born into such strife.

display_text: Woe is me, my mother, that you have borne me, a man of strife, and a man of contention to the whole earth! I have not lent, neither have men lent to me; yet every one of them curses me.
plain: I wish I had never been born, Mother: everyone fights with me. I have neither lent nor borrowed, yet everyone curses me.
core_idea: Cursed by all though I have wronged no one

text: Your words were found, and I ate them. Your words were to me a joy and the rejoicing of my heart, for I am called by your name, Yahweh, God of Armies. I didn’t sit in the assembly of those who make merry and rejoice. I sat alone because of your hand, for you have filled me with indignation. Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuses to be healed? Will you indeed be to me as a deceitful brook, like waters that fail?
note: Loneliness and unending pain despite faith

tags.when_helps: A believer who once delighted in faith but now feels isolated and wonders why their pain never heals.

display_text: Your words were found, and I ate them. Your words were to me a joy and the rejoicing of my heart, for I am called by your name, Yahweh, God of Armies. I didn’t sit in the assembly of those who make merry and rejoice. I sat alone because of your hand, for you have filled me with indignation. Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuses to be healed? Will you indeed be to me as a deceitful brook, like waters that fail?
plain: Your words were my joy, and because of you I sat alone, apart from the merrymakers. Why does my pain never end, and will you fail me like a stream that runs dry?
core_idea: Joy in God's word, yet lonely unending pain

plain_judge.issue: Drops "filled me with indignation" and being called by God's name.

text: Yahweh says: “Cursed is the man who trusts in man, relies on strength of flesh, and whose heart departs from Yahweh. For he will be like a bush in the desert, and will not see when good comes, but will inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, an uninhabited salt land. “Blessed is the man who trusts in Yahweh, and whose confidence is in Yahweh. For he will be as a tree planted by the waters, who spreads out its roots by the river, and will not fear when heat comes, but its leaf will be green; and will not be concerned in the year of drought. It won’t cease from yielding fruit.
note: Where to put trust; steadiness in hard times

tags.when_helps: A believer anxious about hard times ahead who needs the image of a deeply rooted tree that does not fear drought.

display_text: Yahweh says: “Cursed is the man who trusts in man, relies on strength of flesh, and whose heart departs from Yahweh. For he will be like a bush in the desert, and will not see when good comes, but will inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, an uninhabited salt land. “Blessed is the man who trusts in Yahweh, and whose confidence is in Yahweh. For he will be as a tree planted by the waters, who spreads out its roots by the river, and will not fear when heat comes, but its leaf will be green; and will not be concerned in the year of drought. It won’t cease from yielding fruit.
plain: God says those who trust in people and turn from him are like a desert shrub that never sees good. Those who trust God are like a tree by a river: unafraid of heat, green, fruitful even in drought.
core_idea: Trust God and flourish like a well-watered tree

plain_judge.issue: Drops "cursed" and "blessed", softening the hard saying into a comparison.

text: The heart is deceitful above all things and it is exceedingly corrupt. Who can know it?
note: Self-deception and not knowing one's own heart

tags.when_helps: Someone shaken to discover they cannot trust their own motives and wondering how well they know themselves.

display_text: The heart is deceitful above all things and it is exceedingly corrupt. Who can know it?
plain: The human heart is more deceptive than anything, and deeply sick. Who can understand it?
core_idea: The human heart deceives and cannot be fathomed

text: As the partridge that sits on eggs which she has not laid, so is he who gets riches, and not by right. In the middle of his days, they will leave him. At his end, he will be a fool.
note: Wealth gained dishonestly does not last

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to get ahead dishonestly, or envying those who did, who needs to see how such gains end.

display_text: As the partridge that sits on eggs which she has not laid, so is he who gets riches, and not by right. In the middle of his days, they will leave him. At his end, he will be a fool.
plain: Someone who gets rich unjustly is like a partridge sitting on eggs it did not lay. The riches will leave him halfway through life, and at the end he will be shown a fool.
core_idea: Wealth gained wrongly is lost; the gainer proves a fool

text: Heal me, O Yahweh, and I will be healed. Save me, and I will be saved; for you are my praise.
note: Prayer for healing

keywords: heal me and I will be healed
tags.when_helps: A believer who needs healing in body or spirit and wants simple words to ask God for it.

display_text: Heal me, O Yahweh, and I will be healed. Save me, and I will be saved; for you are my praise.
plain: Heal me, Lord, and I will be healed. Save me, and I will be saved, because you are the one I praise.
core_idea: Only God's healing truly heals

text: Then I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was making something on the wheels. When the vessel that he made of the clay was marred in the hand of the potter, he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it. Then Yahweh’s word came to me, saying, “House of Israel, can’t I do with you as this potter?” says Yahweh. “Behold, as the clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.
note: Being remade after something goes wrong

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone who feels spoiled or ruined by failure and needs the image of a potter remaking the same clay into something new.

display_text: Then I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was making something on the wheels. When the vessel that he made of the clay was marred in the hand of the potter, he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it. Then Yahweh’s word came to me, saying, “House of Israel, can’t I do with you as this potter?” says Yahweh. “Behold, as the clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.
plain: At the potter's house I watched a pot go wrong in his hands, so he reshaped it into another, as he saw fit. God then says Israel is like that clay in his hands.
core_idea: God can reshape us as a potter reshapes clay

text: Yahweh, you have persuaded me, and I was persuaded. You are stronger than I, and have prevailed. I have become a laughing-stock all day. Everyone mocks me. For as often as I speak, I cry out; I cry, “Violence and destruction!” because Yahweh’s word has been made a reproach to me, and a derision, all day. If I say, I will not make mention of him, or speak any more in his name, then there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I am weary with holding it in, and I can’t.
note: Mocked for a calling one cannot abandon

keywords: fire shut up in my bones
tags.when_helps: Someone mocked for speaking an unwelcome truth who wants to stop but cannot keep the conviction inside.

display_text: Yahweh, you have persuaded me, and I was persuaded. You are stronger than I, and have prevailed. I have become a laughing-stock all day. Everyone mocks me. For as often as I speak, I cry out; I cry, “Violence and destruction!” because Yahweh’s word has been made a reproach to me, and a derision, all day. If I say, I will not make mention of him, or speak any more in his name, then there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I am weary with holding it in, and I can’t.
plain: Lord, you persuaded me and overpowered me, and now everyone mocks me for your message. Yet if I try to stop speaking, it burns like fire in my bones and I cannot hold it in.
core_idea: God's word burns within and cannot be held in

text: Why did I come out of the womb to see labor and sorrow, that my days should be consumed with shame?
note: Despair and shame over one's life

keywords: why did I come out of the womb
tags.when_helps: Someone weighed down by toil and shame who wonders why they were born and needs to know even prophets felt this.

display_text: Why did I come out of the womb to see labor and sorrow, that my days should be consumed with shame?
plain: Why was I ever born, only to see trouble and sorrow, and spend my days in shame?
core_idea: Why was I born to sorrow and shame?

text: “Should you reign, because you strive to excel in cedar? Didn’t your father eat and drink, and do justice and righteousness? Then it was well with him. He judged the cause of the poor and needy; so it was well, then. Wasn’t this to know me?” says Yahweh.
note: Status and display versus a just, simple life

tags.when_helps: Someone chasing status and luxury who needs reminding that a good life rests on justice and care for those in need.

display_text: “Should you reign, because you strive to excel in cedar? Didn’t your father eat and drink, and do justice and righteousness? Then it was well with him. He judged the cause of the poor and needy; so it was well, then. Wasn’t this to know me?” says Yahweh.
plain: God asks the king: does building with fine cedar make you a king? Your father ate and drank, yet did what was just and fair, and defended the poor and needy; that is what knowing God means.
core_idea: Knowing God means doing justice for the poor

text: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future. You shall call on me, and you shall go and pray to me, and I will listen to you. You shall seek me, and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.
note: Hope for the future; seeking God wholeheartedly

keywords: seek me with all your heart
tags.when_helps: A believer anxious about the future who needs assurance that God intends good for them and will hear their prayer.

display_text: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future. You shall call on me, and you shall go and pray to me, and I will listen to you. You shall seek me, and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.
plain: God says his plans for you are for peace, not harm, to give you hope and a future. Call and pray and he will listen; seek him with all your heart and you will find him.
core_idea: God plans hope for you; seek him and find

text: Yahweh appeared of old to me, saying, “Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love. Therefore I have drawn you with loving kindness.
note: Feeling unloved; assurance of lasting love

tags.when_helps: A believer who doubts they are loved and needs to hear that God's love for them is lasting.

display_text: Yahweh appeared of old to me, saying, “Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love. Therefore I have drawn you with loving kindness.
plain: God appeared to me long ago and said, "I have loved you with a love that lasts forever, so I have drawn you to me with kindness."
core_idea: God loves you with an everlasting love

text: Yahweh says: “A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping, Rachel weeping for her children. She refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.” Yahweh says: “Refrain your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears; for your work will be rewarded,” says Yahweh. “They will come again from the land of the enemy. There is hope for your latter end,” says Yahweh. “Your children will come again to their own territory.
note: Inconsolable grief for children; hope beyond mourning

tags.when_helps: A parent inconsolable over children lost or taken away who needs both their grief honoured and a promise of hope.

display_text: Yahweh says: “A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping, Rachel weeping for her children. She refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.” Yahweh says: “Refrain your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears; for your work will be rewarded,” says Yahweh. “They will come again from the land of the enemy. There is hope for your latter end,” says Yahweh. “Your children will come again to their own territory.
plain: God says a cry is heard: Rachel weeping for her children, refusing comfort, because they are gone. Then God tells her to stop weeping; her work will be rewarded, there is hope, and her children will come home.
core_idea: Weeping mother told her children will return

text: For I have satiated the weary soul, and I have replenished every sorrowful soul.”
note: Weariness and sorrow; being replenished

tags.when_helps: A believer worn out and sorrowful who needs a short promise that their weariness will be restored.

display_text: For I have satiated the weary soul, and I have replenished every sorrowful soul.
plain: God says: I have given the weary soul its fill, and refreshed everyone who is sorrowful.
core_idea: God refreshes the weary and the sorrowful

text: “Behold, I am Yahweh, the God of all flesh. Is there anything too hard for me?
note: Facing an impossible situation; nothing is beyond hope

tags.when_helps: A believer facing something that seems impossible who needs reminding that nothing is too hard for God.

display_text: Behold, I am Yahweh, the God of all flesh. Is there anything too hard for me?
plain: God says: I am the Lord, the God of every living being. Is anything too hard for me?
core_idea: Nothing is too hard for God

text: ‘Call to me, and I will answer you, and will show you great and difficult things, which you don’t know.’
note: Uncertainty; turning to prayer for understanding

keywords: call to me and I will answer
tags.when_helps: A believer searching for answers they cannot find alone who wants encouragement to pray and ask.

display_text: ‘Call to me, and I will answer you, and will show you great and difficult things, which you don’t know.’
plain: God says: call to me and I will answer, and show you great, hidden things you do not know.
core_idea: Call to God and he will answer

text: ‘You said, “Woe is me now! For Yahweh has added sorrow to my pain! I am weary with my groaning, and I find no rest.”’
note: Exhaustion and sorrow piling on pain; no rest

tags.when_helps: Someone for whom one sorrow has piled on another, who is weary and restless and needs that weariness named.

display_text: ‘You said, “Woe is me now! For Yahweh has added sorrow to my pain! I am weary with my groaning, and I find no rest.”’
plain: God repeats Baruch's complaint that God has added sorrow to his pain, and that he is worn out with groaning and finds no rest.
core_idea: Worn out by sorrow and finding no rest

text: Leave your fatherless children. I will preserve them alive. Let your widows trust in me.”
note: Worry for loved ones left behind; trust

tags.when_helps: A believing parent or spouse worried about who will care for their family if they are gone.

display_text: Leave your fatherless children. I will preserve them alive. Let your widows trust in me.
plain: God says: leave your orphaned children with me; I will keep them alive. Let your widows trust in me.
core_idea: God will care for orphans and widows

text: My people have been lost sheep. Their shepherds have caused them to go astray. They have turned them away on the mountains. They have gone from mountain to hill. They have forgotten their resting place.
note: Feeling lost, misled, restless; forgetting where one belongs

tags.when_helps: Someone led astray by others and wandering from place to place who has forgotten where they find rest.

display_text: My people have been lost sheep. Their shepherds have caused them to go astray. They have turned them away on the mountains. They have gone from mountain to hill. They have forgotten their resting place.
plain: My people have been like lost sheep. Their shepherds led them astray and sent them wandering over the hills, until they forgot where their place of rest was.
core_idea: Misled people lost and far from their rest

text: Don’t let your heart faint. Don’t fear for the news that will be heard in the land. For news will come one year, and after that in another year news will come, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler.
note: Anxiety over troubling news and unrest

tags.when_helps: Someone frightened by alarming news who needs reminding that news comes and goes and the heart need not faint.

display_text: Don’t let your heart faint. Don’t fear for the news that will be heard in the land. For news will come one year, and after that in another year news will come, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler.
plain: Don't lose heart or be afraid of the news you hear. One year brings one report, the next year another, with violence and rulers fighting each other.
core_idea: Don't lose heart at alarming news

text: “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return there. Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away. Blessed be Yahweh’s name.”
note: accepting sudden loss

situations: loss of a home or something valued
keywords: the Lord gave and has taken away
tags.when_helps: A believer who has lost much and seeks a way to accept it without losing faith.

display_text: “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return there. Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away. Blessed be Yahweh’s name.”
plain: Job says he was born with nothing and will die with nothing. The Lord gave and the Lord has taken away, and may the Lord's name be blessed.
core_idea: God gives and takes away; bless him still

text: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him. When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky. So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.
note: sitting silently with a grieving friend

tags.when_helps: Someone wondering how to be with a grieving friend, or in grief and needing silent company.

display_text: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him. When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky. plain: When Job's three friends heard of his disaster, they came to comfort him. Seeing him unrecognisable, they wept, tore their robes and sat on the ground with him seven days and nights, silent, because his grief was so great.
core_idea: Friends sat silently with Job in his grief

text: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul, Who long for death, but it doesn’t come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures, who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave? Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in? For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water. For the thing which I fear comes on me, That which I am afraid of comes to me. I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; but trouble comes.”
note: despair, misery, feared things coming true

tags.safety_reason: Describes the miserable as longing for death and rejoicing to find the grave, presenting death as something to long for.
tags.when_helps: Someone in deep misery who needs to know that even this anguish has been voiced in sacred writing.

display_text: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul, Who long for death, but it doesn’t come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures, who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave? Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in? For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water. For the thing which I fear comes on me, That which I am afraid of comes to me. I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; but trouble comes.”
plain: Job asks why people in misery are kept alive, longing for a death that does not come. His groans pour out like water; what he feared has happened, and he has no ease, no quiet, no rest.
core_idea: Why is life given to those in misery?

plain_judge.issue: Drops "whom God has hedged in" and the gladness at finding the grave.

text: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands. Your words have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees. But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.
note: the helper who now needs help

situations: caring for a sick or ageing relative
keywords: now it has come to you
tags.when_helps: A helper who always strengthened others and now finds themselves faltering when trouble arrives.

display_text: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands. Your words have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees. But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.
plain: Job's friend says: you have taught many and strengthened weak, stumbling people with your words. But now trouble has come to you, and you lose heart and are shaken.
core_idea: The comforter falters when trouble reaches him

text: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.
note: resentment and jealousy destroy

tags.when_helps: Someone nursing resentment or jealousy who needs a sharp warning about what it does to them.

display_text: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.
plain: Resentment kills the fool, and jealousy kills the naive.
core_idea: Resentment and jealousy destroy the foolish

text: For affliction doesn’t come out of the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground; but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
note: trouble is part of being human

tags.when_helps: Someone asking why trouble came to them who may find comfort in its being part of every life.

display_text: For affliction doesn’t come out of the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground; but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
plain: Trouble doesn't sprout from the soil like a weed; people are born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
core_idea: Trouble is part of being human

text: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient? Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass? Isn’t it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?
note: exhaustion, patience run out

tags.when_helps: Someone told to be patient who feels they have no strength left to wait.

display_text: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient? Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass? Isn’t it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?
plain: Job asks what strength or future he has to make waiting worthwhile, since he is not made of stone or bronze. He has no help left in him, and good sense has been driven away.
core_idea: Too exhausted to wait any longer

text: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
note: friends owe kindness to the faltering

tags.when_helps: Someone near collapse, even losing faith, who needs to know they deserve a friend's kindness.

display_text: To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
plain: Someone who is about to collapse should be shown kindness by his friend, even if he has stopped fearing God.
core_idea: A friend owes kindness to one who is collapsing

text: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand? As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages, so am I made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me. When I lie down, I say, ‘When shall I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.
note: weary toil and sleepless nights

tags.when_helps: Someone enduring months of misery and sleepless nights who needs to hear it voiced.

display_text: Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand? As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages, so am I made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me. When I lie down, I say, ‘When shall I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.
plain: Job says human life is forced labour, like a hired worker's. He has been given months of misery and weary nights; lying down, he longs for morning and tosses and turns until dawn.
core_idea: Months of misery and sleepless nights

text: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope. Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye shall no more see good.
note: life passing quickly, hopelessness

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels their days are slipping by without hope and needs that feeling named.

display_text: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope. Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye shall no more see good.
plain: Job says his days fly faster than a weaver's shuttle and pass without hope. He asks God to remember that his life is only a breath; he will never see good again.
core_idea: Life is a breath passing without hope

text: “Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of their fathers. (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.) Shall they not teach you, tell you, and utter words out of their heart?
note: learning from those who came before

tags.when_helps: Someone unsure what to do who could learn from the wisdom of those who came before.

display_text: Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of their fathers. (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.) Shall they not teach you, tell you, and utter words out of their heart?
plain: Ask the generations before us and learn what their ancestors discovered, for we are newcomers who know nothing and our days are a shadow. Won't they teach you from their hearts?
core_idea: Learn from the wisdom of past generations

text: “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away, they see no good. They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey. If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;’ I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that you will not hold me innocent. I shall be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?
note: unable to just cheer up

tags.when_helps: Someone who has tried to cheer up and cannot, needing to know that struggle is understood.

display_text: Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away, they see no good. They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey. If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;’ I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that you will not hold me innocent. I shall be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?
plain: Job says his days race by without good. If he tries to forget his complaint and cheer up, he still dreads his sorrows; he knows God won't clear him, so why struggle in vain?
core_idea: Trying to cheer up while dreading one's sorrows

text: “My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
note: weariness and the need to speak bitterness

keywords: give free course to my complaint
tags.when_helps: Someone weary of life who needs permission to speak their bitterness out loud.

display_text: My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
plain: Job says: I am sick of my life. I will let my complaint pour out and speak from the bitterness of my soul.
core_idea: Weary of life, speaking out of bitterness

text: Surely then you shall lift up your face without spot; Yes, you shall be steadfast, and shall not fear: for you shall forget your misery. You shall remember it like waters that have passed away. Life shall be clearer than the noonday. Though there is darkness, it shall be as the morning. You shall be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you shall search, and shall take your rest in safety.
note: misery passing, hope returning

keywords: like waters that have passed away
tags.when_helps: Someone in a long dark stretch who needs to imagine their misery remembered later like passed water.

display_text: Surely then you shall lift up your face without spot; Yes, you shall be steadfast, and shall not fear: for you shall forget your misery. You shall remember it like waters that have passed away. Life shall be clearer than the noonday. Though there is darkness, it shall be as the morning. You shall be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you shall search, and shall take your rest in safety.
plain: Job's friend promises he will lift his face without shame and stand firm without fear. He will forget his misery like water that has flowed past; darkness will become morning, and hope will make him secure.
core_idea: Misery will pass like water; hope brings safety

text: In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune. It is ready for them whose foot slips.
note: the comfortable looking down on the struggling

tags.when_helps: Someone in trouble judged by comfortable people, or comfortable and quick to judge.

display_text: In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune. It is ready for them whose foot slips.
plain: Those who are comfortable look down on people who suffer misfortune; they think disaster is meant for those already slipping.
core_idea: The comfortable scorn those who suffer

text: “But ask the animals, now, and they shall teach you; the birds of the sky, and they shall tell you. Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you. The fish of the sea shall declare to you.
note: learning from nature

tags.when_helps: Someone seeking answers who might learn by looking at the natural world.

display_text: But ask the animals, now, and they shall teach you; the birds of the sky, and they shall tell you. Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you. The fish of the sea shall declare to you.
plain: Ask the animals and they will teach you; ask the birds and they will tell you. Speak to the earth and it will teach you, and the fish of the sea will explain.
core_idea: Creation itself teaches, if you ask

text: Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.
note: when silence is wiser than advice

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tired of unhelpful advice, or tempted to give it, reminded that silence can be wiser.

display_text: Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.
plain: If only you would keep completely quiet! That would be wisdom.
core_idea: Silence would be wiser than your words

text: “Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble. He grows up like a flower, and is cut down. He also flees like a shadow, and doesn’t continue.
note: the brevity and trouble of human life

keywords: few days and full of trouble
tags.when_helps: Someone confronting how brief and troubled human life is.

display_text: Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble. He grows up like a flower, and is cut down. He also flees like a shadow, and doesn’t continue.
plain: A human being lives only a few days, full of trouble. He blooms like a flower and is cut down; he slips away like a shadow and does not last.
core_idea: Human life is short and full of trouble

text: “For there is hope for a tree, If it is cut down, that it will sprout again, that the tender branch of it will not cease. Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stock dies in the ground, yet through the scent of water it will bud, and sprout boughs like a plant.
note: renewal after being cut down

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone who feels cut down to the stump and needs the image of new growth.

display_text: For there is hope for a tree, If it is cut down, that it will sprout again, that the tender branch of it will not cease. Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stock dies in the ground, yet through the scent of water it will bud, and sprout boughs like a plant.
plain: There is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again. Even if its root grows old and its stump dies, at the scent of water it will bud and put out new shoots.
core_idea: A cut-down tree can sprout again

text: “I have heard many such things. You are all miserable comforters! Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer? I also could speak as you do. If your soul were in my soul’s place, I could join words together against you, and shake my head at you, but I would strengthen you with my mouth. The solace of my lips would relieve you. “Though I speak, my grief is not subsided. Though I forbear, what am I eased?
note: unhelpful comfort; grief that talking doesn't ease

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone in grief worn down by well-meant but empty words from friends.

display_text: “I have heard many such things. You are all miserable comforters! Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer? I also could speak as you do. If your soul were in my soul’s place, I could join words together against you, and shake my head at you, but I would strengthen you with my mouth. plain: Job calls his friends miserable comforters full of empty words; in their place he would strengthen them, not lecture. Yet whether he speaks or keeps silent, his grief does not ease.
core_idea: Miserable comforters; grief that will not ease

text: Yet shall the righteous hold on his way. He who has clean hands shall grow stronger and stronger.

tags.when_helps: Someone holding to integrity through hardship who needs to hear it makes them stronger.

display_text: Yet shall the righteous hold on his way. He who has clean hands shall grow stronger and stronger.
plain: Even so, the righteous keep to their path, and those with clean hands grow stronger and stronger.
core_idea: The righteous hold on and grow stronger

text: My days are past, my plans are broken off, as are the thoughts of my heart.
note: broken plans, life derailed

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone whose plans and hopes have all broken off at once, needing the feeling named.

display_text: My days are past, my plans are broken off, as are the thoughts of my heart.
plain: My days are over, my plans broken off, and so are the hopes of my heart.
core_idea: My days are over and my plans broken

text: My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me.

tags.when_helps: Someone whose family and friends have drifted away in hard times.

display_text: My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me.
