text: All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me. My bones stick to my skin and to my flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth. “Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends; for the hand of God has touched me.
note: rejected by loved ones, pleading for pity

tags.when_helps: Someone ill or suffering who has been abandoned by those they loved and is pleading for pity.

display_text: All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me. My bones stick to my skin and to my flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth. “Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends; for the hand of God has touched me.

core_idea: Abandoned by friends, begging for pity

text: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.
note: hope held onto in suffering

tags.when_helps: A believer at a low point who wants to hold on to faith in eventual vindication.

display_text: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.
plain: Job says: I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end he will stand upon the earth.
core_idea: My Redeemer lives and will stand at last

text: “Why do the wicked live, become old, yes, and grow mighty in power? Their child is established with them in their sight, their offspring before their eyes. Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.
note: unfairness: why wrongdoers prosper

tags.when_helps: Someone galled that wrongdoers seem to thrive while they suffer.

display_text: Why do the wicked live, become old, yes, and grow mighty in power? Their child is established with them in their sight, their offspring before their eyes. Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.
plain: Why do wicked people live long and grow powerful? Their children thrive around them, their homes are safe from fear, and God does not punish them.
core_idea: Why do the wicked live safe and prosper?

text: One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet. His pails are full of milk. The marrow of his bones is moistened. Another dies in bitterness of soul, and never tastes of good. They lie down alike in the dust. The worm covers them.
note: death levels fortunate and unfortunate alike

keywords: they lie down alike in the dust
tags.when_helps: Someone troubled by life's unfairness who finds a strange levelling in shared mortality.

display_text: One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet. His pails are full of milk. The marrow of his bones is moistened. Another dies in bitterness of soul, and never tastes of good. They lie down alike in the dust. The worm covers them.
plain: One person dies strong, comfortable and well fed; another dies bitter, never having enjoyed good. Both lie down alike in the dust, covered by worms.
core_idea: Death levels the fortunate and the bitter alike

text: “If I go east, he is not there; if west, I can’t find him; He works to the north, but I can’t see him. He turns south, but I can’t catch a glimpse of him. But he knows the way that I take. When he has tried me, I shall come out like gold.
note: feeling God absent; trial refining

keywords: I shall come out like gold
tags.when_helps: A believer who cannot feel God anywhere yet trusts the trial will refine them.

display_text: If I go east, he is not there; if west, I can’t find him; He works to the north, but I can’t see him. He turns south, but I can’t catch a glimpse of him. But he knows the way that I take. When he has tried me, I shall come out like gold.
plain: Job says he looks east, west, north and south and cannot find God anywhere. But God knows the path he takes, and when God has tested him, he will come out like gold.
core_idea: God knows my way; testing will refine me

text: Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me. I hold fast to my righteousness, and will not let it go. My heart shall not reproach me so long as I live.
note: holding onto integrity under pressure

tags.when_helps: Someone pressured or accused who needs resolve to keep their integrity and a clear conscience.

display_text: Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me. I hold fast to my righteousness, and will not let it go. My heart shall not reproach me so long as I live.
plain: As long as I live I will not give up my integrity. I will hold on to doing right and never let it go; my conscience will not accuse me.
core_idea: Holding on to integrity until death

text: “But where shall wisdom be found? Where is the place of understanding? Man doesn’t know its price; Neither is it found in the land of the living. The deep says, ‘It isn’t in me.’ The sea says, ‘It isn’t with me.’ It can’t be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for its price. It can’t be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire. Gold and glass can’t equal it, neither shall it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold. No mention shall be made of coral or of crystal. Yes, the price of wisdom is above rubies.
note: wisdom worth more than wealth

tags.when_helps: Someone chasing wealth or answers who wonders where real understanding comes from and what it is worth.

display_text: But where shall wisdom be found? Where is the place of understanding? Man doesn’t know its price; Neither is it found in the land of the living. The deep says, ‘It isn’t in me.’ The sea says, ‘It isn’t with me.’ It can’t be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for its price. It can’t be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire. Gold and glass can’t equal it, neither shall it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold. plain: Where can wisdom be found? It is not in the deep or the sea, it cannot be bought with gold, silver or jewels, and it is worth more than rubies.
core_idea: Wisdom is priceless and cannot be bought

text: To man he said, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom. To depart from evil is understanding.’”
note: what wisdom really is

tags.when_helps: A believer seeking a simple definition of wisdom rooted in reverence and turning from wrong.

display_text: To man he said, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom. To depart from evil is understanding.’
plain: God told humankind: reverence for the Lord is wisdom, and turning away from evil is understanding.
core_idea: Revering God is wisdom; shunning evil, understanding

text: “Oh that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me; when his lamp shone on my head, and by his light I walked through darkness, as I was in the ripeness of my days, when the friendship of God was in my tent, when the Almighty was yet with me, and my children were around me, when my steps were washed with butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me, when I went out to the city gate, when I prepared my seat in the street.
note: longing for better days that are gone

situations: loss of a home or something valued
tags.when_helps: Someone aching for a former life when they felt blessed, close to God and surrounded by family.

display_text: Oh that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me; when his lamp shone on my head, and by his light I walked through darkness, as I was in the ripeness of my days, when the friendship of God was in my tent, when the Almighty was yet with me, and my children were around me, when my steps were washed with butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me, when I went out to the city gate, when I prepared my seat in the street.
plain: Job longs for the old days when God watched over him and lit his way through darkness, when God's friendship filled his home, his children were around him, life overflowed, and he was honoured in the city.
core_idea: Longing for past days of God's closeness

text: I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame. I was a father to the needy. The cause of him who I didn’t know, I searched out.
note: serving those in need

tags.when_helps: Someone wanting a picture of a life spent helping the vulnerable and championing strangers' causes.

display_text: I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame. I was a father to the needy. The cause of him who I didn’t know, I searched out.
plain: I was eyes for the blind and feet for the lame. I was a father to the poor, and I looked into the case of strangers.
core_idea: I served the blind, the lame, the poor

text: Didn’t I weep for him who was in trouble? Wasn’t my soul grieved for the needy? When I looked for good, then evil came; When I waited for light, there came darkness. My heart is troubled, and doesn’t rest. Days of affliction have come on me.
note: good done, yet hardship came anyway

tags.when_helps: A kind person who did right by others and still met hardship, troubled and unable to rest.

display_text: Didn’t I weep for him who was in trouble? Wasn’t my soul grieved for the needy? When I looked for good, then evil came; When I waited for light, there came darkness. My heart is troubled, and doesn’t rest. Days of affliction have come on me.
plain: Job wept for people in trouble and grieved for the poor, yet when he hoped for good, evil came, and when he waited for light, darkness came. His heart is restless, and days of suffering have arrived.
core_idea: I hoped for light, and darkness came

text: “I made a covenant with my eyes, how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?

display_text: I made a covenant with my eyes, how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?
plain: Job says he made a promise with his own eyes, so how could he look lustfully at a young woman?
core_idea: A covenant with my eyes against lust

tags.when_helps: A young person hesitant to speak among elders, reminded that understanding is not owned by age or rank.

display_text: I am young, and you are very old; Therefore I held back, and didn’t dare show you my opinion. plain: A young man says he held back from speaking to his elders, thinking age should teach wisdom. But understanding comes from God's breath in a person; greatness and age don't make someone wise or just.
core_idea: Wisdom comes from God's spirit, not age

text: “For has any said to God, ‘I am guilty, but I will not offend any more. Teach me that which I don’t see. If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more’?
note: admitting fault and resolving to change

keywords: teach me what I don't see
tags.when_helps: Someone who has done wrong and wants humbly to admit it, learn their blind spots and change.

display_text: For has any said to God, ‘I am guilty, but I will not offend any more. Teach me that which I don’t see. If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more’?
plain: Has anyone ever said to God that they are guilty and won't do wrong again, and asked to be taught what they cannot see?
core_idea: Admit guilt, ask to see, and stop doing wrong

text: But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night, who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?’
note: comfort and songs in dark times

tags.when_helps: A believer in a dark season who has forgotten to seek the God who gives songs in the night.

display_text: But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night, who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?’
plain: No one asks, "Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night and makes us wiser than the animals and birds?"
core_idea: God gives songs in the night, yet none seek him

text: Don’t let riches entice you to wrath, neither let the great size of a bribe turn you aside. Would your wealth sustain you in distress, or all the might of your strength?
note: wealth cannot save you in distress

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted by money or a bribe, asked whether wealth could really hold them up in distress.

display_text: Don’t let riches entice you to wrath, neither let the great size of a bribe turn you aside. Would your wealth sustain you in distress, or all the might of your strength?
plain: Don't let wealth lure you into anger or a big bribe lead you astray. Would your riches or all your strength keep you safe when trouble comes?
core_idea: Wealth and strength won't save you in distress

text: Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
note: pausing to notice wonder

tags.when_helps: Someone rushing or overwhelmed who needs to pause and take in the wonder around them.

display_text: Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
plain: Stop, and think about the wonderful works of God.
core_idea: Pause and consider God's wondrous works

text: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding. Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it? Whereupon were its foundations fastened? Or who laid its cornerstone, when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
note: perspective and humility before the vastness of creation

tags.when_helps: Someone demanding answers from life or God, invited to see their questions against the vastness of creation.

display_text: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding. Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it? Whereupon were its foundations fastened? Or who laid its cornerstone, when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
plain: God asks Job where he was when the earth's foundations were laid, and tells him to answer if he understands. Who set its measurements and its cornerstone, while the morning stars sang and the angels shouted for joy?
core_idea: Where were you when God made the earth?

text: “Behold, I am of small account. What shall I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth. I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”
note: humility, knowing when to stop arguing

tags.when_helps: Someone realising they have said too much and choosing humble silence.

display_text: “Behold, I am of small account. What shall I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth. I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”
plain: Job answers God that he is insignificant and has nothing to say, and puts his hand over his mouth. He has spoken once, even twice, and will say no more.
core_idea: Humbled before God, I fall silent

text: “Yet even now,” says Yahweh, “turn to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning.” Tear your heart, and not your garments, and turn to Yahweh, your God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and relents from sending calamity.
note: Guilt and regret; sincere change of heart, not show

keywords: tear your heart, not your garments
tags.when_helps: A believer full of remorse who needs to know sincere return is met with grace, not outward show.

display_text: “Yet even now,” says Yahweh, “turn to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning.” Tear your heart, and not your garments, and turn to Yahweh, your God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and relents from sending calamity.
plain: God says: even now, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning. Tear your hearts, not your clothes, and return to God, who is gracious, merciful, slow to anger and full of love.
core_idea: Return to God with a torn heart

text: I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten, the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my great army, which I sent among you.
note: Hope of restoring lost, wasted years

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone mourning wasted or lost years who needs hope that what was lost can be restored.

display_text: I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten, the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my great army, which I sent among you.
plain: God says: I will repay you for the years the locusts ate, the swarms I sent among you.
core_idea: God will restore the years that were lost

text: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it.
note: Hope in dark times

tags.when_helps: Someone in a dark season who needs to hear that the darkness has not overcome the light.

display_text: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it.
plain: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
core_idea: Darkness cannot overcome the light

text: The wind blows where it wants to, and you hear its sound, but don’t know where it comes from and where it is going. So is everyone who is born of the Spirit.”
note: Spiritual renewal; freedom beyond our control

keywords: the wind blows where it wants
tags.when_helps: Someone who cannot predict where life is taking them and wonders if that can be a kind of freedom.

display_text: The wind blows where it wants to, and you hear its sound, but don’t know where it comes from and where it is going. So is everyone who is born of the Spirit.
plain: The wind blows where it wants; you hear it but don't know where it comes from or goes. That is how it is with everyone born of the Spirit.
core_idea: Those born of the Spirit are like the wind

text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life. For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.
note: Being loved rather than condemned

tags.when_helps: A believer afraid of judgement who needs to hear that the aim is saving, not condemning.

display_text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life. For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.
plain: God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, so that whoever believes in him will not perish but have eternal life. God sent him not to condemn the world but to save it.
core_idea: God gave his Son to save the world

text: For everyone who does evil hates the light, and doesn’t come to the light, lest his works would be exposed. But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his works may be revealed, that they have been done in God.”
note: Hiding wrongdoing versus living openly

tags.when_helps: Someone hiding a wrong who is weighing whether to bring it into the open.

display_text: For everyone who does evil hates the light, and doesn’t come to the light, lest his works would be exposed. But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his works may be revealed, that they have been done in God.
plain: Everyone who does evil hates the light and avoids it, so their deeds won't be exposed. But whoever lives by the truth comes into the light, so it is clear their deeds were done in God.
core_idea: Evil hides from light; truth comes into it

text: Jesus answered her, “Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again, but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”
note: Restless longing that nothing satisfies

tags.when_helps: Someone who keeps chasing satisfactions that leave them thirsty again, longing for something lasting.

display_text: Jesus answered her, “Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again, but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”
plain: Jesus tells her that whoever drinks this water will be thirsty again, but whoever drinks the water he gives will never thirst; it becomes in them a spring welling up to eternal life.
core_idea: Jesus offers water that ends all thirst

text: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”
note: Sincere inner devotion over outward place or form

tags.when_helps: A believer tired of empty ritual who seeks worship that is sincere and inward.

display_text: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.
plain: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and in truth.
core_idea: Worship God in spirit and truth

text: For in this the saying is true, ‘One sows, and another reaps.’ I sent you to reap that for which you haven’t labored. Others have labored, and you have entered into their labor.”
note: Gratitude for others' work; work whose fruit others see

tags.when_helps: Someone whose labour others will harvest, or who reaps what others sowed, reflecting on shared work.

display_text: For in this the saying is true, ‘One sows, and another reaps.’ I sent you to reap that for which you haven’t labored. Others have labored, and you have entered into their labor.
plain: The saying is true: one person sows and another reaps. I sent you to harvest what you did not work for; others did the labour, and you have benefited from it.
core_idea: We reap what others have sown

text: A certain man was there, who had been sick for thirty-eight years. When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he had been sick for a long time, he asked him, “Do you want to be made well?” The sick man answered him, “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up, but while I’m coming, another steps down before me.” Jesus said to him, “Arise, take up your mat, and walk.” Immediately, the man was made well, and took up his mat and walked.
note: Feeling stuck for years with no one to help

keywords: do you want to be made well
tags.when_helps: Someone long stuck in illness or circumstance with no one to help, asked whether they are ready to rise.

display_text: A certain man was there, who had been sick for thirty-eight years. plain: Jesus asked a man ill for thirty-eight years if he wanted to be well; the man said no one would help him into the pool. Jesus told him to take his mat and walk, and he was healed at once.
core_idea: Do you want to be made well?

text: How can you believe, who receive glory from one another, and you don’t seek the glory that comes from the only God?
note: Seeking approval from other people

tags.when_helps: Someone hungry for others' approval who is challenged to seek a deeper source of worth.

display_text: How can you believe, who receive glory from one another, and you don’t seek the glory that comes from the only God?
plain: How can you believe, when you seek praise from one another and not the honour that comes from the only God?
core_idea: Seeking human praise blocks faith in God

text: He who comes to me I will in no way throw out.
note: Fear of rejection; being welcomed

tags.when_helps: Someone afraid of rejection who needs assurance that they will be received, not turned away.

display_text: He who comes to me I will in no way throw out.
plain: Jesus says: whoever comes to me I will never turn away.
core_idea: Jesus turns no one away

text: Don’t judge according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.”
note: Judging others by appearances

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to judge by surface, or judged that way, reminded to look deeper.

display_text: Don’t judge according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.
plain: Don't judge by appearances; judge fairly.
core_idea: Judge rightly, not by appearances

text: The scribes and the Pharisees brought a woman taken in adultery. Having set her in the middle, they told him, “Teacher, we found this woman in adultery, in the very act. Now in our law, Moses commanded us to stone such women. What then do you say about her?” They said this testing him, that they might have something to accuse him of. But Jesus stooped down, and wrote on the ground with his finger. But when they continued asking him, he looked up and said to them, “He who is without sin among you, let him throw the first stone at her.” Again he stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground. They, when they heard it, being convicted by their conscience, went out one by one, beginning from the oldest, even to the last. Jesus was left alone with the woman where she was, in the middle. Jesus, standing up, saw her and said, “Woman, where are your accusers? Did no one condemn you?” She said, “No one, Lord.” Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way. From now on, sin no more.”
note: Public shame, judgment and a fresh start

tags.when_helps: Someone publicly shamed for a wrong, or tempted to condemn another, who needs mercy and a fresh start.

display_text: The scribes and the Pharisees brought a woman taken in adultery. Having set her in the middle, they told him, “Teacher, we found this woman in adultery, in the very act. But Jesus stooped down, and wrote on the ground with his finger. plain: Leaders brought Jesus a woman caught in adultery, and he told them whoever was without sin should throw the first stone, so they all left. He told her he did not condemn her, and to go and sin no more.
core_idea: Let the sinless throw the first stone

text: You will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.”
note: Honesty and facing the truth

keywords: the truth will make you free
tags.when_helps: Someone afraid of facing or telling the truth who needs reminding that truth frees.

display_text: You will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.
plain: You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.
core_idea: The truth will set you free

text: As he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth. His disciples asked him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?” Jesus answered, “Neither did this man sin, nor his parents; but, that the works of God might be revealed in him.
note: Suffering is not punishment; blaming yourself or family

tags.when_helps: Someone, or a parent, wondering whether an illness or disability is punishment for wrongdoing.

display_text: As he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth. His disciples asked him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?” Jesus answered, “Neither did this man sin, nor his parents; but, that the works of God might be revealed in him.
plain: Seeing a man blind from birth, the disciples asked whose sin caused it, his or his parents'. Jesus said neither sinned; it happened so that God's works could be shown in him.
core_idea: Suffering is not always punishment for sin

text: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. He who is a hired hand, and not a shepherd, who doesn’t own the sheep, sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep, and flees. The wolf snatches the sheep, and scatters them. The hired hand flees because he is a hired hand, and doesn’t care for the sheep.
note: True care versus duty; staying when it's hard

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels exposed and abandoned and wants the assurance of one who cares and will not flee.

display_text: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. He who is a hired hand, and not a shepherd, who doesn’t own the sheep, sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep, and flees. The wolf snatches the sheep, and scatters them. The hired hand flees because he is a hired hand, and doesn’t care for the sheep.
plain: Jesus says: I am the good shepherd, who gives his life for the sheep. A hired hand who doesn't own them runs when the wolf comes and leaves them scattered, because he doesn't care for them.
core_idea: The good shepherd gives his life for the sheep

text: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies. Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
note: Grief and hope beyond death

tags.when_helps: A Christian grieving a death or facing their own who needs the promise of life beyond it.

display_text: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies. Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
plain: Jesus tells her he is the resurrection and the life: whoever believes in him will live even after dying, and whoever lives and believes in him will never die. He asks if she believes this.
core_idea: Jesus is the resurrection and the life

text: Therefore when Mary came to where Jesus was, and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying to him, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.” When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews weeping who came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled, and said, “Where have you laid him?” They told him, “Lord, come and see.” Jesus wept.
note: Grief, regret and being wept with

tags.when_helps: Someone grieving a death who wonders why help did not come and needs to know their tears are shared.

display_text: Therefore when Mary came to where Jesus was, and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying to him, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.” When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews weeping who came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled, and said, “Where have you laid him?” They told him, “Lord, come and see.” Jesus wept.
plain: Mary fell at Jesus's feet weeping: if he had been there, her brother would not have died. Seeing her and the others weeping, Jesus was deeply moved and troubled, asked where they had laid him, and wept.
core_idea: Jesus wept with those who grieved

text: Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
note: Loss and endings that make new life possible

situations: loss of a dream or plan
keywords: grain of wheat falls and dies
tags.when_helps: Someone facing an ending who needs to see that letting something die can be what allows new life to grow.

display_text: Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
plain: Jesus says: unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it stays a single seed. But if it dies, it produces a great harvest.
core_idea: A seed must die to bear much fruit

text: “Now my soul is troubled. What shall I say? ‘Father, save me from this time?’ But for this cause I came to this time.
note: Facing a dreaded ordeal with purpose

tags.when_helps: Someone troubled before an ordeal they cannot avoid who wants to meet it as part of their purpose.

display_text: Now my soul is troubled. What shall I say? ‘Father, save me from this time?’ But for this cause I came to this time.
plain: Jesus says his soul is troubled, and asks whether he should pray to be saved from this hour. But this hour is the very reason he came.
core_idea: Troubled, yet facing the hour he came for

text: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you. Most certainly I tell you, a servant is not greater than his lord, neither one who is sent greater than he who sent him. If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.
note: Humble service to one another

tags.when_helps: Someone in a position of authority who needs reminding that leading means humble service to others.

display_text: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you. Most certainly I tell you, a servant is not greater than his lord, neither one who is sent greater than he who sent him. If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.
plain: Jesus says that since he, their Lord and teacher, washed their feet, they should wash each other's feet, following his example. A servant is not above his master, and they are blessed if they act on this.
core_idea: Serve one another as Jesus served

text: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.”
note: Love as the mark of a life

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: A Christian wondering how to treat others, especially when it is hard, who needs the plain command to love.

display_text: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.
plain: Jesus gives a new commandment: love one another as he has loved you. Everyone will know you are his disciples by your love for each other.
core_idea: Love one another as Jesus loved you

text: “Don’t let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me. In my Father’s house are many homes. If it weren’t so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you. If I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and will receive you to myself; that where I am, you may be there also.
note: Troubled heart, separation and belonging

keywords: many homes in my Father's house
don't let your heart be troubled
tags.when_helps: A Christian troubled by death or separation who needs the promise of a place prepared and reunion.

display_text: Don’t let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me. In my Father’s house are many homes. If it weren’t so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you. If I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and will receive you to myself; that where I am, you may be there also.
plain: Jesus says not to let your hearts be troubled, but to trust in God and in him. His Father's house has many rooms; he goes to prepare a place for you and will come back for you.
core_idea: Don't be troubled; a place is prepared for you

text: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, give I to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
note: Fear and anxiety; a deeper peace

keywords: my peace I give to you
tags.when_helps: A Christian with a troubled, fearful heart who needs a gift of peace the world cannot give.

display_text: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, give I to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
plain: Jesus says: I leave you peace, my own peace, not the kind the world gives. Don't let your hearts be troubled or afraid.
core_idea: Jesus gives a peace unlike the world's

text: “This is my commandment, that you love one another, even as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
note: Sacrificial love and friendship

tags.when_helps: Someone reflecting on what true love and friendship ask, including sacrifice for others.

display_text: This is my commandment, that you love one another, even as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
plain: Jesus commands: love one another as I have loved you. There is no greater love than to give your life for your friends.
core_idea: No greater love than dying for friends

text: Most certainly I tell you, that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy. A woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow, because her time has come. But when she has delivered the child, she doesn’t remember the anguish any more, for the joy that a human being is born into the world. Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.
note: Present sorrow that will turn to joy

tags.when_helps: A believer in a season of sorrow who needs the image of labour pains giving way to joy.

display_text: Most certainly I tell you, that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy. tags.when_helps: A Christian abandoned by those around them who needs to hear they are not truly alone.

display_text: Behold, the time is coming, yes, and has now come, that you will be scattered, everyone to his own place, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me. tags.when_helps: Someone near death or grieving who is thinking about who will care for the loved ones left behind.

note: Ageing, dependence, loss of control

tags.when_helps: Someone facing ageing or dependence on others, grieving lost independence and seeking acceptance.

display_text: Most certainly I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself, and walked where you wanted to. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will dress you, and carry you where you don’t want to go.

text: The waters surrounded me, even to the soul. The deep was around me. The weeds were wrapped around my head. I went down to the bottoms of the mountains. note: feeling overwhelmed and drowning, then rescued through prayer

tags.when_helps: A believer feeling engulfed and sinking who needs to hear that others cried out from the depths and were lifted.

display_text: The waters surrounded me, even to the soul. The deep was around me. The weeds were wrapped around my head. I went down to the bottoms of the mountains. The earth barred me in forever: yet have you brought up my life from the pit, Yahweh my God. “When my soul fainted within me, I remembered Yahweh. My prayer came in to you, into your holy temple.
plain: Jonah prays that the waters closed over him and he sank to the roots of the mountains, shut in forever, yet God brought his life up from the pit. When he was fainting, he remembered the Lord.
core_idea: From the depths, God brought my life up

text: Yahweh said, “Is it right for you to be angry?”
note: questioning whether one's anger is justified

keywords: is it right to be angry
tags.when_helps: Someone caught in anger who could use one simple question to pause and examine it.

display_text: Yahweh said, “Is it right for you to be angry?”
plain: God asked Jonah, "Is it right for you to be angry?"
core_idea: Is your anger justified?

text: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.
note: Courage when stepping into something new and daunting

tags.when_helps: A believer about to face something daunting who needs courage and the sense of not going alone.

display_text: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.
plain: God says: be strong and brave, as I have commanded you, and don't be afraid or discouraged. The Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
core_idea: Be strong and brave; God goes with you

text: Nothing failed of any good thing which Yahweh had spoken to the house of Israel. All came to pass.
note: trust that promised good will come; faithfulness

tags.when_helps: A believer looking back and seeing promises fulfilled, wanting to give thanks for God's faithfulness.

display_text: Nothing failed of any good thing which Yahweh had spoken to the house of Israel. All came to pass.
plain: Not one of the good things God had promised Israel failed; every one came true.
core_idea: Every good promise God made came true

text: Behold, today I am going the way of all the earth. You know in all your hearts and in all your souls that not one thing has failed of all the good things which Yahweh your God spoke concerning you. All have happened to you. Not one thing has failed of it.
note: facing death with gratitude for promises kept

keywords: the way of all the earth
tags.when_helps: An older believer near the end of life who wants to look back with gratitude on goodness received.

display_text: Behold, today I am going the way of all the earth. You know in all your hearts and in all your souls that not one thing has failed of all the good things which Yahweh your God spoke concerning you. All have happened to you. Not one thing has failed of it.
plain: Joshua says he is about to die. They know in their hearts that not one of the good things God promised them has failed; every one has come true.
core_idea: Not one of God's good promises has failed

text: If it seems evil to you to serve Yahweh, choose today whom you will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell; but as for me and my house, we will serve Yahweh.
note: making a decisive commitment; choosing what to live for

keywords: choose today whom you will serve
tags.when_helps: A believer torn between competing loyalties who needs a call to decide where they and their household stand.

display_text: If it seems evil to you to serve Yahweh, choose today whom you will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell; but as for me and my house, we will serve Yahweh.
plain: If you don't want to serve the Lord, choose today whom you will serve, your ancestors' gods or the gods of this land. But as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.
core_idea: Choose today whom you will serve

text: But you, beloved, keep building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit. Keep yourselves in God’s love, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to eternal life.
note: Staying steady in faith and prayer amid division

tags.when_helps: A Christian whose faith feels thin, encouraged to keep building it through prayer.

display_text: But you, beloved, keep building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit. Keep yourselves in God’s love, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to eternal life.
plain: But you, dear friends, keep building yourselves up in your holy faith and praying in the Holy Spirit. Keep yourselves in God's love as you wait for the mercy of Jesus Christ that brings eternal life.
core_idea: Build up your faith and stay in God's love

text: My soul, march on with strength.
note: self-encouragement to keep going

tags.when_helps: Someone flagging partway through a struggle who needs a brief word to keep going.

display_text: My soul, march on with strength.
plain: Deborah sings to herself: march on, my soul, and be strong.
core_idea: March on, my soul, with strength

text: The trees set out to anoint a king over themselves. They said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’ “But the olive tree said to them, ‘Should I stop producing my oil, with which they honor God and man by me, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’ “The trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come and reign over us.’ “But the fig tree said to them, ‘Should I leave my sweetness, and my good fruit, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’ “The trees said to the vine, ‘Come and reign over us.’ “The vine said to them, ‘Should I leave my new wine, which cheers God and man, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’ “Then all the trees said to the bramble, ‘Come and reign over us.’ “The bramble said to the trees, ‘If in truth you anoint me king over you, then come and take refuge in my shade; and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.’
note: ambition versus meaningful work; who seeks power

situations: a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted by a position of power over others, weighing it against the good work they already do.

display_text: The trees set out to anoint a king over themselves. They said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’ “But the olive tree said to them, ‘Should I stop producing my oil, with which they honor God and man by me, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’ “The trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come and reign over us.’ “But the fig tree said to them, ‘Should I leave my sweetness, and my good fruit, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’ “The trees said to the vine, ‘Come and reign over us.’ “The vine said to them, ‘Should I leave my new wine, which cheers God and man, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’ “Then all the trees said to the bramble, ‘Come and reign over us.’ “The bramble said to the trees, ‘If in truth you anoint me king over you, then come and take refuge in my shade; and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.’
plain: The trees wanted a king, but the olive, fig and vine each refused to give up their good gifts to rule. Only the bramble accepted, offering shade but threatening fire if refused.
core_idea: The worthy decline power; the worthless seize it

text: How can you say, ‘I love you,’ when your heart is not with me?
note: love that is spoken but not felt; trust in relationships

tags.when_helps: Someone who hears 'I love you' but senses their partner's heart is elsewhere.

display_text: How can you say, ‘I love you,’ when your heart is not with me?
plain: Delilah asks Samson how he can say he loves her when his heart is not with her.
core_idea: Love means the heart is truly with you

text: You are a helper of the oppressed, an upholder of the weak, a protector of the forlorn, a savior of those who are without hope.
note: hopelessness, weakness; prayer for help

tags.when_helps: A believer feeling weak, forgotten or oppressed who needs to hear God sides with the helpless.

display_text: You are a helper of the oppressed, an upholder of the weak, a protector of the forlorn, a savior of those who are without hope.
plain: Judith prays to God: you help the oppressed, support the weak, protect the abandoned, and save those who have no hope.
core_idea: God helps the oppressed and the hopeless

text: How the city sits solitary, that was full of people! She has become as a widow, who was great among the nations! She who was a princess among the provinces has become a slave! She weeps bitterly in the night. Her tears are on her cheeks. Among all her lovers she has no one to comfort her. All her friends have dealt treacherously with her. They have become her enemies.
note: Loneliness, loss of status, betrayal by friends

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone who has fallen from a full life to isolation, betrayed by friends, weeping alone at night.

display_text: How the city sits solitary, that was full of people! She has become as a widow, who was great among the nations! She who was a princess among the provinces has become a slave! She weeps bitterly in the night. Her tears are on her cheeks. Among all her lovers she has no one to comfort her. All her friends have dealt treacherously with her. They have become her enemies.
plain: The once-crowded city sits alone like a widow, a princess turned slave, weeping all night with no one to comfort her. Her friends have betrayed her and become her enemies.
core_idea: Desolate, betrayed and with no one to comfort

text: “Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look, and see if there is any sorrow like my sorrow, which is brought on me, with which Yahweh has afflicted me in the day of his fierce anger.
note: Grief that others pass by without noticing

tags.when_helps: Someone whose suffering feels unseen by passers-by, longing for it to be acknowledged.

display_text: Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look, and see if there is any sorrow like my sorrow, which is brought on me, with which Yahweh has afflicted me in the day of his fierce anger.
plain: Does it mean nothing to you, all who pass by? Look and see if there is any sorrow like mine, which the Lord brought on me in his fierce anger.
core_idea: Is there any sorrow like my sorrow?

text: “Look, Yahweh; for I am in distress. My heart is troubled. My heart turns over within me, for I have grievously rebelled. Abroad, the sword bereaves. At home, it is like death.
note: Distress and remorse; no refuge anywhere

tags.when_helps: Someone in distress, aware of their own wrongs, surrounded by danger with no safe place.

display_text: Look, Yahweh; for I am in distress. My heart is troubled. My heart turns over within me, for I have grievously rebelled. Abroad, the sword bereaves. At home, it is like death.
plain: Look, Lord, I am in distress, and my heart churns within me because I rebelled badly. Outside the sword kills, and at home there is only death.
core_idea: In distress, heart churning over my wrongs

text: Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches! Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift up your hands toward him for the life of your young children, who faint for hunger at the head of every street.
note: Pouring out one's heart in desperate prayer

keywords: pour out your heart like water
tags.when_helps: A believer desperate for their children's wellbeing, urged to pour out their heart in prayer.

display_text: Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches! Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift up your hands toward him for the life of your young children, who faint for hunger at the head of every street.
plain: Get up and cry out in the night, pouring out your heart like water before the Lord. Lift your hands to him for the lives of your children, fainting from hunger in every street.
core_idea: Pour out your heart before the Lord

text:
You have removed my soul far away from peace. I forgot prosperity.
I said, “My strength has perished, along with my expectation from Yahweh.”
Remember my affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the bitterness.
My soul still remembers them, and is bowed down within me.
This I recall to my mind; therefore I have hope.
It is because of Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn’t fail.
They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
“Yahweh is my portion,” says my soul. “Therefore I will hope in him.”
note: Despair turning to hope; mercies new every morning

tags.when_helps: Someone bowed down by misery who needs a path from bitterness back to hope, morning by morning.

display_text:
You have removed my soul far away from peace. I forgot prosperity.
I said, “My strength has perished, along with my expectation from Yahweh.”
Remember my affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the bitterness.
My soul still remembers them, and is bowed down within me.
This I recall to my mind; therefore I have hope.
