plain: I had lost all peace, strength and hope, but I call this to mind and so I have hope. God's love keeps us from ruin; his mercies are new every morning, and great is his faithfulness.
core_idea: His mercies are new every morning

plain_judge.issue: Drops "Yahweh is my portion; I will hope in him" and the remembered bitterness.

text:
Yahweh is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him.
It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of Yahweh.
note: Patience; waiting quietly in hope

tags.when_helps: A believer in a long wait who needs encouragement to hope quietly and patiently.

display_text:
Yahweh is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him.
It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of Yahweh.
plain: The Lord is good to those who wait for him and seek him. It is good to hope and wait quietly for the Lord to save.
core_idea: Wait quietly in hope for the Lord

text:
For the Lord will not cast off forever.
For though he causes grief, yet he will have compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
For he does not afflict willingly, nor grieve the children of men.
note: Grief that will not last forever

tags.when_helps: A believer in grief who fears they are abandoned and needs assurance compassion will return.

display_text:
For the Lord will not cast off forever.
For though he causes grief, yet he will have compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
For he does not afflict willingly, nor grieve the children of men.
plain: The Lord will not reject anyone forever. Though he brings grief, he will show compassion out of his great love, for he does not willingly cause suffering or grief.
core_idea: God does not reject forever; compassion follows grief

text:
Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to Yahweh.
Let us lift up our heart with our hands to God in the heavens.
note: Self-examination and turning back

tags.when_helps: Someone ready to examine their life honestly and turn back toward God.

display_text:
Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to Yahweh.
Let us lift up our heart with our hands to God in the heavens.
plain: Let us examine our ways and return to the Lord. Let us lift our hearts and our hands to God in heaven.
core_idea: Examine our ways and return to God

text:
Waters flowed over my head. I said, “I am cut off.”
I called on your name, Yahweh, out of the lowest dungeon.
You heard my voice: “Don’t hide your ear from my sighing, and my cry.”
You came near in the day that I called on you. You said, “Don’t be afraid.”
note: Overwhelmed at the lowest point; being heard

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling cut off and drowning who needs the memory that a cry from the depths was heard.

display_text:
Waters flowed over my head. I said, “I am cut off.”
I called on your name, Yahweh, out of the lowest dungeon.
You heard my voice: “Don’t hide your ear from my sighing, and my cry.”
You came near in the day that I called on you. You said, “Don’t be afraid.”
plain: Waters closed over my head and I thought I was finished, so I called your name, Lord, from the deepest pit. You heard me, came near, and said, "Don't be afraid."
core_idea: From the depths I called, and God said: don't fear

text:
The joy of our heart has ceased. Our dance is turned into mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!
note: Joy lost to mourning; regret

situations: loss of a home or something valued
tags.when_helps: Someone whose joy has turned to mourning, partly through their own wrongs, wanting to name the loss.

display_text:
The joy of our heart has ceased. Our dance is turned into mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!
plain: Our hearts have lost their joy, and our dancing has turned to mourning. The crown has fallen from our head; how terrible for us, for we have sinned.
core_idea: Our dancing has turned to mourning

text:
You, Yahweh, remain forever. Your throne is from generation to generation.
Why do you forget us forever, and forsake us for so long a time?
Turn us to yourself, Yahweh, and we will be turned. Renew our days as of old.
note: Feeling forgotten for too long; longing for renewal

keywords: renew our days as of old
tags.when_helps: A believer who feels forgotten by God and longs for renewal.

display_text:
You, Yahweh, remain forever. Your throne is from generation to generation.
Why do you forget us forever, and forsake us for so long a time?
Turn us to yourself, Yahweh, and we will be turned. Renew our days as of old.
plain: You, Lord, reign forever, so why have you forgotten us for so long? Bring us back to you and we will return; make our days new as they were before.
core_idea: Bring us back, Lord, and renew our days

text: My soul magnifies the Lord. My spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior, for he has looked at the humble state of his servant. For behold, from now on, all generations will call me blessed. For he who is mighty has done great things for me. Holy is his name.
note: joy and gratitude when lifted from humble circumstances

tags.when_helps: A believer overflowing with joy and thanks after something great, especially a pregnancy, wanting to give praise.

display_text: My soul magnifies the Lord. My spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior, for he has looked at the humble state of his servant. For behold, from now on, all generations will call me blessed. For he who is mighty has done great things for me. Holy is his name.
plain: Mary praises the Lord and rejoices in God her Saviour, who has noticed his humble servant. Every generation will call her blessed, for the Mighty One has done great things for her, and his name is holy.
core_idea: My soul praises God, who lifted the humble

text: The multitudes asked him, “What then must we do?” He answered them, “He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.”
note: simple generosity; sharing what you have

tags.when_helps: Someone asking what they should actually do, given a plain answer: share what you have.

display_text: The multitudes asked him, “What then must we do?” He answered them, “He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.”
plain: The crowds asked John what they should do. He answered: whoever has two coats should give one to someone with none, and whoever has food should do the same.
core_idea: If you have two, share with one who has none

text: Soldiers also asked him, saying, “What about us? What must we do?” He said to them, “Extort from no one by violence, neither accuse anyone wrongfully. Be content with your wages.”
note: honesty and contentment in ordinary work

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to cut corners at work for more money who needs plain counsel on honesty and contentment.

display_text: Soldiers also asked him, saying, “What about us? What must we do?” He said to them, “Extort from no one by violence, neither accuse anyone wrongfully. Be content with your wages.”
plain: Soldiers asked John what they should do. He told them not to extort money by force or make false accusations, and to be content with their pay.
core_idea: Take nothing by force; be content with your pay

text: Jesus answered him, saying, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’”
note: material needs are not the whole of life

tags.when_helps: Someone whose material needs are met yet who feels empty, reminded that people need more than bread.

display_text: Jesus answered him, saying, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’”
plain: Jesus answered that it is written: people don't live on bread alone, but on every word of God.
core_idea: We do not live by bread alone

text: The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the broken hearted, to proclaim release to the captives, recovering of sight to the blind, to deliver those who are crushed, and to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.
note: heartbreak and feeling crushed; hope of release

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels crushed or brokenhearted and needs to hear that healing and release are promised to them.

display_text: The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the broken hearted, to proclaim release to the captives, recovering of sight to the blind, to deliver those who are crushed, and to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.
plain: Jesus reads: the Spirit of the Lord is on me, sending me to bring good news to the poor, heal the broken-hearted, free captives, give sight to the blind, release the oppressed, and announce the Lord's year of favour.
core_idea: Good news for the poor and broken-hearted

text: When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep, and let down your nets for a catch.” Simon answered him, “Master, we worked all night, and took nothing; but at your word I will let down the net.” When they had done this, they caught a great multitude of fish, and their net was breaking.
note: discouraged after fruitless effort; trying once more

tags.when_helps: Someone who has worked all night with nothing to show, encouraged to try once more.

display_text: When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep, and let down your nets for a catch.” Simon answered him, “Master, we worked all night, and took nothing; but at your word I will let down the net.” When they had done this, they caught a great multitude of fish, and their net was breaking.
plain: Simon had fished all night and caught nothing, but when Jesus told him to let down his nets in deep water, he did it at his word. They caught so many fish that the nets began to break.
core_idea: After a fruitless night, trust brings a full net

text: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
note: grief and want; sorrow will not last

tags.when_helps: Someone hungry or weeping now who needs a promise that this will turn to fullness and laughter.

display_text: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
plain: Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
core_idea: Those who weep now will laugh

text: But I tell you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
note: responding to people who hurt or hate you

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone mistreated and wanting to hit back, challenged to respond with goodwill instead.

display_text: But I tell you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
plain: Jesus says to those listening: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
core_idea: Love your enemies and bless those who curse you

text: As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them. If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
note: treating others well beyond reciprocity

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone deciding how to treat others, especially those who don't treat them well.

display_text: As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them. If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
plain: Treat others exactly as you would want them to treat you. Loving only those who love you earns no credit, because even sinners do that.
core_idea: Treat others as you want to be treated

text: Don’t judge, and you won’t be judged. Don’t condemn, and you won’t be condemned. Set free, and you will be set free.
note: judging others; releasing resentment

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone quick to judge or condemn who might find freedom in releasing others.

display_text: Don’t judge, and you won’t be judged. Don’t condemn, and you won’t be condemned. Set free, and you will be set free.
plain: Don't judge, and you won't be judged; don't condemn, and you won't be condemned. Set others free, and you will be set free.
core_idea: Don't judge or condemn; set free and be freed

text: Why do you see the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye? Or how can you tell your brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck of chaff that is in your eye,’ when you yourself don’t see the beam that is in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye.
note: criticising others while blind to your own faults

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone fixated on another's faults who needs to look at their own first.

display_text: Why do you see the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye? Or how can you tell your brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck of chaff that is in your eye,’ when you yourself don’t see the beam that is in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye.
plain: Why notice the speck in your brother's eye and ignore the plank in your own, offering to fix his while blind to yours? You hypocrite: first remove your own plank, then you will see clearly to help him.
core_idea: Fix your own faults before judging others

text: The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings out that which is good, and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings out that which is evil, for out of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks.
note: words reveal what fills the heart

tags.when_helps: Someone noticing what their words reveal about their heart and wanting to change it.

display_text: The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings out that which is good, and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings out that which is evil, for out of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks.
plain: A good person brings good out of the good stored in their heart, and an evil person brings evil out of the evil stored there. What fills the heart comes out of the mouth.
core_idea: The mouth speaks what fills the heart

text: Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words, and does them, I will show you who he is like. He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep, and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood arose, the stream broke against that house, and could not shake it, because it was founded on the rock. But he who hears, and doesn’t do, is like a man who built a house on the earth without a foundation, against which the stream broke, and immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great.
note: building a life that withstands crisis

tags.when_helps: Someone bracing for hard times who wants to build their life on a foundation that holds.

display_text: Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words, and does them, I will show you who he is like. He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep, and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood arose, the stream broke against that house, and could not shake it, because it was founded on the rock. But he who hears, and doesn’t do, is like a man who built a house on the earth without a foundation, against which the stream broke, and immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great.
plain: Whoever hears Jesus's words and acts on them is like a man who built his house on rock, which the flood could not shake. Whoever hears but doesn't act built without foundation, and his house fell in ruins.
core_idea: Build your life on hearing and doing

text: No one, having put his hand to the plow, and looking back, is fit for God’s Kingdom.
note: commitment; not dwelling on what you left behind

tags.when_helps: Someone who has committed to a new path but keeps looking back, urged to keep going.

display_text: No one, having put his hand to the plow, and looking back, is fit for God’s Kingdom.
plain: No one who puts a hand to the plough and keeps looking back is fit for God's Kingdom.
core_idea: Don't look back once you've committed

text: A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving him half dead. By chance a certain priest was going down that way. When he saw him, he passed by on the other side. In the same way a Levite also, when he came to the place, and saw him, passed by on the other side. But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion, came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
note: compassion for strangers; not passing by suffering

tags.when_helps: Someone deciding whether to stop for a stranger in need, shown that compassion crosses every boundary.

display_text: A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving him half dead. By chance a certain priest was going down that way. When he saw him, he passed by on the other side. In the same way a Levite also, when he came to the place, and saw him, passed by on the other side. But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion, came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
plain: A man was robbed and left half dead, and a priest and a Levite saw him and passed by on the other side. But a Samaritan felt compassion, bandaged his wounds and took him to an inn.
core_idea: The Samaritan who stopped and showed compassion

text: As they went on their way, he entered into a certain village, and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house. She had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word. But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she came up to him, and said, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me.” Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things, but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”
note: busy, overwhelmed and resentful; what truly matters

tags.when_helps: Someone frazzled by endless tasks and resentful of others who rest, reminded that one thing matters most.

display_text: As they went on their way, he entered into a certain village, and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house. She had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word. But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she came up to him, and said, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me.” Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things, but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”
plain: Martha, busy serving, complained that her sister Mary sat listening at Jesus's feet instead of helping. Jesus said Martha was anxious about many things when only one is needed, and Mary had chosen the good part.
core_idea: Anxious about many things when one is needed

text: When you pray, say, ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. May your Kingdom come. May your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us day by day our daily bread. Forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us. Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’
note: how to pray; daily needs, forgiveness, protection

tags.when_helps: A believer unsure how to pray who wants simple words for daily needs, forgiveness and protection.

display_text: When you pray, say, ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. May your Kingdom come. May your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us day by day our daily bread. Forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us. Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’
plain: Jesus teaches them to pray: Father in heaven, may your name be holy, your Kingdom come, your will be done. Give us our daily bread, forgive our sins as we forgive others, and keep us from temptation and from evil.
core_idea: The Lord's Prayer: how Jesus taught us to pray

text: I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given you. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
note: persistence when answers are slow to come

tags.when_helps: Someone who has been seeking without answer, encouraged to keep asking and knocking.

display_text: I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given you. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
plain: Keep asking and you will receive, keep seeking and you will find, keep knocking and the door will open. Everyone who asks, seeks and knocks will receive, find and be let in.
core_idea: Ask, seek, knock, and it will be given

text: “Aren’t five sparrows sold for two assaria coins? Not one of them is forgotten by God. But the very hairs of your head are all counted. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
note: Fear and feeling worthless or forgotten

tags.when_helps: Someone afraid and feeling overlooked who needs to hear that they are not forgotten and are valued.

display_text: Aren’t five sparrows sold for two assaria coins? Not one of them is forgotten by God. But the very hairs of your head are all counted. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
plain: God forgets not even one cheap sparrow, and every hair on your head is counted. So don't be afraid: you are worth more than many sparrows.
core_idea: God counts every hair; don't be afraid

text: He said to them, “Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”
note: Greed; life is more than possessions

tags.when_helps: Someone caught up in wanting more things, reminded that life isn't measured by possessions.

display_text: He said to them, “Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”
plain: Jesus warns: watch out and guard against greed, because a person's life is not made up of how much they own.
core_idea: Life is not measured by possessions

text: Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothing. Consider the ravens: they don’t sow, they don’t reap, they have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds! Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height? If then you aren’t able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?
note: Anxiety about money and daily needs

tags.when_helps: Someone anxious about food, clothes or money who needs to hear that worry adds nothing and they are cared for.

display_text: Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothing. Consider the ravens: they don’t sow, they don’t reap, they have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds! Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height? If then you aren’t able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?
plain: Life is more than food and clothes; God feeds the ravens, who neither sow nor store, and you are worth far more. Worry can't add an inch to your height, so why worry about the rest?
core_idea: Worry adds nothing; God feeds the ravens

text: Sell that which you have, and give gifts to the needy. Make for yourselves purses which don’t grow old, a treasure in the heavens that doesn’t fail, where no thief approaches, neither moth destroys. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
note: What we value shapes where our heart goes

tags.when_helps: Someone whose heart is tied to possessions, invited to consider where their real treasure lies.

display_text: Sell that which you have, and give gifts to the needy. Make for yourselves purses which don’t grow old, a treasure in the heavens that doesn’t fail, where no thief approaches, neither moth destroys. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
plain: Sell what you own, give to the poor, and store up treasure in heaven that no thief or moth can reach. Where your treasure is, your heart will be too.
core_idea: Where your treasure is, your heart is

text: To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more will be asked.
note: Responsibility that comes with gifts and privilege

tags.when_helps: Someone with talents or privilege weighing the responsibility that comes with them.

display_text: To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more will be asked.
plain: Much will be required of whoever has been given much, and even more will be asked of whoever has been trusted with much.
core_idea: Much given means much required

text: He spoke this parable. “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it, and found none. He said to the vine dresser, ‘Behold, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none. Cut it down. Why does it waste the soil?’ He answered, ‘Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it, and fertilize it. If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’”
note: Patience and a second chance for slow growth

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels they have borne no fruit and fears being given up on, offered patience and another chance.

display_text: He spoke this parable. “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it, and found none. He said to the vine dresser, ‘Behold, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none. Cut it down. Why does it waste the soil?’ He answered, ‘Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it, and fertilize it. If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’”
plain: A man wanted to cut down a fig tree that had borne no fruit for three years. His gardener asked for one more year to tend and fertilise it, and to cut it down only if it still bore nothing.
core_idea: One more year of care before giving up

text: “When you are invited by anyone to a marriage feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him, and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place. But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
note: Humility, status and pride

tags.when_helps: Someone eager for status at a gathering, or stung by being put down, given practical counsel on humility.

display_text: “When you are invited by anyone to a marriage feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him, and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place. But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
plain: At a wedding feast, take the lowest seat rather than the best, so your host may move you up with honour instead of down in shame. Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
core_idea: Take the lowest seat; the humble will be raised

text: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it? Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation, and is not able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him, saying, ‘This man began to build, and wasn’t able to finish.’
note: Weighing a big decision before committing

tags.when_helps: Someone about to start a big project or commitment who should first count the cost.

display_text: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it? Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation, and is not able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him, saying, ‘This man began to build, and wasn’t able to finish.’
plain: Who builds a tower without first sitting down to count the cost? Otherwise, having laid the foundation and been unable to finish, people will mock: this man began building but couldn't finish.
core_idea: Count the cost before you begin

text: “Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep, and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one that was lost, until he found it? When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing. When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’ I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.
note: Feeling lost; being sought and welcomed back

tags.when_helps: Someone who has gone astray and fears there is no way back, told they are sought and welcomed with joy.

display_text: Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep, and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one that was lost, until he found it? When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing. When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’ I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.
plain: Anyone who lost one sheep of a hundred would leave the ninety-nine, search until it was found, and carry it home rejoicing. Heaven rejoices more over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine who need no repentance.
core_idea: Heaven rejoices over one lost one found

text: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
note: Integrity in small things

tags.when_helps: Someone wondering whether small honesty or small duties matter, reminded that character shows in little things.

display_text: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
plain: Whoever is faithful in small things is faithful in big things too. Whoever is dishonest in small things is dishonest in big things too.
core_idea: Faithful in little, faithful in much

text: No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. You aren’t able to serve God and Mammon.”
note: Divided loyalties; money versus deeper values

tags.when_helps: Someone torn between money and their deeper values who must choose what they serve.

display_text: No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. You aren’t able to serve God and Mammon.
plain: No servant can serve two masters; he will hate one and love the other, or be loyal to one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.
core_idea: You cannot serve God and money

text: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him. If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”
note: Forgiving someone who keeps hurting you

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone wronged repeatedly by a sibling or friend who wants guidance on speaking up and forgiving.

display_text: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him. If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.
plain: Watch yourself. If your brother wrongs you, tell him so; if he is sorry, forgive him. Even if he wrongs you seven times in one day and comes back each time saying sorry, forgive him.
core_idea: Forgive a brother who repents, however often he returns.

plain_judge.issue: 'Rebuke him' softened to 'tell him so'.

text: Being asked by the Pharisees when God’s Kingdom would come, he answered them, “God’s Kingdom doesn’t come with observation; neither will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for behold, God’s Kingdom is within you.”
note: Seeking meaning outside instead of within

tags.when_helps: Someone searching outside themselves for the sacred, invited to look within.

display_text: Being asked by the Pharisees when God’s Kingdom would come, he answered them, “God’s Kingdom doesn’t come with observation; neither will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for behold, God’s Kingdom is within you.”
plain: Asked by the Pharisees when God's Kingdom would arrive, Jesus said it is not something you can watch for or point to here or there, because God's Kingdom is within you.
core_idea: God's Kingdom is within you, not out there.

text: Whoever seeks to save his life loses it, but whoever loses his life preserves it.
note: Clinging versus letting go

tags.when_helps: Someone clinging tightly to security who might find that letting go is how one truly lives.

display_text: Whoever seeks to save his life loses it, but whoever loses his life preserves it.
plain: Whoever tries to hold on to their life loses it, and whoever lets go of their life keeps it.
core_idea: Clinging to life loses it; letting go keeps it.

plain_judge.issue: 'Loses his life' softened to 'lets go of their life'.

text: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray, and not give up, saying, “There was a judge in a certain city who didn’t fear God, and didn’t respect man. A widow was in that city, and she often came to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’ He wouldn’t for a while, but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God, nor respect man, yet because this widow bothers me, I will defend her, or else she will wear me out by her continual coming.’”
note: Persistence when no one seems to listen

tags.when_helps: Someone seeking justice or an answer who is tempted to give up, encouraged to persist.

display_text: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray, and not give up, saying, “There was a judge in a certain city who didn’t fear God, and didn’t respect man. A widow was in that city, and she often came to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’ He wouldn’t for a while, but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God, nor respect man, yet because this widow bothers me, I will defend her, or else she will wear me out by her continual coming.’”
plain: Jesus told a story to show that people should keep praying and never give up: a widow kept pleading with a judge who cared for neither God nor people, until he helped her just to stop her pestering.
core_idea: Keep praying persistently and do not give up.

text: “Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector. The Pharisee stood and prayed to himself like this: ‘God, I thank you, that I am not like the rest of men, extortionists, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector. I fast twice a week. I give tithes of all that I get.’ But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’ I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
note: Self-righteousness, guilt and honest humility

tags.when_helps: Someone ashamed of their failings who fears they are worse than others; honest humility is what is welcomed.

display_text: “Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector. The Pharisee stood and prayed to himself like this: ‘God, I thank you, that I am not like the rest of men, extortionists, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector. I fast twice a week. I give tithes of all that I get.’ But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’ I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
plain: A proud Pharisee thanked God he was better than others; a tax collector stood far off begging mercy as a sinner. The humble man went home right with God, for the proud will be humbled and the humble raised.
core_idea: The humble are lifted up; the self-exalting are humbled.

text: But he said, “The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.”
note: Facing what seems impossible

tags.when_helps: A believer facing what seems impossible who needs to remember that God's possibilities exceed human ones.

display_text: But he said, “The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.”
plain: Jesus said that what people cannot do, God can.
core_idea: What is impossible for people is possible for God.

text: He looked up, and saw the rich people who were putting their gifts into the treasury. He saw a certain poor widow casting in two small brass coins. He said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow put in more than all of them, for all these put in gifts for God from their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in all that she had to live on.”
note: Feeling your small contribution doesn't count

tags.when_helps: Someone who can only give a little and feels it doesn't count, told that a gift from poverty counts most.

display_text: He looked up, and saw the rich people who were putting their gifts into the treasury. He saw a certain poor widow casting in two small brass coins. He said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow put in more than all of them, for all these put in gifts for God from their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in all that she had to live on.”
plain: Jesus watched the rich give to the temple treasury and a poor widow drop in two small coins. She gave more than all of them, he said: they gave from surplus, she gave all she had.
core_idea: A poor person's whole gift outweighs the rich's surplus.

text: He said to them, “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called ‘benefactors.’ But not so with you. But one who is the greater among you, let him become as the younger, and one who is governing, as one who serves. For who is greater, one who sits at the table, or one who serves? Isn’t it he who sits at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
note: Ambition, leadership and serving others

tags.when_helps: Someone leading others or vying for rank who needs to see leadership as service.

display_text: He said to them, “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called ‘benefactors.’ But not so with you. But one who is the greater among you, let him become as the younger, and one who is governing, as one who serves. For who is greater, one who sits at the table, or one who serves? Isn’t it he who sits at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
plain: Jesus told his followers that rulers lord it over people, but among them the greatest should act like the youngest and the leader like a servant, just as he lives among them as one who serves.
core_idea: True greatness means serving others, as Jesus served.

plain_judge.issue: Drops the ironic 'benefactors' title and the table-versus-servant question.

text: He was withdrawn from them about a stone’s throw, and he knelt down and prayed, saying, “Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”
note: Dreading what lies ahead; surrender and acceptance

tags.when_helps: A believer dreading what lies ahead, asking for it to pass while trying to surrender to God's will.

display_text: He was withdrawn from them about a stone’s throw, and he knelt down and prayed, saying, “Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”
plain: Jesus went a little apart, knelt, and prayed: Father, if you are willing, take this suffering away from me; yet let your will be done, not mine.
core_idea: Surrender your own will to God's, even in anguish.

text: Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.”
note: Forgiving those who hurt you

keywords: they know not what they do
tags.when_helps: Someone deeply wronged who is wrestling with whether forgiveness is possible.

display_text: Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.”
plain: Jesus prayed, Father, forgive them, because they do not know what they are doing.
core_idea: Forgive those who harm you without understanding.

text: Don’t we all have one father? Hasn’t one God created us? Why do we deal treacherously every man against his brother, profaning the covenant of our fathers?
note: shared humanity and betrayal between people

tags.when_helps: Someone in a bitter feud with kin or neighbours, reminded of their shared origin.

display_text: Don’t we all have one father? Hasn’t one God created us? Why do we deal treacherously every man against his brother, profaning the covenant of our fathers?
plain: Don't we all share one father, made by the one God? So why do we betray one another and dishonour the covenant our ancestors made?
core_idea: One God made us all, so why betray each other?

text: You have said, ‘It is vain to serve God;’ and ‘What profit is it that we have followed his instructions, and that we have walked mournfully before Yahweh of Armies? Now we call the proud happy; yes, those who work wickedness are built up; yes, they tempt God, and escape.’ Then those who feared Yahweh spoke one with another; and Yahweh listened, and heard, and a book of memory was written before him, for those who feared Yahweh, and who honored his name. They shall be mine,” says Yahweh of Armies, “my own possession in the day that I make, and I will spare them, as a man spares his own son who serves him.
note: discouragement when wrongdoers seem to prosper

tags.when_helps: A believer wondering if faithfulness is pointless when the dishonest seem to thrive.

display_text: You have said, ‘It is vain to serve God;’ and ‘What profit is it that we have followed his instructions, and that we have walked mournfully before Yahweh of Armies? Now we call the proud happy; yes, those who work wickedness are built up; yes, they tempt God, and escape.’ Then those who feared Yahweh spoke one with another; and Yahweh listened, and heard, and a book of memory was written before him, for those who feared Yahweh, and who honored his name. They shall be mine,” says Yahweh of Armies, “my own possession in the day that I make, and I will spare them, as a man spares his own son who serves him.
plain: You complain that serving God is pointless, since the proud seem happy and the wicked prosper unpunished. Then Yahweh heard those who revered him, had their names recorded, and promised to keep and spare them as his own.
core_idea: When the wicked prosper, God still remembers the faithful.

plain_judge.issue: Drops the image of sparing them as a father spares a serving son.

text: Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
note: feeling unworthy; help is for the struggling

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels too sinful to be welcomed, reminded that the call is for exactly them.

display_text: Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
plain: Healthy people don't need a doctor; sick people do. Jesus said he came to call not the righteous but sinners to turn back.
core_idea: Jesus came for sinners, as doctors come for the sick.

text: No one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, or else the patch shrinks and the new tears away from the old, and a worse hole is made. No one puts new wine into old wineskins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and the wine pours out, and the skins will be destroyed; but they put new wine into fresh wineskins.
note: real change needs new forms, not patches

situations: a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: Someone trying to fit something new into an old structure who may need a fresh form for it.

display_text: No one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, or else the patch shrinks and the new tears away from the old, and a worse hole is made. No one puts new wine into old wineskins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and the wine pours out, and the skins will be destroyed; but they put new wine into fresh wineskins.
plain: Nobody patches an old garment with new cloth, or it shrinks and tears a worse hole. Nobody pours new wine into old wineskins, or they burst and both are lost; new wine goes into new skins.
core_idea: The new cannot be forced into old forms.

text: The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
note: rules should serve people, not burden them

tags.when_helps: Someone burdened by rules or obligations who needs reminding that rest and rules exist to serve people.

display_text: The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
plain: The Sabbath was made to serve people, not people to serve the Sabbath.
core_idea: Rules exist for people, not people for rules.

text: If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand. If a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
note: family or inner conflict; division destroys

tags.when_helps: Someone in a household or group pulling itself apart, prompted to see that division cannot stand.

display_text: If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand. If a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
plain: A kingdom split against itself cannot last, and neither can a household split against itself.
core_idea: A divided kingdom or house cannot stand.

text: God’s Kingdom is as if a man should cast seed on the earth, and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, though he doesn’t know how. For the earth bears fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
note: patience; growth happens slowly and unseen

tags.when_helps: Someone anxious that their effort isn't working who can trust that growth happens unseen, in its own time.

display_text: God’s Kingdom is as if a man should cast seed on the earth, and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, though he doesn’t know how. For the earth bears fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
plain: God's Kingdom is like a man who scatters seed and goes on sleeping and waking while it sprouts and grows without his knowing how. The earth produces the crop by itself, step by step, from shoot to full grain.
core_idea: God's Kingdom grows quietly, beyond our understanding or control.

text: How will we liken God’s Kingdom? Or with what parable will we illustrate it? It’s like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, though it is less than all the seeds that are on the earth, yet when it is sown, grows up, and becomes greater than all the herbs, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can lodge under its shadow.
note: small beginnings can grow into something great

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels their beginning is tiny, encouraged that small seeds can shelter many.

display_text: How will we liken God’s Kingdom? Or with what parable will we illustrate it? It’s like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, though it is less than all the seeds that are on the earth, yet when it is sown, grows up, and becomes greater than all the herbs, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can lodge under its shadow.
plain: God's Kingdom is like a mustard seed: the smallest of seeds when planted, it grows into the largest of plants, with branches big enough for birds to shelter in its shade.
core_idea: God's Kingdom starts tiny and grows great.

text: Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house.”
note: unappreciated by family and those closest

tags.when_helps: Someone overlooked by their own relatives and hometown who needs to know they are in good company.

display_text: Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house.”
plain: Jesus said a prophet is honoured everywhere except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own home.
core_idea: Prophets go unhonoured among their own people.

text: He said to them, “You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
note: overwork and exhaustion; the need to rest

tags.when_helps: Someone so busy they have no time even to eat, invited to step away and rest awhile.

display_text: He said to them, “You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
plain: Jesus told his followers to come away with him to a quiet place and rest for a while, because so many people were coming and going that they had no time even to eat.
core_idea: Step away from the crowd and rest awhile.

text: There is nothing from outside of the man, that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.
note: character comes from within, not outward things

keywords: what proceeds out of a man
tags.when_helps: Someone anxious about outward contamination who needs to focus on what comes from within.

display_text: There is nothing from outside of the man, that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.
plain: Nothing that enters a person from outside can make them unclean; what makes a person unclean is what comes out of them.
core_idea: What comes out of you defiles, not what goes in.

text: For what does it profit a man, to gain the whole world, and forfeit his life? For what will a man give in exchange for his life?
note: ambition and success at the cost of the soul

tags.when_helps: Someone pursuing gain who senses they may be trading away their own life for it.

display_text: For what does it profit a man, to gain the whole world, and forfeit his life? For what will a man give in exchange for his life?
plain: What good is it to win the whole world and lose your own life? What could anyone give in exchange for their life?
core_idea: Gaining the world is worthless if you lose your life.

text: Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes.” Immediately the father of the child cried out with tears, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”
note: wanting to hope while struggling with doubt

tags.when_helps: Someone desperate for a loved one who wants to believe but doubts, and needs to know that honest plea is enough.

display_text: Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes.” Immediately the father of the child cried out with tears, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”
plain: Jesus told a father that everything is possible for someone who believes. At once the father cried out in tears, I do believe; help me with my unbelief!
core_idea: Faith can be honest about its own doubt.

text: If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.
note: ambition, status, and humble service

keywords: last of all, servant of all
tags.when_helps: Someone eager to be first who needs the reversal: greatness lies in serving.

display_text: If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.
plain: Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and the servant of everyone.
core_idea: To be first, be last and serve all.

text: Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.
note: openness and trust like a child

tags.when_helps: A seeker overthinking their faith, invited to receive with a child's simple openness.

display_text: Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.
plain: Jesus said that anyone who does not receive God's Kingdom the way a little child does will never enter it.
core_idea: Receive God's Kingdom like a little child.

text: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.
note: wealth and attachment to possessions

tags.when_helps: Someone absorbed in wealth who needs a sharp reminder of how riches can block what matters most.

display_text: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.
plain: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter God's Kingdom.
core_idea: Wealth makes entering God's Kingdom very hard.

text: Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone; so that your Father, who is in heaven, may also forgive you your transgressions.
note: holding a grudge; letting go through forgiveness

tags.when_helps: A believer holding something against someone, reminded to forgive as they seek forgiveness in prayer.

display_text: Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone; so that your Father, who is in heaven, may also forgive you your transgressions.
plain: When you stand to pray and hold something against anyone, forgive them, so that your Father in heaven will also forgive your wrongs.
core_idea: Forgive others when you pray, so God forgives you.

text: The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one: you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment. The second is like this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.
note: what matters most: wholehearted love of God and neighbour

tags.when_helps: A believer wondering what truly matters, given the two great commandments of love.

display_text: The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one: you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment. The second is like this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.
plain: The greatest commandment is that the Lord our God is one, and you must love God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength. The second is to love your neighbour as yourself. No commandment is greater than these.
core_idea: Love God wholly and your neighbour as yourself.

text: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury, and saw how the multitude cast money into the treasury. Many who were rich cast in much. A poor widow came, and she cast in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin. He called his disciples to himself, and said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury, for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”
note: feeling your small contribution doesn't count

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels their small gift is worthless beside others', reminded that what is given from little counts most.

display_text: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury, and saw how the multitude cast money into the treasury. Many who were rich cast in much. A poor widow came, and she cast in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin. He called his disciples to himself, and said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury, for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”
plain: Jesus watched the rich put large sums into the temple treasury and a poor widow put in two tiny coins. She gave more than all of them, he said: they gave from surplus, she gave everything she had.
core_idea: A poor person's whole gift outweighs the rich's surplus.

text: When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. For those must happen, but the end is not yet.
note: anxiety about frightening world news

tags.when_helps: Someone shaken by news of conflict who needs to hear not to be troubled.

display_text: When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. For those must happen, but the end is not yet.
plain: When you hear of wars and rumours of wars, don't be alarmed. These things must happen, but they are not yet the end.
core_idea: Don't be alarmed by wars; the end is not yet.

text: A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children; she wouldn’t be comforted, because they are no more.
note: Inconsolable grief over lost children

tags.when_helps: A parent grieving a child who cannot be comforted and needs their grief recognised, not fixed.

display_text: A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children; she wouldn’t be comforted, because they are no more.
plain: A cry was heard in Ramah, weeping and deep mourning: Rachel crying for her children, refusing to be comforted, because they are gone.
core_idea: A mother's grief for lost children refuses comfort.

text: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.
note: Needing more than material things; meaning beyond survival

tags.when_helps: Someone whose material needs are met yet who feels unfed, reminded life needs more than bread.

display_text: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.
plain: People do not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from God's mouth.
core_idea: People live by God's word, not bread alone.

text: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven. Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted. Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth. Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled. Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy. Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God. Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God. Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
note: Comfort for the mourning, humble, gentle and wronged

tags.when_helps: Someone mourning, humbled or mistreated for doing right who needs to hear they are blessed.

display_text: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven. Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted. Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth. Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled. Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy. Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God. Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God. Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
plain: Blessed are the humble in spirit, the grieving, the gentle, those who long for what is right, the merciful, the pure in heart, the peacemakers and the persecuted: God's Kingdom, comfort and mercy will be theirs.
core_idea: God blesses the humble, grieving, merciful and peacemaking.

plain_judge.issue: Merges the distinct promises; drops inheriting the earth, being filled, seeing God, children of God.

text: You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden. Neither do you light a lamp, and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house. Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
note: Not hiding your gifts; letting your goodness show

tags.when_helps: Someone hiding their gifts who needs encouragement to let their good shine openly.

display_text: You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden. Neither do you light a lamp, and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house. Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
plain: You are the light of the world, like a city on a hill that cannot be hidden. No one hides a lamp; so let your light shine, that people see your good deeds and praise your Father in heaven.
core_idea: Let your light shine so others see good.

text: You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’ But I tell you, don’t resist him who is evil; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also. If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also. Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.
note: Answering harm without revenge

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone wronged and wanting to retaliate, challenged to answer with generosity instead.

display_text: You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’ But I tell you, don’t resist him who is evil; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also. If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also. Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.
plain: You were taught an eye for an eye, but Jesus says don't fight back against someone who wrongs you. Struck on one cheek, offer the other; sued for your coat, give your cloak; forced one mile, go two.
core_idea: Do not retaliate; answer wrong with more generosity.

text: You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you, that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.
note: Loving enemies; responding to people who hurt you

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
keywords: rain on the just and unjust
tags.when_helps: Someone holding hatred toward an enemy, challenged to love and pray for them.

display_text: You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you, that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.
plain: You were taught to love your neighbour and hate your enemy, but Jesus says love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, to be children of your Father, who sends sun and rain on good and bad alike.
core_idea: Love your enemies, as God gives to all alike.

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you'.

text: When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward. But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
note: Private, sincere prayer rather than show

tags.when_helps: Someone whose faith has become performance, invited to quiet, private prayer.

display_text: When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward. But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
plain: When you pray, don't be like hypocrites who pray in public to be seen; that attention is all the reward they get. Instead pray privately behind a closed door, and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
core_idea: Pray in private, not to be seen by others.

text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
note: Forgiving others; struggling to forgive

tags.when_helps: A believer struggling to forgive someone, reminded that forgiving and being forgiven go together.

display_text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
plain: If you forgive others the wrongs they do, your heavenly Father will forgive you too; but if you don't forgive them, your Father will not forgive your wrongs.
core_idea: God forgives you as you forgive others.

text: Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal; but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal; for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
note: Money, possessions and what the heart values

tags.when_helps: Someone absorbed in building wealth, asked where their heart is really invested.

display_text: Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal; but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal; for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
plain: Don't store up treasures on earth, where they decay or get stolen; store up treasures in heaven, where they are safe. Your heart will be wherever your treasure is.
core_idea: Your heart follows what you treasure.

text: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing? See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. note: Worry about money and basic needs

tags.when_helps: Someone consumed by worry about money and basic needs who needs perspective on what worry can achieve.

display_text: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing? See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they? “Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
plain: Don't worry about what you will eat, drink or wear; life is more than food and clothes. The birds don't farm, yet your heavenly Father feeds them, and you are worth more. Worrying cannot add a moment to your life.
core_idea: Don't worry; God cares for you, and worry adds nothing.

text: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.

display_text: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
plain: So don't worry about tomorrow; tomorrow will bring its own worries. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
core_idea: Don't worry about tomorrow; today has enough trouble.

text: Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged. For with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you. Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye? Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye;’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye? You hypocrite! note: Judging others while ignoring your own faults

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone fixated on another person's faults, challenged to look honestly at their own first.

display_text: Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged. For with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you. Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye? Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye;’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
plain: Don't judge, or you will be judged by the standard you use. Why notice the speck in your brother's eye and ignore the plank in your own? Remove your own plank first; then you can help him.
core_idea: Fix your own faults before judging others'.

plain_judge.issue: Drops the rebuke 'You hypocrite!' and the idea of seeing clearly.

text: Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you. For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.

display_text: Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you. For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.

core_idea: Ask, seek and knock, and you will receive.

tags.when_helps: Someone unsure how to treat a difficult person, reminded to do as they would be done by.

display_text: Therefore whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.

text: Enter in by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter in by it. How narrow is the gate, and restricted is the way that leads to life! Few are those who find it.

tags.when_helps: Someone choosing the harder, less popular right path while most around them take the easy way.

display_text: Enter in by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter in by it. How narrow is the gate, and restricted is the way that leads to life! Few are those who find it.

core_idea: The road to life is narrow and few find it.

text: Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.
note: Feeling unworthy; help is for those who struggle

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels too broken or flawed to deserve help, reminded that help is meant for exactly them.

display_text: Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.

core_idea: Help is for those who need it.

display_text: Freely you received, so freely give.
plain: You were given freely, so give freely.
core_idea: Give freely, as you freely received.

text: Aren’t two sparrows sold for an assarion coin? Not one of them falls on the ground apart from your Father’s will, but the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
note: Fear and feeling insignificant; being known and valued

tags.when_helps: Someone afraid and feeling insignificant who needs to hear they are seen, counted and valued.

display_text: Aren’t two sparrows sold for an assarion coin? Not one of them falls on the ground apart from your Father’s will, but the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
plain: Two sparrows sell for a small coin, yet not one falls to the ground without your Father's will, and every hair on your head is counted. So don't be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
core_idea: God cares for you, so do not fear.

text: Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
note: Exhaustion and heavy burdens; longing for rest

tags.when_helps: Someone worn out and weighed down who longs for rest and gentleness rather than more demands.

display_text: Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
plain: Jesus invites everyone who is worn out and weighed down to come to him for rest. Take on his yoke and learn from him, for he is gentle and humble; his yoke is easy and his load is light.
core_idea: Come to Jesus when weary and find rest.

text: Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.

display_text: Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.

core_idea: Division brings any kingdom or house to ruin.

text: For out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks. The good man out of his good treasure brings out good things, and the evil man out of his evil treasure brings out evil things.
note: Words reveal the heart; speech and character

tags.when_helps: Someone reflecting on their words who wants to tend the heart they come from.

display_text: For out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks. The good man out of his good treasure brings out good things, and the evil man out of his evil treasure brings out evil things.
plain: The mouth speaks from what fills the heart. A good person brings good things out of the good stored inside, and an evil person brings evil things out of the evil stored inside.
core_idea: Words reveal what fills the heart.

text: Behold, a farmer went out to sow. As he sowed, some seeds fell by the roadside, and the birds came and devoured them. tags.when_helps: Someone whose efforts keep falling flat who needs to see that some seed always finds good soil.

display_text: Behold, a farmer went out to sow. As he sowed, some seeds fell by the roadside, and the birds came and devoured them. Others fell on rocky ground, where they didn’t have much soil, and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of earth. When the sun had risen, they were scorched. plain: A farmer sowed seed. Some fell on the path and birds ate it; some on rocky ground, sprang up fast and withered without roots; some among thorns and was choked; and some on good soil, yielding a rich harvest.
core_idea: The same seed thrives only in good soil.

text: The Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field; which indeed is smaller than all seeds. But when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs, and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels their start is too small to matter, reminded that tiny beginnings can grow great.

display_text: The Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field; which indeed is smaller than all seeds. But when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs, and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.
plain: The Kingdom of Heaven is like a mustard seed a man planted: the smallest of all seeds, it grows into a tree big enough for birds to nest in its branches.
core_idea: The Kingdom of Heaven starts tiny and grows great.

text: A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and in his own house.

tags.when_helps: Someone respected elsewhere but dismissed by family or hometown who needs to know this is a common fate.

display_text: A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and in his own house.

core_idea: Prophets go unhonoured among their own people.

text: That which enters into the mouth doesn’t defile the man; but that which proceeds out of the mouth, this defiles the man.
