keywords: what comes out of the mouth
tags.when_helps: Someone fixated on outward rules or purity who needs reminding that what they say and do matters more.

display_text: That which enters into the mouth doesn’t defile the man; but that which proceeds out of the mouth, this defiles the man.
plain: What goes into a person's mouth does not make them unclean; what comes out of their mouth does.
core_idea: What you say defiles you, not what you eat.

text: If the blind guide the blind, both will fall into a pit.
note: Choosing whom to follow; bad guidance

tags.when_helps: Someone deciding whose guidance to follow who should check that the guide can actually see.

display_text: If the blind guide the blind, both will fall into a pit.
plain: If a blind person leads a blind person, both will fall into a ditch.
core_idea: The blind cannot lead the blind.

text: For what will it profit a man, if he gains the whole world, and forfeits his life? Or what will a man give in exchange for his life?
note: Success and ambition at the cost of your soul

tags.when_helps: Someone chasing success who suspects they may be losing themselves along the way.

display_text: For what will it profit a man, if he gains the whole world, and forfeits his life? Or what will a man give in exchange for his life?
plain: What good is it to win the whole world and lose your own life? What could anyone give in exchange for their life?
core_idea: Gaining the world is worthless if you lose your life.

text: For most certainly I tell you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will tell this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.
note: Facing impossible obstacles; small faith, great results

tags.when_helps: A believer facing something that feels immovable who needs reminding how much even small faith can do.

display_text: For most certainly I tell you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will tell this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.
plain: Jesus said that with faith as small as a mustard seed you could tell a mountain to move and it would move; nothing would be impossible for you.
core_idea: Even tiny faith can move mountains.

text: Most certainly I tell you, unless you turn, and become as little children, you will in no way enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
note: Humility, simplicity and childlike openness

tags.when_helps: Someone whose sophistication has hardened them, invited to recover a childlike openness.

display_text: Most certainly I tell you, unless you turn, and become as little children, you will in no way enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
plain: Jesus said that unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the Kingdom of Heaven.
core_idea: Become like a child to enter the Kingdom.

text: What do you think? If a man has one hundred sheep, and one of them goes astray, doesn’t he leave the ninety-nine, go to the mountains, and seek that which has gone astray? If he finds it, most certainly I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine which have not gone astray.
note: Feeling lost or strayed; being sought and wanted

tags.when_helps: Someone who has strayed or feels forgotten, assured that the one who wandered is sought and rejoiced over.

display_text: What do you think? If a man has one hundred sheep, and one of them goes astray, doesn’t he leave the ninety-nine, go to the mountains, and seek that which has gone astray? If he finds it, most certainly I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine which have not gone astray.
plain: If a man with a hundred sheep loses one, won't he leave the ninety-nine and search the hills for the lost one? And if he finds it, he is happier over that one than over the ninety-nine that never strayed.
core_idea: The one who strays is sought and rejoiced over.

text: If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.
note: Addressing a hurt directly and privately

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone wronged by a sibling or friend unsure how to raise it; go to them privately first.

display_text: If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.
plain: If your brother wrongs you, go and point it out to him privately. If he listens, you have won your brother back.
core_idea: Settle a wrong privately and win your brother back.

text: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?” Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.
note: Forgiving someone who keeps hurting you

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tired of forgiving the same person again and again, asking where the limit lies.

display_text: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?” Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.
plain: Peter asked how many times he should forgive a brother who keeps wronging him, as many as seven? Jesus said not seven times, but seventy times seven.
core_idea: Forgive again and again, without counting.

text: With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.
note: Facing something that feels impossible

keywords: with God all things are possible
tags.when_helps: A believer facing something humanly impossible who needs to lean on trust in God.

display_text: With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.
plain: For people this is impossible, but for God everything is possible.
core_idea: All things are possible with God.

text: You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them. It shall not be so among you, but whoever desires to become great among you shall be your servant. Whoever desires to be first among you shall be your bondservant, even as the Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
note: Ambition, status and leadership as service

tags.when_helps: Someone in or seeking authority who needs to rethink greatness as serving others rather than ruling them.

display_text: You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them. It shall not be so among you, but whoever desires to become great among you shall be your servant. Whoever desires to be first among you shall be your bondservant, even as the Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
plain: Rulers lord it over their people, but not so among you: whoever wants to be great must serve, and whoever wants to be first must be a slave, as the Son of Man came to serve and give his life.
core_idea: Greatness means serving, as the Son of Man served.

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'as a ransom for many' from the Son of Man's giving his life.

text: A man had two sons, and he came to the first, and said, ‘Son, go work today in my vineyard.’ He answered, ‘I will not,’ but afterward he changed his mind, and went. He came to the second, and said the same thing. He answered, ‘I’ m going, sir,’ but he didn’t go. Which of the two did the will of his father?
note: Actions matter more than words; changing your mind

tags.when_helps: Someone who said no but now wants to do the right thing, or who promised and did not follow through.

display_text: A man had two sons, and he came to the first, and said, ‘Son, go work today in my vineyard.’ He answered, ‘I will not,’ but afterward he changed his mind, and went. He came to the second, and said the same thing. He answered, ‘I’m going, sir,’ but he didn’t go. Which of the two did the will of his father?
plain: A father asked two sons to work in his vineyard. The first refused but later changed his mind and went; the second said he would go but never did. Which one did what his father wanted?
core_idea: Doing what is asked matters more than promising.

text: The stone which the builders rejected, the same was made the head of the corner.
note: Being rejected, then proving essential

tags.when_helps: Someone who has been rejected or overlooked, reminded that the rejected can become the cornerstone.

display_text: The stone which the builders rejected, the same was made the head of the corner.
plain: The stone the builders threw away has become the cornerstone.
core_idea: What was rejected becomes the foundation.

text: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the first and great commandment. A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments.
note: What matters most: love of God and neighbour

tags.when_helps: A believer seeking what matters most, given the heart of the law: love God and neighbour.

display_text: ‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the first and great commandment. A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments.
plain: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul and mind; this is the first and greatest commandment. The second is like it: love your neighbour as yourself. All the law and the prophets rest on these two.
core_idea: Love God fully and your neighbour as yourself.

text: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
note: Pride and humility

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to promote themselves, or feeling small, reminded that humility is what truly raises a person.

display_text: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
plain: Whoever lifts themselves up will be brought low, and whoever lowers themselves will be lifted up.
core_idea: The proud are humbled and the humble raised.

text: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets, and stones those who are sent to her! How often I would have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not!
note: Love offered and refused; grief over those who turn away

tags.when_helps: Someone whose love has been refused by people they longed to protect, such as an estranged child.

display_text: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets, and stones those who are sent to her! How often I would have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not!
plain: Jesus grieves over Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets sent to it: how often he longed to gather its children as a hen gathers chicks under her wings, but they would not let him.
core_idea: Love that longs to shelter is refused.

text: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you aren’t troubled, for all this must happen, but the end is not yet.
note: Anxiety about world events and bad news

tags.when_helps: Someone alarmed by frightening world news who needs steadying not to be troubled.

display_text: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you aren’t troubled, for all this must happen, but the end is not yet.
plain: You will hear of wars and rumours of wars. Don't be alarmed; these things must happen, but the end is not yet.
core_idea: Don't be alarmed by wars; the end is not yet.

text: Because iniquity will be multiplied, the love of many will grow cold. But he who endures to the end, the same will be saved.
note: Staying steadfast when the world grows cold

tags.when_helps: Someone disheartened by a hardening world who needs encouragement to endure and keep loving.

display_text: Because iniquity will be multiplied, the love of many will grow cold. But he who endures to the end, the same will be saved.
plain: As wrongdoing spreads, most people's love will grow cold. But whoever holds out to the end will be saved.
core_idea: Endure to the end though love grows cold.

plain_judge.issue: 'The love of many' widened to 'most people's love'.

text: Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.
note: Faithfulness in small tasks; work well done

keywords: well done, good and faithful servant
tags.when_helps: Someone who has worked faithfully at small things and wonders whether it counted.

display_text: Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.
plain: Well done, good and faithful servant. You were trustworthy with a little, so I will put you in charge of much. Come and share your master's joy.
core_idea: Faithfulness in small things leads to greater trust.

text: Then the King will tell those on his right hand, ‘Come, blessed of my Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world; for I was hungry, and you gave me food to eat. I was thirsty, and you gave me drink. I was a stranger, and you took me in. I was naked, and you clothed me. I was sick, and you visited me. I was in prison, and you came to me.’ “Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, and feed you; or thirsty, and give you a drink? When did we see you as a stranger, and take you in; or naked, and clothe you? When did we see you sick, or in prison, and come to you?’ “The King will answer them, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’
note: Caring for strangers, the sick and the poor

situations: caring for a sick or ageing relative
tags.when_helps: Someone caring for the hungry, sick or imprisoned who wonders whether such quiet service matters.

display_text: Then the King will tell those on his right hand, ‘Come, blessed of my Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world; for I was hungry, and you gave me food to eat. I was thirsty, and you gave me drink. I was a stranger, and you took me in. I was naked, and you clothed me. I was sick, and you visited me. I was in prison, and you came to me.’ “Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, and feed you; or thirsty, and give you a drink? When did we see you as a stranger, and take you in; or naked, and clothe you? When did we see you sick, or in prison, and come to you?’ “The King will answer them, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’
plain: The King welcomes those who fed, clothed, sheltered and visited him when he was hungry, a stranger, sick or in prison. When they ask when, he says: whatever you did for the least of my brothers, you did for me.
core_idea: Serving the least of people is serving the King.

text: He went forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
note: facing dread; surrendering to what cannot be avoided

tags.when_helps: A believer dreading something coming who wants it taken away yet seeks to accept what must be.

display_text: He went forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
plain: Jesus went a little farther, fell face down, and prayed: My Father, if it is possible, take this suffering away from me; yet let it be as you want, not as I want.
core_idea: Surrender your own will to God's, even in anguish.

text: Watch and pray, that you don’t enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
note: good intentions undone by weakness

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone who means well but keeps giving in to temptation, needing watchfulness and prayer.

display_text: Watch and pray, that you don’t enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
plain: Stay alert and pray so you don't give in to temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak.
core_idea: The spirit is willing but the flesh is weak.

text: Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back into its place, for all those who take the sword will die by the sword.
note: anger and retaliation breed more violence

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to strike back in anger who needs reminding that violence returns on itself.

display_text: Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back into its place, for all those who take the sword will die by the sword.
plain: Jesus told his follower to put his sword away, because everyone who lives by the sword will die by the sword.
core_idea: Those who take up the sword die by it.

text: About the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lima sabachthani?” That is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
note: feeling abandoned in suffering

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels abandoned by God and needs to know even Jesus cried out this way.

display_text: About the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lima sabachthani?” That is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
plain: Around three in the afternoon Jesus cried out loudly, My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?
core_idea: Even Jesus cried out, feeling abandoned by God.

text: Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.
note: loneliness; reassurance of presence

tags.when_helps: A believer feeling alone or afraid of what lies ahead who needs assurance of constant presence.

display_text: Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.
plain: Jesus promises that he is with you always, to the very end of the age.
core_idea: Jesus is with you always.

text: They will beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, neither will they learn war any more. But they will sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and no one will make them afraid: For the mouth of Yahweh of Armies has spoken.
note: Longing for peace and an end to conflict

keywords: under his vine and fig tree
tags.when_helps: Someone weary of conflict and violence who longs for a vision of peace where no one is afraid.

display_text: They will beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, neither will they learn war any more. But they will sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and no one will make them afraid: For the mouth of Yahweh of Armies has spoken.
plain: People will hammer their swords into ploughs and their spears into pruning tools. Nations will no longer fight or train for war; everyone will sit under their own vine and fig tree, unafraid, for Yahweh of Armies has said so.
core_idea: Yahweh promises a peace where war is unlearned.

text: How shall I come before Yahweh, and bow myself before the exalted God? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old? Will Yahweh be pleased with thousands of rams? With tens of thousands of rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my disobedience? The fruit of my body for the sin of my soul? He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
note: What really matters: justice, mercy, humility over grand gestures

keywords: act justly, love mercy, walk humbly
tags.when_helps: Someone anxious about how to make amends or please God who needs the simple core: justice, mercy and humility.

display_text: How shall I come before Yahweh, and bow myself before the exalted God? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old? Will Yahweh be pleased with thousands of rams? With tens of thousands of rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my disobedience? The fruit of my body for the sin of my soul? He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
plain: How should I approach Yahweh: with burnt offerings, thousands of rams, rivers of oil, even my firstborn child? No. He has shown you what is good: to act justly, love mercy and walk humbly with your God.
core_idea: God asks for justice, mercy and humility, not sacrifices.

text: But as for me, I will look to Yahweh. I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me. Don’t rejoice against me, my enemy. When I fall, I will arise. When I sit in darkness, Yahweh will be a light to me.
note: Getting up after a fall; light in darkness

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
keywords: when I fall, I will arise
tags.when_helps: A believer who has fallen and feels others gloating, who needs to say they will rise again.

display_text: But as for me, I will look to Yahweh. I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me. Don’t rejoice against me, my enemy. When I fall, I will arise. When I sit in darkness, Yahweh will be a light to me.
plain: I will look to Yahweh and wait for the God who saves me; he will hear me. Don't gloat, my enemy: when I fall I will get up, and in darkness Yahweh will be my light.
core_idea: When I fall, I rise; God is my light.

text: Who is a God like you, who pardons iniquity, and passes over the disobedience of the remnant of his heritage? He doesn’t retain his anger forever, because he delights in loving kindness. He will again have compassion on us. He will tread our iniquities under foot; and you will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
note: Guilt and forgiveness; mercy that does not hold grudges

tags.when_helps: A believer burdened by past wrongs who needs to hear that God delights in mercy and casts sins away.

display_text: Who is a God like you, who pardons iniquity, and passes over the disobedience of the remnant of his heritage? He doesn’t retain his anger forever, because he delights in loving kindness. He will again have compassion on us. He will tread our iniquities under foot; and you will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
plain: Who is a God like you, forgiving wrongdoing and overlooking his people's rebellion? He doesn't stay angry forever, because he loves kindness. He will have mercy on us again and throw our sins into the deep sea.
core_idea: God delights in mercy and buries our sins.

text: Yahweh is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knows those who take refuge in him.
note: finding refuge and safety in hard times

keywords: stronghold in the day of trouble
tags.when_helps: A believer in a time of trouble who needs to know God is a refuge who knows them.

display_text: Yahweh is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knows those who take refuge in him.
plain: Yahweh is good, a safe stronghold when trouble comes, and he knows those who take shelter in him.
core_idea: Yahweh is a refuge in times of trouble.

text: The king said to me, “Why is your face sad, since you are not sick? This is nothing else but sorrow of heart.” Then I was very much afraid. I said to the king, “Let the king live forever! Why shouldn’t my face be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers’ tombs, lies waste, and its gates have been consumed with fire?”
note: Grief that shows on the face; sorrow for a ruined home

situations: loss of a home or something valued
tags.when_helps: Someone whose sadness over a lost or ruined homeland shows on their face despite trying to hide it.

display_text: The king said to me, “Why is your face sad, since you are not sick? This is nothing else but sorrow of heart.” Then I was very much afraid. I said to the king, “Let the king live forever! Why shouldn’t my face be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers’ tombs, lies waste, and its gates have been consumed with fire?”
plain: The king asked why I looked sad when I wasn't ill; it must be grief. Terrified, I answered: how could I not be sad when the city of my ancestors' graves lies ruined, its gates burned?
core_idea: Grief for a ruined home shows on the face.

text: Judah said, “The strength of the bearers of burdens is fading, and there is much rubble; so that we are not able to build the wall.”
note: Exhaustion and burnout; the work feels too much

tags.when_helps: Someone worn out midway through a long project who feels there is too much rubble to finish.

display_text: Judah said, “The strength of the bearers of burdens is fading, and there is much rubble; so that we are not able to build the wall.”
plain: The people of Judah said the workers carrying loads were worn out and there was so much rubble that they could not build the wall.
core_idea: Exhaustion and rubble can make the work seem impossible.

text: Remember to me, my God, for good, all that I have done for this people.
note: Feeling unseen or unthanked for service to others

tags.when_helps: A believer whose service to others goes unseen, asking God to remember it.

display_text: Remember to me, my God, for good, all that I have done for this people.
plain: My God, remember me kindly for all I have done for this people.
core_idea: Asking God to remember the good one has done.

text: I am doing a great work, so that I can’t come down. Why should the work cease, while I leave it, and come down to you?
note: Staying focused on important work despite distractions

tags.when_helps: Someone being pulled away from important work by distractions who needs permission to say no.

display_text: I am doing a great work, so that I can’t come down. Why should the work cease, while I leave it, and come down to you?
plain: I am doing important work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it to come to you?
core_idea: Don't abandon important work for distractions.

text: There are no such things done as you say, but you imagine them out of your own heart.
note: Facing false accusations and rumours

tags.when_helps: Someone falsely accused who wants to answer the rumours plainly.

display_text: There are no such things done as you say, but you imagine them out of your own heart.
plain: None of the things you claim have happened; you are making them up in your own mind.
core_idea: Rejecting false accusations as inventions.

text: Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of Yahweh is your strength.
note: Permission to set grief aside and share joy

keywords: the joy of Yahweh is your strength
share with those who have nothing
tags.when_helps: A believer weighed down by sorrow on a day meant for celebration, invited to rejoice and share.

display_text: Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of Yahweh is your strength.
plain: Go and enjoy rich food and sweet drinks, and share with those who have nothing, because today is holy to our Lord. Don't be sad, for the joy of Yahweh is your strength.
core_idea: The joy of Yahweh is your strength.

text: But you are a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and didn’t forsake them.
note: Fear of being unforgivable; mercy after repeated failure

tags.when_helps: A believer who fears they have failed God too often and needs to hear of a God ready to pardon.

display_text: But you are a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and didn’t forsake them.
plain: But you are a God who is ready to forgive, gracious and merciful, slow to anger and full of loving kindness, and you did not abandon them.
core_idea: God is ready to forgive and does not abandon.

text: The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high, who says in his heart, ‘Who will bring me down to the ground?’ Though you mount on high as the eagle, and though your nest is set among the stars, I will bring you down from there,” says Yahweh.
note: pride and the illusion of being untouchable

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling untouchable at the height of success who needs a warning about the fall that follows pride.

display_text: The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high, who says in his heart, ‘Who will bring me down to the ground?’ Though you mount on high as the eagle, and though your nest is set among the stars, I will bring you down from there,” says Yahweh.
plain: Yahweh says your proud heart has fooled you, living high among the rocks and thinking no one can bring you down. Even if you soar like an eagle and nest among the stars, he will bring you down.
core_idea: Pride deceives; God brings the lofty down.

text: But don’t look down on your brother in the day of his disaster, and don’t rejoice over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction. Don’t speak proudly in the day of distress.
note: not gloating over another's misfortune

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to gloat over a rival or sibling's misfortune who needs to check that impulse.

display_text: But don’t look down on your brother in the day of his disaster, and don’t rejoice over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction. Don’t speak proudly in the day of distress.
plain: Don't look down on your brother on the day of his disaster, don't gloat over Judah's people on the day of their ruin, and don't boast when they are in distress.
core_idea: Don't gloat over others in their disaster.

text: Brothers, I don’t regard myself as yet having taken hold, but one thing I do. Forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
note: letting go of the past, pressing forward

tags.when_helps: Someone held back by past mistakes or failures who needs encouragement to let them go and press forward.

display_text: Brothers, I don’t regard myself as yet having taken hold, but one thing I do. Forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
plain: Paul says he has not yet arrived, but he does one thing: forgetting what lies behind and reaching for what lies ahead, he presses on toward the goal, the prize of God's heavenly call in Christ Jesus.
core_idea: Forget what is behind and press on ahead.

text: Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, “Rejoice!” Let your gentleness be known to all men. The Lord is at hand. In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
note: anxiety, worry, finding peace

tags.when_helps: A believer anxious about many things who needs the practice of bringing them to God with thanks.

display_text: Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, “Rejoice!” Let your gentleness be known to all men. The Lord is at hand. In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
plain: Always rejoice in the Lord, and let everyone see your gentleness; the Lord is near. Don't worry about anything, but pray about everything with thanks, and God's peace, beyond understanding, will guard your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.
core_idea: Pray instead of worrying, and God's peace guards you.

text: Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are honorable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report; if there is any virtue, and if there is any praise, think about these things.
note: where to direct the mind

tags.when_helps: Someone whose thoughts keep spiralling toward the negative who needs a list of better things to dwell on.

display_text: Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are honorable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report; if there is any virtue, and if there is any praise, think about these things.
plain: Finally, fill your mind with whatever is true, honourable, just, pure, lovely and well spoken of, whatever is excellent and worthy of praise.
core_idea: Think about what is true, good and lovely.

text: I know how to be humbled, and I know also how to abound. In everything and in all things I have learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need. I can do all things through Christ, who strengthens me.
note: contentment in plenty and in need

tags.when_helps: A believer in a season of plenty or want who wants to learn contentment and strength either way.

display_text: I know how to be humbled, and I know also how to abound. In everything and in all things I have learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need. I can do all things through Christ, who strengthens me.
plain: Paul says he knows how to live with little and with plenty; he has learned the secret of being content whether full or hungry, rich or in need. He can do all things through Christ, who gives him strength.
core_idea: Contentment in plenty or want, through Christ's strength.

text: You, O Lord, according to your great goodness have promised repentance and forgiveness to those who have sinned against you: and of your infinite mercies have appointed repentance to sinners, that they may be saved.
note: Forgiveness is open to those who have done wrong

tags.when_helps: A believer afraid they are beyond forgiveness, needing assurance that repentance is offered to them.

display_text: You, O Lord, according to your great goodness have promised repentance and forgiveness to those who have sinned against you: and of your infinite mercies have appointed repentance to sinners, that they may be saved.
plain: Lord, in your great goodness you have promised repentance and forgiveness to those who have sinned against you, and in your endless mercy you have given sinners the way of repentance so they may be saved.
core_idea: God's mercy offers sinners repentance and forgiveness.

text: I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned, and I acknowledge my iniquities: but, I humbly beseech you, forgive me, O Lord, forgive me, and destroy me not with my iniquities. Be not angry with me forever, by reserving evil for me; neither condemn me into the lower parts of the earth. For you, O Lord, are the God of those who repent; and in me you will show all your goodness: for you will save me, that am unworthy, according to your great mercy.
note: Guilt, admitting wrong, and hoping for mercy

tags.when_helps: A believer crushed by their wrongdoing who wants words to ask God for mercy.

display_text: I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned, and I acknowledge my iniquities: but, I humbly beseech you, forgive me, O Lord, forgive me, and destroy me not with my iniquities. Be not angry with me forever, by reserving evil for me; neither condemn me into the lower parts of the earth. For you, O Lord, are the God of those who repent; and in me you will show all your goodness: for you will save me, that am unworthy, according to your great mercy.
plain: I have sinned, Lord, and I admit my wrongs. I humbly beg you to forgive me and not stay angry forever. You are the God of those who repent, and in your mercy you will save unworthy me.
core_idea: A sinner begs for God's mercy and forgiveness.

plain_judge.issue: Drops pleas not to be destroyed or condemned to the lower parts of the earth.

text: Don’t let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart. So you will find favor, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
note: holding onto kindness and honesty

tags.when_helps: Someone wanting a simple rule to live by: keep kindness and honesty close.

display_text: Don’t let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart. So you will find favor, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
plain: Never let kindness and truth leave you; tie them around your neck and write them on your heart. Then you will win favour and a good name with God and people.
core_idea: Hold fast to kindness and truth.

text: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
note: uncertainty, letting go of control

keywords: lean not on your own understanding
tags.when_helps: A believer overthinking a decision who needs to trust rather than control every step.

display_text: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
plain: Trust Yahweh with all your heart and don't rely on your own understanding. Acknowledge him in everything you do, and he will make your paths straight.
core_idea: Trust God fully, not your own understanding.

text: My son, don’t despise Yahweh’s discipline, neither be weary of his reproof: for whom Yahweh loves, he reproves; even as a father reproves the son in whom he delights.
note: hardship and correction as a form of love

tags.when_helps: A believer weary of correction or hardship, invited to see it as a sign of love.

display_text: My son, don’t despise Yahweh’s discipline, neither be weary of his reproof: for whom Yahweh loves, he reproves; even as a father reproves the son in whom he delights.
plain: My son, don't reject Yahweh's discipline or resent his correction, because Yahweh corrects those he loves, as a father corrects the son he delights in.
core_idea: God corrects those he loves.

text: Happy is the man who finds wisdom, the man who gets understanding. For her good profit is better than getting silver, and her return is better than fine gold. She is more precious than rubies. None of the things you can desire are to be compared to her. Length of days is in her right hand. In her left hand are riches and honor. Her ways are ways of pleasantness. All her paths are peace. She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her. Happy is everyone who retains her.
note: wisdom valued above wealth

tags.when_helps: Someone chasing wealth or status who wants to weigh it against the worth of wisdom.

display_text: Happy is the man who finds wisdom, the man who gets understanding. For her good profit is better than getting silver, and her return is better than fine gold. She is more precious than rubies. None of the things you can desire are to be compared to her. Length of days is in her right hand. In her left hand are riches and honor. Her ways are ways of pleasantness. All her paths are peace. She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her. Happy is everyone who retains her.
plain: Happy is the one who finds wisdom. She is worth more than silver, gold or rubies, more than anything you could want. She brings long life, riches, honour and peace, a tree of life to those who hold her.
core_idea: Wisdom is worth more than any riches.

text: Don’t be afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it comes: for Yahweh will be your confidence, and will keep your foot from being taken.
note: sudden fear and anxiety

tags.when_helps: A believer seized by sudden fear of disaster who needs a steady confidence.

display_text: Don’t be afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it comes: for Yahweh will be your confidence, and will keep your foot from being taken.
plain: Don't be afraid of sudden terror or of the ruin that comes on the wicked, because Yahweh will be your confidence and keep your foot from being caught.
core_idea: Don't fear sudden terror; God keeps you safe.

text: Don’t withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it. Don’t say to your neighbor, “Go, and come again; tomorrow I will give it to you,” when you have it by you.
note: generosity now, not putting off kindness

tags.when_helps: Someone putting off helping or repaying another when they could act now.

display_text: Don’t withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it. Don’t say to your neighbor, “Go, and come again; tomorrow I will give it to you,” when you have it by you.
plain: Don't hold back good from those who deserve it when you are able to give it. Don't tell your neighbour to come back tomorrow when you have it with you now.
core_idea: Do good now when you are able.

text: Don’t strive with a man without cause, if he has done you no harm. Don’t envy the man of violence. Choose none of his ways.
note: needless quarrels and envy

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to pick a needless quarrel or admire people who get ahead by force.

display_text: Don’t strive with a man without cause, if he has done you no harm. Don’t envy the man of violence. Choose none of his ways.
plain: Don't quarrel with someone for no reason when they have done you no harm. Don't envy a violent person or copy any of their ways.
core_idea: Avoid needless quarrels and don't envy the violent.

text: But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light, that shines more and more until the perfect day. The way of the wicked is like darkness. They don’t know what they stumble over.
note: choosing the right path

tags.when_helps: Someone trying to live rightly who needs a picture of growth that brightens over time.

display_text: But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light, that shines more and more until the perfect day. The way of the wicked is like darkness. They don’t know what they stumble over.
plain: The path of the righteous is like the first light of dawn, growing brighter until full day. The way of the wicked is like darkness; they don't even know what trips them up.
core_idea: The righteous path grows brighter; the wicked stumble.

text: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life. Put away from yourself a perverse mouth. Put corrupt lips far from you. Let your eyes look straight ahead. Fix your gaze directly before you.
note: guarding the heart, staying focused

tags.when_helps: Someone distracted and pulled sideways who needs to guard their heart and focus ahead.

display_text: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life. Put away from yourself a perverse mouth. Put corrupt lips far from you. Let your eyes look straight ahead. Fix your gaze directly before you.
plain: Guard your heart above all, because your whole life flows from it. Keep crooked and corrupt talk far from you. Keep your eyes looking straight ahead and fix your gaze on what is before you.
core_idea: Guard your heart; life flows from it.

text: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise; which having no chief, overseer, or ruler, provides her bread in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest. How long will you sleep, sluggard? When will you arise out of your sleep? A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep: so your poverty will come as a robber, and your scarcity as an armed man.
note: procrastination and laziness

tags.when_helps: Someone procrastinating or drifting who needs a firm nudge to start working.

display_text: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise; which having no chief, overseer, or ruler, provides her bread in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest. How long will you sleep, sluggard? When will you arise out of your sleep? A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep: so your poverty will come as a robber, and your scarcity as an armed man.
plain: Lazy one, go watch the ant and learn: with no boss, she stores food in summer and harvest. How long will you sleep? A little more sleep and rest, and poverty will come on you like a robber.
core_idea: Learn diligence from the ant, or poverty comes.

text: Can a man scoop fire into his lap, and his clothes not be burned? Or can one walk on hot coals, and his feet not be scorched? So is he who goes in to his neighbor’s wife. Whoever touches her will not be unpunished.
note: temptation and inevitable consequences

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted toward something they know will burn them, needing a blunt reminder of consequences.

display_text: Can a man scoop fire into his lap, and his clothes not be burned? Or can one walk on hot coals, and his feet not be scorched? So is he who goes in to his neighbor’s wife. Whoever touches her will not be unpunished.
plain: Can a man carry fire in his lap without burning his clothes, or walk on hot coals without scorching his feet? So it is with the man who sleeps with his neighbour's wife: he will not go unpunished.
core_idea: Adultery, like playing with fire, brings harm.

text: He who corrects a mocker invites insult. He who reproves a wicked man invites abuse. Don’t reprove a scoffer, lest he hate you. Reprove a wise man, and he will love you. Instruct a wise man, and he will be still wiser. Teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning.
note: giving and receiving criticism

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone frustrated that their advice keeps being rejected, deciding whether correcting another person is worth it.

display_text: He who corrects a mocker invites insult. He who reproves a wicked man invites abuse. Don’t reprove a scoffer, lest he hate you. Reprove a wise man, and he will love you. Instruct a wise man, and he will be still wiser. Teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning.
plain: Correcting a mocker or a wicked person only gets you insults and abuse, and the scoffer will hate you. Correct a wise person and they will love you; teach the wise and righteous and they will grow wiser still.
core_idea: The wise welcome correction; mockers resent it.

text: He who walks blamelessly walks surely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.
note: integrity versus deceit

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to cut a corner, or uneasy about something hidden, weighing the security of honest conduct.

display_text: He who walks blamelessly walks surely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.
plain: Whoever lives with integrity walks securely, but whoever takes crooked paths will be found out.
core_idea: Integrity is secure; crookedness gets exposed.

text: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.
note: resentment, forgiveness in relationships

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone caught in a feud who keeps stirring it, needing a reminder that love can cover wrongs.

display_text: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.
plain: Hatred stirs up fights, but love covers over every wrong.
core_idea: Love covers all wrongs; hatred stirs strife.

text: In the multitude of words there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his lips does wisely.
note: talking too much, holding one's tongue

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone who tends to say too much in heated moments and wants to learn restraint in speech.

display_text: In the multitude of words there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his lips does wisely.
plain: Where there are many words, wrongdoing is never far away, but whoever holds their tongue is wise.
core_idea: Too many words lead to wrong; restraint is wise.

text: When pride comes, then comes shame, but with humility comes wisdom.
note: pride and humility

tags.when_helps: Someone riding high on success or recently humbled after overreaching, reflecting on pride and humility.

display_text: When pride comes, then comes shame, but with humility comes wisdom.
plain: Pride is followed by shame, but humility brings wisdom.
core_idea: Pride brings shame; humility brings wisdom.

text: One who despises his neighbor is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding holds his peace. One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one who is of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.
note: gossip, contempt, keeping confidences

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to gossip or belittle a neighbour or colleague, deciding to hold their tongue.

display_text: One who despises his neighbor is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding holds his peace. One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one who is of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.
plain: Whoever looks down on their neighbour lacks sense, but a person of understanding stays quiet. A gossip betrays secrets, but a trustworthy person keeps them.
core_idea: The wise stay quiet and keep confidences.

text: Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the multitude of counselors there is victory.
note: seeking advice before decisions

tags.when_helps: Someone facing a big decision alone who needs encouragement to seek advice from several people.

display_text: Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the multitude of counselors there is victory.
plain: Without wise guidance a nation falls, but with many advisers comes victory.
core_idea: Many good advisers bring success.

text: The merciful man does good to his own soul, but he who is cruel troubles his own flesh.
note: kindness benefits the giver

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to be harsh, reminded that mercy benefits the giver and cruelty harms oneself.

display_text: The merciful man does good to his own soul, but he who is cruel troubles his own flesh.
plain: A merciful person does good to their own soul, but a cruel person brings trouble on their own body.
core_idea: Mercy benefits yourself; cruelty harms yourself.

text: There is one who scatters, and increases yet more. There is one who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains poverty. The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.
note: generosity versus stinginess

tags.when_helps: Someone holding tightly to what they have out of fear, considering whether to give more generously.

display_text: There is one who scatters, and increases yet more. There is one who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains poverty. The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.
plain: Some give freely and grow richer; others hold back more than they should and end up poor. A generous person will prosper, and whoever refreshes others will be refreshed.
core_idea: Generosity enriches; stinginess impoverishes.

text: A fool shows his annoyance the same day, but one who overlooks an insult is prudent.
note: being insulted, choosing not to react

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone stung by an insult today, wanting to react, who could choose to let it pass.

display_text: A fool shows his annoyance the same day, but one who overlooks an insult is prudent.
plain: A fool shows their irritation at once, but a sensible person ignores an insult.
core_idea: The prudent overlook insults.

text: There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
note: hurtful words versus healing words

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone who spoke rashly and hurt someone, or is about to, reflecting on the power of words to wound or heal.

display_text: There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
plain: Careless words can cut like a sword, but the words of the wise bring healing.
core_idea: Rash words wound; wise words heal.

text: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
note: anxiety and the power of kindness

tags.when_helps: Someone weighed down by worry, or wanting to help an anxious friend with a kind word.

display_text: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
plain: Worry weighs a person's heart down, but a kind word lifts it up.
core_idea: A kind word lifts an anxious heart.

text: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.
note: waiting, disappointment, longing

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone sick at heart from waiting for something that keeps not arriving.

display_text: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.
plain: Hope that keeps being put off makes the heart sick, but a longing that comes true is like a tree of life.
core_idea: Delayed hope sickens; fulfilled longing gives life.

text: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
note: choosing friends and influences

tags.when_helps: Someone reconsidering the company they keep, wanting friends who help them grow.

display_text: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
plain: Spend time with wise people and you become wise; keep company with fools and you get hurt.
core_idea: You become like the company you keep.

text: The heart knows its own bitterness and joy; he will not share these with a stranger.
note: private grief no one else fully sees

keywords: the heart knows its own bitterness
tags.when_helps: Someone feeling that no one else can fully understand what they carry inside.

display_text: The heart knows its own bitterness and joy; he will not share these with a stranger.
plain: Only your own heart knows its bitterness and its joy; no stranger can share them.
core_idea: Each heart knows its own sorrow and joy.

text: Even in laughter the heart may be sorrowful, and mirth may end in heaviness.
note: hidden sadness behind a smile

tags.when_helps: Someone smiling on the outside while sad inside, who needs to know this is a common human experience.

display_text: Even in laughter the heart may be sorrowful, and mirth may end in heaviness.
plain: Even while laughing, the heart can be sad, and joy can end in grief.
core_idea: Laughter can hide a sorrowful heart.

text: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.
note: envy and inner peace

tags.when_helps: Someone eaten up by envy of another's life, reminded that a peaceful heart is the real health.

display_text: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.
plain: A peaceful heart gives life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
core_idea: A peaceful heart gives life; envy rots.

text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
note: defusing conflict

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone about to respond to an angry person, choosing how to answer without escalating.

display_text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
plain: A gentle answer calms anger, but a harsh word stirs it up.
core_idea: Gentle answers calm anger; harsh words inflame it.

text: Better is little, with the fear of Yahweh, than great treasure with trouble. Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, than a fattened calf with hatred.
note: love and peace over wealth

tags.when_helps: Someone with little money who worries it matters most, reminded that love outweighs abundance.

display_text: Better is little, with the fear of Yahweh, than great treasure with trouble. Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, than a fattened calf with hatred.
plain: Better to have little and revere Yahweh than great wealth with trouble. Better a simple meal of vegetables where there is love than a feast of fattened beef with hatred.
core_idea: Little with love beats plenty with strife.

text: A man’s heart plans his course, but Yahweh directs his steps.
note: plans versus what actually happens

tags.when_helps: A believer anxious that their plans may fail, invited to trust that God guides their path.

display_text: A man’s heart plans his course, but Yahweh directs his steps.
plain: A person plans their route in their heart, but Yahweh guides their steps.
core_idea: We make plans, but God directs our steps.

text: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
note: pride and its consequences

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling invincible after success who needs a warning about arrogance.

display_text: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
plain: Pride comes before ruin, and an arrogant spirit before a fall.
core_idea: Pride comes before a fall.

text: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
note: the effect of kind words

tags.when_helps: Someone wondering whether kind words to a struggling person really make a difference.

display_text: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
plain: Kind words are like honey: sweet to the soul and healing to the body.
core_idea: Kind words are sweet and healing.

text: Gray hair is a crown of glory. It is attained by a life of righteousness.
note: ageing with dignity

tags.when_helps: Someone uneasy about growing older, reminded that a life well lived makes age a crown.

display_text: Gray hair is a crown of glory. It is attained by a life of righteousness.
plain: Grey hair is a crown of honour, earned by living rightly.
core_idea: Grey hair honours a righteous life.

text: One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than he who takes a city.
note: anger and self-control

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone struggling with a quick temper, reminded that mastering oneself is greater strength than conquest.

display_text: One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than he who takes a city.
plain: Someone slow to anger is better than a warrior, and someone who controls their temper is better than one who captures a city.
core_idea: Self-control is greater than conquest.

text: He who covers an offense promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.
note: forgiving friends, not dwelling on offences

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to keep bringing up a friend's offence, weighing whether to let it go.

display_text: He who covers an offense promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.
plain: Whoever lets an offence go builds love, but whoever keeps bringing it up drives close friends apart.
core_idea: Forgiving offences builds love; repeating them divides.

text: The beginning of strife is like breaching a dam, therefore stop contention before quarreling breaks out.
note: stopping an argument before it escalates

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone feeling an argument about to start, wanting to stop it before it breaks loose.

display_text: The beginning of strife is like breaching a dam, therefore stop contention before quarreling breaks out.
plain: Starting a quarrel is like breaking open a dam, so stop the argument before it bursts out.
core_idea: Stop a quarrel before it breaks loose.

text: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
note: true friendship in hard times

tags.when_helps: Someone going through hard times who wants to remember the worth of loyal friends and family.

display_text: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
plain: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born to help in hard times.
core_idea: True friends and family stand by you in trouble.

text: A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
note: mood and wellbeing

tags.when_helps: Someone whose low spirits are wearing them down, reminded that cheerfulness is a kind of medicine.

display_text: A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
plain: A cheerful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones.
core_idea: A cheerful heart is good medicine.

text: He who spares his words has knowledge. He who is even tempered is a man of understanding. Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise. When he shuts his lips, he is thought to be discerning.
note: the wisdom of saying less

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels pressure to speak up and react, reminded that calm restraint shows understanding.

display_text: He who spares his words has knowledge. He who is even tempered is a man of understanding. Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise. When he shuts his lips, he is thought to be discerning.
plain: Someone who holds back their words has knowledge, and someone calm has understanding. Even a fool who keeps quiet is taken for wise, and seems sensible when they keep their mouth shut.
core_idea: Restraint in speech shows wisdom.

text: He who gives answer before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
note: listening before responding

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone who tends to answer before fully listening, wanting to hear others out first.

display_text: He who gives answer before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
plain: Answering before you have listened is foolish and shameful.
core_idea: Listen before you answer.

text: A man’s spirit will sustain him in sickness, but a crushed spirit, who can bear?
note: illness and a broken spirit

tags.when_helps: Someone ill or struggling whose spirit feels crushed, recognising that inner strength carries the body.

display_text: A man’s spirit will sustain him in sickness, but a crushed spirit, who can bear?
plain: A person's spirit can carry them through illness, but who can bear a crushed spirit?
core_idea: A strong spirit sustains; a crushed one is unbearable.

text: He who pleads his cause first seems right; until another comes and questions him.
note: hearing both sides of a dispute

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone convinced they are right after hearing only one side, reminded to hear the other.

display_text: He who pleads his cause first seems right; until another comes and questions him.
plain: The first to state their case seems right, until someone else comes and questions them.
core_idea: Hear both sides before judging.

text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; those who love it will eat its fruit.
note: the weight of what we say

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone reflecting on how their words shape relationships and outcomes.

display_text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; those who love it will eat its fruit.
plain: The tongue holds the power of life and death, and those who love to talk will live with the results.
core_idea: Words hold the power of life and death.

text: A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

tags.when_helps: Someone with many acquaintances but few true friends, valuing one loyal friend.

display_text: A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
plain: Someone with many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.
core_idea: One true friend outweighs many companions.

text: It isn’t good to have zeal without knowledge; nor being hasty with one’s feet and missing the way.

tags.when_helps: Someone eager to rush into something new who would benefit from slowing down and learning first.

display_text: It isn’t good to have zeal without knowledge; nor being hasty with one’s feet and missing the way.
plain: Eagerness without knowledge is not good, and rushing ahead makes you lose your way.
core_idea: Zeal without knowledge leads astray.

text: All the relatives of the poor shun him: how much more do his friends avoid him! He pursues them with pleas, but they are gone.

display_text: All the relatives of the poor shun him: how much more do his friends avoid him! He pursues them with pleas, but they are gone.
plain: All the relatives of a poor man avoid him, and his friends keep even further away. He chases after them pleading, but they are gone.
core_idea: The poor are abandoned by family and friends.

text: The discretion of a man makes him slow to anger. It is his glory to overlook an offense.

tags.when_helps: Someone wronged and angry, invited to see letting an offence pass as strength, not weakness.

display_text: The discretion of a man makes him slow to anger. It is his glory to overlook an offense.

core_idea: It is noble to overlook an offence.

text: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.

display_text: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.

core_idea: The wise draw out what lies deep in hearts.

display_text: Who can say, “I have made my heart pure. I am clean and without sin?”
plain: Who can claim to have made their heart pure and to be clean and free of sin?
core_idea: No one can claim to be free of sin.

text: Don’t say, “I will pay back evil.” Wait for Yahweh, and he will save you.

plain: Don't say you will get even for a wrong. Wait for Yahweh, and he will rescue you.
core_idea: Don't take revenge; wait for God.

text: The glory of young men is their strength. The splendor of old men is their gray hair.
note: youth and ageing each have worth

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling their age, reminded that each stage of life has its own splendour.

display_text: The glory of young men is their strength. The splendor of old men is their gray hair.
plain: The pride of young men is their strength, and the honour of old men is their grey hair.
core_idea: Youth has strength; age has honour.

text: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.
note: reputation and character over wealth

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to trade their integrity for money, weighing what is truly valuable.

display_text: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.
plain: A good name is worth more than great wealth, and being well regarded is better than silver or gold.
core_idea: A good name is worth more than riches.

text: Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man, and don’t associate with one who harbors anger: lest you learn his ways, and ensnare your soul.

tags.when_helps: Someone drawn into the orbit of an angry person, considering how their company shapes them.

display_text: Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man, and don’t associate with one who harbors anger: lest you learn his ways, and ensnare your soul.
plain: Don't make friends with a hot-tempered or angry person, or you may pick up their ways and trap yourself.
core_idea: Avoid angry people, or you'll become like them.

text: Don’t weary yourself to be rich. In your wisdom, show restraint. Why do you set your eyes on that which is not? For it certainly sprouts wings like an eagle and flies in the sky.

tags.when_helps: Someone wearing themselves out chasing wealth, reminded how quickly riches fly away.

plain: Don't wear yourself out trying to get rich; be wise enough to hold back. Why fix your eyes on wealth that is gone in a moment? It sprouts wings and flies off like an eagle.
core_idea: Riches fly away; don't exhaust yourself chasing them.

text: Don’t let your heart envy sinners; but rather fear Yahweh all day long. Indeed surely there is a future hope, and your hope will not be cut off.
note: envying those who prosper unfairly

keywords: your hope will not be cut off
tags.when_helps: A believer envious of people who prosper by doing wrong, reassured that their hope is secure.

display_text: Don’t let your heart envy sinners; but rather fear Yahweh all day long. Indeed surely there is a future hope, and your hope will not be cut off.
plain: Don't envy sinners in your heart; keep revering Yahweh all day long. There truly is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
core_idea: Don't envy sinners; your hope has a future.

text: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes? Those who stay long at the wine; those who go to seek out mixed wine. Don’t look at the wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly. In the end, it bites like a snake, and poisons like a viper.
note: drinking problems and their cost

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone struggling with drinking, facing honestly what it costs them.

display_text: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes? Those who stay long at the wine; those who go to seek out mixed wine. Don’t look at the wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly. In the end, it bites like a snake, and poisons like a viper.

core_idea: Heavy drinking brings misery and bites like a snake.

text: Don’t lay in wait, wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous. Don’t destroy his resting place: for a righteous man falls seven times, and rises up again; but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
note: resilience, getting up after falling

tags.when_helps: Someone knocked down again and again who needs encouragement to rise once more.

display_text: Don’t lay in wait, wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous. Don’t destroy his resting place: for a righteous man falls seven times, and rises up again; but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
plain: Wicked man, don't lie in wait to attack the home of the righteous, because a righteous person falls seven times and gets up again, but the wicked are brought down by disaster.
core_idea: The righteous fall seven times and rise again.

text: Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls. Don’t let your heart be glad when he is overthrown; lest Yahweh see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
note: gloating over an enemy's misfortune

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to rejoice when a rival or enemy falls.

display_text: Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls. Don’t let your heart be glad when he is overthrown; lest Yahweh see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
plain: Don't celebrate when your enemy falls or be glad when he is brought down, or Yahweh may see it, be displeased, and turn his anger away from him.
core_idea: Don't rejoice when your enemy falls.

text: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
note: the right words at the right time

tags.when_helps: Someone thinking about the right words to say to someone, reminded of their value.

display_text: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
plain: A word spoken at the right moment is like golden apples set in silver.
core_idea: A well-timed word is precious.

text: As one who takes away a garment in cold weather, or vinegar on soda, so is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
note: comforting someone who is grieving

tags.when_helps: Someone hurt by forced cheerfulness from others, or wanting to comfort a grieving friend well.

display_text: As one who takes away a garment in cold weather, or vinegar on soda, so is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
plain: Singing cheerful songs to someone with a heavy heart is like taking away their coat on a cold day, or pouring vinegar on soda.
core_idea: Cheerfulness forced on the grieving hurts them.

text: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink: for you will heap coals of fire on his head, and Yahweh will reward you.
note: kindness toward an enemy

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone with an enemy, challenged to answer hostility with kindness.

display_text: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink: for you will heap coals of fire on his head, and Yahweh will reward you.
plain: If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him water. In doing so you heap burning coals on his head, and Yahweh will reward you.
core_idea: Answer your enemy's need with kindness.

text: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.

tags.when_helps: Someone who keeps losing control of their impulses and wants to build self-restraint.

display_text: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
plain: A person who cannot control themselves is as defenceless as a city whose walls have been torn down.
core_idea: Without self-control, a person is defenceless

text: For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.

tags.when_helps: Someone caught in an ongoing quarrel fed by talk behind backs, wanting it to die down.

display_text: For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
plain: A fire dies when it runs out of wood, and a quarrel dies down when no one keeps gossiping.
core_idea: Gossip feeds quarrels; without it they end

text: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.

display_text: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.
plain: Don't brag about what you'll do tomorrow, because you have no idea what the day will bring.
core_idea: Tomorrow is unknown, so don't boast about it

text: Better is open rebuke than hidden love. Faithful are the wounds of a friend; although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
note: honest friends versus flatterers

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone hurt by a friend's honest criticism, seeing it as a sign of real care.

display_text: Better is open rebuke than hidden love. Faithful are the wounds of a friend; although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
plain: Honest correction said openly is better than love kept hidden. A friend's wounding words can be trusted, while an enemy's many kisses cannot.
core_idea: A friend's honest rebuke beats an enemy's flattery

text: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.

tags.when_helps: Someone far from home feeling unmoored and homesick.

display_text: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.
plain: A man who strays from his home is like a bird that has wandered away from its nest.
core_idea: Leaving home leaves a person unsettled and exposed

text: Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster: better is a neighbor who is near than a distant brother.

tags.when_helps: Someone in trouble whose family is distant, valuing the friends and neighbours close at hand.

display_text: Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster: better is a neighbor who is near than a distant brother.
plain: Don't abandon your friends or your family's old friends. When disaster hits, a neighbour close by is more help than a brother far away.
core_idea: A near neighbour helps more than distant kin

plain_judge.issue: Drops the warning not to go to your brother's house in the day of disaster.

text: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
note: friends who make each other better

tags.when_helps: Someone grateful for a friend who challenges them to grow.

display_text: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
plain: Just as one piece of iron sharpens another, people sharpen and improve each other.
core_idea: Friends sharpen each other

text: Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man. Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.

display_text: Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man. Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.
plain: As water shows you your face, your heart shows who you really are. Death and the grave are never satisfied, and neither are human eyes.
core_idea: The heart reveals the person; desire never ends

text: The wicked flee when no one pursues; but the righteous are as bold as a lion.

display_text: The wicked flee when no one pursues; but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
plain: Wrongdoers run away even when no one is chasing them, but people who do right are as bold as a lion.
core_idea: A clear conscience makes a person bold

display_text: He who conceals his sins doesn’t prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.
plain: If you hide your wrongdoing you won't do well, but if you admit it and turn away from it, you will find mercy.
core_idea: Confessing wrongs brings mercy; hiding them doesn't

tags.when_helps: Someone about to unload their anger on someone, choosing to hold it in check.

plain: A fool lets all their anger out, but a wise person keeps themselves under control.

text: The fear of man proves to be a snare, but whoever puts his trust in Yahweh is kept safe.

text: “Two things I have asked of you; don’t deny me before I die: Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches. tags.when_helps: A believer anxious about money who wants only enough, and honesty, not wealth.

display_text: Two things I have asked of you; don’t deny me before I die: Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with the food that is needful for me; lest I be full, deny you, and say, ‘Who is Yahweh?’ or lest I be poor, and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.
plain: The speaker asks God for two things before dying: keep lies far away, and give neither poverty nor wealth, just enough, so that riches don't lead to forgetting God or need to stealing.
core_idea: Ask for enough, neither poverty nor riches
