display_text: Don’t say, I shall be hidden from the Lord; And who will remember me from on high? I will not be known among so many people; For what is my soul in a boundless creation?
plain: Don't tell yourself you can hide from the Lord, that no one up there will remember you, that you'll be lost among so many people, or that your soul counts for nothing in a boundless creation.
core_idea: Don't think you're too small for God to notice

text: When a man has finished, then he is but at the beginning; And when he ceaseth, then will he be in perplexity. What is man, and whereto serves he? What is his good, and what is his evil? The number of man’s days at the most are a hundred years. As a drop of water from the sea, and a pebble from the sand; So are a few years in the day of eternity.
note: Brevity of life; questioning purpose and meaning

keywords: a drop of water from the sea
tags.when_helps: Someone wondering what a human life amounts to against eternity.

display_text: When a man has finished, then he is but at the beginning; And when he ceaseth, then will he be in perplexity. What is man, and whereto serves he? What is his good, and what is his evil? The number of man’s days at the most are a hundred years. As a drop of water from the sea, and a pebble from the sand; So are a few years in the day of eternity.
plain: When a person thinks they've finished, they are only beginning. What is a human, and what is their good or evil? A hundred years at most: a drop from the sea against eternity.
core_idea: A lifetime is a drop against eternity

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'when he ceases, he will be in perplexity' and the pebble image.

text: The mercy of a man is upon his neighbor; But the mercy of the Lord is upon all flesh; Reproving, and chastening, and teaching, And bringing again, as a shepherd does his flock.
note: Mercy that reaches everyone; being brought back

tags.when_helps: A believer who has strayed, reassured that divine mercy reaches all and brings them back.

display_text: The mercy of a man is upon his neighbor; But the mercy of the Lord is upon all flesh; Reproving, and chastening, and teaching, And bringing again, as a shepherd does his flock.
plain: A person's mercy reaches their neighbour, but the Lord's mercy reaches every living being; he corrects, disciplines and teaches, and brings people back like a shepherd with his flock.
core_idea: God's mercy shepherds everyone

text: My son, to your good deeds add no blemish; And no grief of words in any of your giving. Shall not the dew assuage the scorching heat? So is a word better than a gift. Behold, is not a word better than a gift? And both are with a gracious man.
note: Kind words matter more than gifts

keywords: a word better than a gift
tags.when_helps: Someone helping others who wants to give without grudging words, knowing kindness of speech matters.

display_text: My son, to your good deeds add no blemish; And no grief of words in any of your giving. Shall not the dew assuage the scorching heat? So is a word better than a gift. Behold, is not a word better than a gift? And both are with a gracious man.
plain: Don't spoil your good deeds or hurt people with words when you give. As dew cools scorching heat, a kind word is worth more than a gift, and a gracious person offers both.
core_idea: A kind word is better than a gift

text: In the days of fulness remember the time of hunger, And poverty and lack in the days of wealth. From morning until evening the time changes; And all things are speedy before the Lord.
note: Remembering hard times in good times; change comes fast

tags.when_helps: Someone in good times, or hard ones, reminded that fortunes change between morning and evening.

display_text: In the days of fulness remember the time of hunger, And poverty and lack in the days of wealth. From morning until evening the time changes; And all things are speedy before the Lord.
plain: When you have plenty, remember hunger; when you are wealthy, remember poverty and need. Things change between morning and evening, and everything passes quickly before the Lord.
core_idea: In plenty, remember want; things change fast

text: Hast you heard a word? let it die with you: Be of good courage, it will not burst you.
note: Keeping a confidence; resisting the urge to gossip

tags.when_helps: Someone itching to pass on gossip or a secret, reassured they can hold it in.

display_text: Hast you heard a word? let it die with you: Be of good courage, it will not burst you.
plain: Have you heard something said? Let it die with you. Take heart: keeping it won't make you burst.
core_idea: Keep what you hear to yourself

text: Reprove a friend; it may be he did it not: And if he did something, that he may do it no more. Reprove your neighbor; it may be he said it not: And if he has said it, that he may not say it again. Reprove a friend; for many times there is slander: And trust not every word. There is one that slips, and not from the heart: And who is he that has not sinned with his tongue?
note: Hurt by a friend; talk to them before believing rumours

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone hurt by what they heard about a friend, counselled to ask before assuming the worst.

display_text: Reprove a friend; it may be he did it not: And if he did something, that he may do it no more. Reprove your neighbor; it may be he said it not: And if he has said it, that he may not say it again. Reprove a friend; for many times there is slander: And trust not every word. There is one that slips, and not from the heart: And who is he that has not sinned with his tongue?
plain: If you hear something against a friend, ask them: perhaps they didn't do or say it, and if they did, they may stop. Slander is common, so don't believe every word; who has never slipped with their tongue?
core_idea: Ask a friend before believing what you hear

plain_judge.issue: 'Reprove' softened to 'ask'; adds a hearsay framing not in the passage.

text: There is one that keeps silence, and is found wise; And there is one that is hated for his much talk. There is one that keeps silence, for he has no answer to make; And there is that keeps silence, as knowing his time. A wise man will be silent till his time come; But the braggart and fool will overpass his time.
note: When to stay silent and when to speak

tags.when_helps: Someone unsure when to speak and when to stay quiet.

display_text: There is one that keeps silence, and is found wise; And there is one that is hated for his much talk. There is one that keeps silence, for he has no answer to make; And there is that keeps silence, as knowing his time. A wise man will be silent till his time come; But the braggart and fool will overpass his time.
plain: Some keep silent and are thought wise; others are disliked for talking too much. Some are silent for lack of an answer, others because they know their moment. The wise wait; the boaster and fool don't.
core_idea: The wise keep silent until the right time

text: There is a prosperity that a man finds in misfortunes; And there is a gain that turns to loss. There is a gift that will not profit you; And there is a gift whose recompense is double. There is an abasement because of glory; And there is that has lifted up his head from a low estate.
note: Misfortune that turns to good; success that turns to loss

tags.when_helps: Someone after a setback, reminded that losses and gains often turn out the reverse of how they look.

display_text: There is a prosperity that a man finds in misfortunes; And there is a gain that turns to loss. There is a gift that will not profit you; And there is a gift whose recompense is double. There is an abasement because of glory; And there is that has lifted up his head from a low estate.
plain: Some people find good fortune in misfortune, and some gains turn into losses. Some gifts bring no benefit, others pay back double. Some are brought low by glory, and some rise from a low place.
core_idea: Fortune and misfortune often reverse

text: My son, have you sinned? add no more thereto; And make supplication for your former sins.
note: After a wrong: stop, and seek forgiveness

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone who has done wrong and needs the simple next step: stop adding to it and seek forgiveness.

display_text: My son, have you sinned? add no more thereto; And make supplication for your former sins.
plain: Have you sinned? Don't add more to it, and pray to be forgiven for what you've already done.
core_idea: After sinning, stop and seek forgiveness

text: If a man of knowledge hear a wise word, He will commend it, and add to it: The dissolute man hears it, and it displeases him, And he puts it away behind his back.
note: Receiving advice or criticism openly

tags.when_helps: Someone given good advice they dislike, invited to receive and build on it instead of dismissing it.

display_text: If a man of knowledge hear a wise word, He will commend it, and add to it: The dissolute man hears it, and it displeases him, And he puts it away behind his back.
plain: When a thoughtful person hears a wise saying, they praise it and build on it. When a careless person hears it, they dislike it and toss it behind their back.
core_idea: The wise welcome wisdom; the careless discard it

text: The heart of fools is in their mouth; But the mouth of wise men is their heart.
note: Speaking impulsively versus speaking from the heart

tags.when_helps: Someone who speaks before thinking, reminded that the wise let the heart guide the tongue.

display_text: The heart of fools is in their mouth; But the mouth of wise men is their heart.
plain: Fools have their heart in their mouth, but the wise keep their mouth in their heart.
core_idea: Fools blurt; the wise speak from the heart

text: Weep for the dead, for light has failed him; And weep for a fool, for understanding has failed him: Weep more sweetly for the dead, because he has found rest; But the life of the fool is worse than death.
note: Mourning the dead; they have found rest

tags.safety_reason: Says the dead have found rest and that a fool's life is worse than death, presenting death as a release.
tags.when_helps: Someone mourning who is reflecting on what is truly worth grieving, including wasted lives.

display_text: Weep for the dead, for light has failed him; And weep for a fool, for understanding has failed him: Weep more sweetly for the dead, because he has found rest; But the life of the fool is worse than death.
plain: Weep for the dead, who have lost the light, and weep for a fool, who has lost understanding. Weep more gently for the dead, because they are at rest; a fool's life is worse than death.
core_idea: A fool's life is worse than death

text: Timber girded and bound into a building will not be loosed with shaking: So a heart established in due season on well advised counsel will not be afraid. A heart settled upon a thoughtful understanding Is as an ornament of plaister on a polished wall. Pales set on a high place will not stand against the wind: So a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool will not stand against any fear.
note: Fear and anxiety; a settled heart withstands shaking

tags.when_helps: Someone easily shaken by fear who wants a heart settled on sound thinking.

display_text: Timber girded and bound into a building will not be loosed with shaking: So a heart established in due season on well advised counsel will not be afraid. A heart settled upon a thoughtful understanding Is as an ornament of plaister on a polished wall. Pales set on a high place will not stand against the wind: So a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool will not stand against any fear.
plain: Timber bound into a building won't shake loose, and a heart settled on sound advice won't be afraid. But stakes on a hilltop fall in the wind, and a fool's fearful heart gives way to any fear.
core_idea: A heart grounded in good counsel stands firm

text: Whoso casts a stone at birds frays them away; And he that upbraids a friend will dissolve friendship. If you have drawn a sword against a friend, despair not; For there may be a returning. If you have opened your mouth against a friend, fear not; For there may be a reconciling; Except it be for upbraiding, and arrogance, and disclosing of a secret, and a treacherous blow: For these things every friend will flee.
note: A falling-out with a friend; hope of reconciliation

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone who has fought with a friend and wonders if the friendship can be repaired.

display_text: Whoso casts a stone at birds frays them away; And he that upbraids a friend will dissolve friendship. If you have drawn a sword against a friend, despair not; For there may be a returning. If you have opened your mouth against a friend, fear not; For there may be a reconciling; Except it be for upbraiding, and arrogance, and disclosing of a secret, and a treacherous blow: For these things every friend will flee.
plain: Taunting a friend ends a friendship. Even after a drawn sword or harsh words there can be reconciliation, but not after insult, arrogance, a betrayed secret or a treacherous blow; those drive any friend away.
core_idea: Friendship survives anger, not betrayal

text: Gain trust with your neighbor in his poverty, That in his prosperity you may have gladness: Abide stedfast to him in the time of his affliction, That you may be heir with him in his inheritance.
note: Standing by someone through their hard times

tags.when_helps: Someone whose friend has fallen on hard times, encouraged to stay loyal through it.

display_text: Gain trust with your neighbor in his poverty, That in his prosperity you may have gladness: Abide stedfast to him in the time of his affliction, That you may be heir with him in his inheritance.
plain: Earn your neighbour's trust while they are poor, so you can share their gladness when they prosper. Stand by them in hard times, so you can share in their good fortune.
core_idea: Stand by people in hard times

text: Who shall set a watch over my mouth, And a seal of shrewdness upon my lips, That I fall not from it, and that my tongue destroy me not?
note: Wishing to guard one's words; regret over speech

tags.when_helps: Someone afraid their tongue will get them into trouble, praying for restraint in speech.

display_text: Who shall set a watch over my mouth, And a seal of shrewdness upon my lips, That I fall not from it, and that my tongue destroy me not?
plain: The speaker wishes someone would guard his mouth and seal his lips with good sense, so that he doesn't slip and his own tongue doesn't destroy him.
core_idea: A prayer to guard one's tongue

text: In three things I was beautified, And stood up beautiful before the Lord and men: The concord of kindred, and friendship of neighbors, And a woman and her husband that walk together in agreement.
note: Harmony in family, neighbours and marriage

tags.when_helps: Someone treasuring harmony at home, with neighbours and in marriage.

display_text: In three things I was beautified, And stood up beautiful before the Lord and men: The concord of kindred, and friendship of neighbors, And a woman and her husband that walk together in agreement.
plain: The speaker names three things that made her beautiful before God and people: relatives who get along, neighbours who are friends, and a wife and husband who live in harmony.
core_idea: Harmony in family, neighbours and marriage is beautiful

plain_judge.issue: Assigns the speaker a female gender, which the passage does not state.

text: In your youth you have not gathered, And how should you find in your old age? How beautiful a thing is judgement for gray hairs, And for elders to know counsel! How beautiful is the wisdom of old men, And thought and counsel to men that are in honor! Much experience is the crown of old men; And their glorying is the fear of the Lord.
note: Ageing well; the wisdom that experience brings

tags.when_helps: Someone growing older who wonders whether they have gathered the wisdom and experience their years should bring.

display_text: In your youth you have not gathered, And how should you find in your old age? How beautiful a thing is judgement for gray hairs, And for elders to know counsel! How beautiful is the wisdom of old men, And thought and counsel to men that are in honor! Much experience is the crown of old men; And their glorying is the fear of the Lord.
plain: If you gathered nothing when young, how will you have anything when old? Good judgement and counsel are beautiful in the grey-haired. Long experience is the crown of the old, and their pride is the fear of the Lord.
core_idea: Experience is the crown of old age

text: Whether a man be rich or poor, A good heart makes at all times a cheerful countenance.
note: Contentment comes from the heart, not wealth

tags.when_helps: Someone measuring their worth by wealth who needs reminding that a good heart brings cheer whether rich or poor.

display_text: Whether a man be rich or poor, A good heart makes at all times a cheerful countenance.
plain: Rich or poor, a good heart always brings a cheerful face.
core_idea: A good heart gives a cheerful face

text: Of three things my heart was afraid; And concerning the fourth kind I made supplication: The slander of a city, and the assembly of a multitude, and a false accusation: All these are more grievous than death.
note: Fear of slander, public shame and false accusation

tags.when_helps: Someone afraid of slander, a mob or a false accusation who needs to know others have felt this dread too.

display_text: Of three things my heart was afraid; And concerning the fourth kind I made supplication: The slander of a city, and the assembly of a multitude, and a false accusation: All these are more grievous than death.
plain: The speaker was afraid of three things, and prayed about a fourth: a whole city's slander, a mob gathering, and a false accusation. All of these are worse than death.
core_idea: Slander and false accusation are worse than death

text: The furnace will prove the potter’s vessels; And the trial of a man is in his reasoning. The fruit of a tree declares the husbandry thereof; So is the utterance of the thought of the heart of a man. Praise no man before you hear him reason; For this is the trial of men.
note: Judging character by how someone thinks and speaks

tags.when_helps: Someone judging others too quickly, or being tested, who needs reminding that character shows in how one reasons and speaks.

display_text: The furnace will prove the potter’s vessels; And the trial of a man is in his reasoning. The fruit of a tree declares the husbandry thereof; So is the utterance of the thought of the heart of a man. Praise no man before you hear him reason; For this is the trial of men.
plain: A kiln tests a potter's pots, and a person is tested by how they reason. As fruit shows how a tree was tended, words show the heart. Don't praise anyone before you hear them reason.
core_idea: Words reveal the heart; judge by reasoning

text: Love a friend, and keep faith with him: But if you reveal his secrets, You shall not pursue after him; For as a man has destroyed his enemy, So have you destroyed the friendship of your neighbor. And as a bird which you have loosed out of your hand, So have you let your neighbor go, and you will not catch him again: Pursue him not, for he is gone far away, And has escaped as a gazelle out of the snare. For a wound may be bound up, and after reviling there may be a reconcilement; But he that reveals secrets has lost hope.
note: Betraying a friend's trust; a friendship that cannot be recovered

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to reveal a friend's secret, or who has, and must face what that does to trust.

display_text: Love a friend, and keep faith with him: But if you reveal his secrets, You shall not pursue after him; For as a man has destroyed his enemy, So have you destroyed the friendship of your neighbor. And as a bird which you have loosed out of your hand, So have you let your neighbor go, and you will not catch him again: Pursue him not, for he is gone far away, And has escaped as a gazelle out of the snare. For a wound may be bound up, and after reviling there may be a reconcilement; But he that reveals secrets has lost hope.
plain: Love a friend and keep faith. If you reveal their secrets, don't chase them; the friendship is gone like a bird let loose. A wound can heal and insults be forgiven, but betraying secrets leaves no hope.
core_idea: Betraying a secret destroys a friendship for good

text: Forgive your neighbor the hurt that he has done you; And then your sins will be pardoned when you pray. Man cherisheth anger against man; And does he seek healing from the Lord? Upon a man like himself he has no mercy; And does he make supplication for his own sins? He being himself flesh nourishes wrath: Who will make atonement for his sins? Remember your last end, and cease from enmity: Remember corruption and death, and abide in the commandments. Remember the commandments, and be not angry with your neighbor; And remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.
note: Holding a grudge; forgiving as you hope to be forgiven

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone nursing a grudge who needs to see that holding anger while seeking mercy for themselves does not add up.

display_text: Forgive your neighbor the hurt that he has done you; And then your sins will be pardoned when you pray. Man cherisheth anger against man; And does he seek healing from the Lord? Upon a man like himself he has no mercy; And does he make supplication for his own sins? He being himself flesh nourishes wrath: Who will make atonement for his sins? Remember your last end, and cease from enmity: Remember corruption and death, and abide in the commandments. Remember the commandments, and be not angry with your neighbor; And remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.
plain: Forgive your neighbour and your sins will be forgiven when you pray. How can someone nurse anger yet ask the Lord for healing, or refuse mercy yet beg it? Remember death, drop hostility, overlook others' faults.
core_idea: Forgive others to be forgiven yourself

plain_judge.issue: Drops remembering the commandments and covenant; 'ignorance' broadened to 'faults'.

text: A contention begun in haste kindles a fire; And a hasty fighting sheds blood. If you blow a spark, it will burn; And if you spit upon it, it will be quenched: And both these shall come out of your mouth.
note: Escalating or calming a quarrel with your words

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
keywords: blow a spark or spit on it
tags.when_helps: Someone about to say something heated in a quarrel, who can choose whether their words fan or quench it.

display_text: A contention begun in haste kindles a fire; And a hasty fighting sheds blood. If you blow a spark, it will burn; And if you spit upon it, it will be quenched: And both these shall come out of your mouth.
plain: A quarrel started in haste lights a fire, and a hasty fight sheds blood. Blow on a spark and it burns; spit on it and it goes out, and both come from the same mouth.
core_idea: Your mouth can fan or quench a quarrel

text: The stroke of a whip makes a mark in the flesh; But the stroke of a tongue will break bones. Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: Yet not so many as those who have fallen because of the tongue.
note: Wounding words; the damage of harsh speech

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
keywords: stroke of a tongue breaks bones
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to wound with words, or hurt by harsh words, who needs to weigh their real force.

display_text: The stroke of a whip makes a mark in the flesh; But the stroke of a tongue will break bones. Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: Yet not so many as those who have fallen because of the tongue.
plain: A whip leaves a mark on the skin, but a tongue's blow breaks bones. Many have died by the sword, but not as many as have fallen because of the tongue.
core_idea: The tongue wounds more than the sword

text: The chief thing for life is water, and bread, And a garment, and a house to cover shame. Better is the life of a poor man under a shelter of logs, Than sumptuous fare in another man’s house. With little or with much, be well satisfied.
note: Contentment with little; independence over luxury

tags.when_helps: Someone with little who envies others' comfort and needs to hear that a humble home of one's own is enough.

display_text: The chief thing for life is water, and bread, And a garment, and a house to cover shame. Better is the life of a poor man under a shelter of logs, Than sumptuous fare in another man’s house. With little or with much, be well satisfied.
plain: What life really needs is water, bread, clothing and a roof. A poor man's life under a log shelter is better than lavish food in someone else's house. Whether you have little or much, be content.
core_idea: Be content with little or much

text: Better is a poor man, being sound and strong of constitution, Than a rich man that is plagued in his body. Health and a good constitution are better than all gold; And a strong body than wealth without measure. There is no riches better than health of body; And there is no gladness above the joy of the heart.
note: Health and inner joy matter more than wealth

tags.when_helps: Someone chasing wealth, or recovering their health, who needs reminding that a sound body and glad heart outrank riches.

display_text: Better is a poor man, being sound and strong of constitution, Than a rich man that is plagued in his body. Health and a good constitution are better than all gold; And a strong body than wealth without measure. There is no riches better than health of body; And there is no gladness above the joy of the heart.
plain: A poor man who is healthy is better off than a rich man plagued by illness. Health is worth more than all gold; no wealth beats a healthy body, and no gladness beats joy of heart.
core_idea: Health is worth more than wealth

text: Give not over your soul to sorrow; And afflict not yourself in your own counsel. Gladness of heart is the life of a man; And the joyfulness of a man is length of days. Love your own soul, and comfort your heart: And remove sorrow far from you; For sorrow has destroyed many, And there is no profit therein. Envy and wrath shorten a man’s days; And care brings old age before the time.
note: Sadness, rumination and worry; be kind to yourself

tags.when_helps: Someone sinking into sorrow and worry who needs gentle permission to comfort their own heart.

display_text: Give not over your soul to sorrow; And afflict not yourself in your own counsel. Gladness of heart is the life of a man; And the joyfulness of a man is length of days. Love your own soul, and comfort your heart: And remove sorrow far from you; For sorrow has destroyed many, And there is no profit therein. Envy and wrath shorten a man’s days; And care brings old age before the time.
plain: Don't give yourself over to sorrow or torment yourself with your thoughts. Gladness of heart is life and lengthens your days. Comfort your heart and push sorrow away; envy, anger and worry age you early.
core_idea: Don't give yourself to sorrow; gladness is life

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'love your own soul' and 'sorrow has destroyed many'.

text: Wakefulness that comes of riches consumes the flesh, And the anxiety thereof puts away sleep. Wakeful anxiety will crave slumber; And in a sore disease sleep will be broken.
note: Money worries and sleepless nights

tags.when_helps: Someone lying awake worrying about money or possessions, who may see how that worry consumes them.

display_text: Wakefulness that comes of riches consumes the flesh, And the anxiety thereof puts away sleep. Wakeful anxiety will crave slumber; And in a sore disease sleep will be broken.
plain: Lying awake over wealth wears down the body, and its worries drive away sleep. Anxious wakefulness longs for sleep, and serious illness breaks it.
core_idea: Worry over money steals sleep

text: Wine is as good as life to men, If you drink it in its measure: What life is there to a man that is without wine? And it has been created to make men glad. Wine drunk in season and to satisfy Is joy of heart, and gladness of soul: Wine drunk largely is bitterness of soul, With provocation and conflict.
note: Drinking in moderation versus excess

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone enjoying a drink or celebrating who wants to keep pleasure from turning into bitterness and conflict.

display_text: Wine is as good as life to men, If you drink it in its measure: What life is there to a man that is without wine? And it has been created to make men glad. Wine drunk in season and to satisfy Is joy of heart, and gladness of soul: Wine drunk largely is bitterness of soul, With provocation and conflict.
plain: Wine drunk in moderation is as good as life; it was made to gladden people. Taken at the right time and amount it brings joy, but drunk heavily it brings bitterness and fighting.
core_idea: Wine in measure gladdens; in excess embitters

text: Speak, young man, if there be need of you; Yet scarcely if you be twice asked. Sum up your speech, many things in few words; Be as one that knows and yet holds his tongue.
note: Speaking briefly; restraint when young or new

situations: a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: A young or new person unsure when to speak up, looking for counsel on brevity and restraint.

display_text: Speak, young man, if there be need of you; Yet scarcely if you be twice asked. Sum up your speech, many things in few words; Be as one that knows and yet holds his tongue.
plain: Young man, speak if you are needed, but hardly at all unless asked twice. Keep it short, say much in few words, and be like someone who knows but holds their tongue.
core_idea: Speak little; say much in few words

text: Do nothing without counsel; And when you have once done, repent not.
note: Making decisions carefully, then not second-guessing

tags.when_helps: Someone agonising over a decision, or second-guessing one already made, who needs to seek advice then let it rest.

display_text: Do nothing without counsel; And when you have once done, repent not.
plain: Do nothing without taking advice, and once you have acted, don't regret it.
core_idea: Seek advice first, then don't regret

text: Vain and false hopes are for a man void of understanding; And dreams give wings to fools. As one that catches at a shadow, and follows after the wind, So is he that sets his mind on dreams.
note: Chasing false hopes and fantasies

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone pinning everything on fanciful hopes who might benefit from a sober reminder to stay grounded.

display_text: Vain and false hopes are for a man void of understanding; And dreams give wings to fools. As one that catches at a shadow, and follows after the wind, So is he that sets his mind on dreams.
plain: Empty and false hopes belong to a person without sense, and dreams lift fools off the ground. Fixing your mind on dreams is like grabbing at a shadow or chasing the wind.
core_idea: Chasing dreams is grasping at shadows

text: A well-instructed man knows many things; And he that has much experience will declare understanding. He that has no experience knows few things: But he that has wandered shall increase his skill. In my wandering I have seen many things; And more than my words is my understanding. Ofttimes was I in danger even to death; And I was preserved because of these things.
note: Learning from experience, travel and hardship

tags.when_helps: Someone who has wandered or faced danger and wonders what it was for; their experience has become understanding.

display_text: A well-instructed man knows many things; And he that has much experience will declare understanding. He that has no experience knows few things: But he that has wandered shall increase his skill. In my wandering I have seen many things; And more than my words is my understanding. Ofttimes was I in danger even to death; And I was preserved because of these things.
plain: A well-taught, experienced person understands much; the inexperienced know little, but travel builds skill. The speaker has seen much in his wanderings, understands more than he can say, and survived deadly dangers because of it.
core_idea: Experience and travel deepen understanding

text: Every friend will say, I also am his friend: But there is a friend, which is only a friend in name. Is there not a grief in it even to death, When a companion and friend is turned to enmity?
note: Betrayal by a friend; false friendship

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone hurt by a friend who has turned against them.

display_text: Every friend will say, I also am his friend: But there is a friend, which is only a friend in name. Is there not a grief in it even to death, When a companion and friend is turned to enmity?
plain: Everyone says they are your friend, but some friends are friends only in name. Isn't it a grief close to death when a companion and friend turns into an enemy?
core_idea: A friend turned enemy is a deathly grief

text: Forget not a friend in your soul; And be not unmindful of him in your riches.

tags.when_helps: Someone whose fortunes have risen, reminded not to forget friends who were there before.

display_text: Forget not a friend in your soul; And be not unmindful of him in your riches.
plain: Don't forget a friend in your heart, and don't neglect them when you become rich.
core_idea: Don't forget friends when you prosper

text: And make the counsel of your heart to stand; For there is none more faithful to you than it. For a man’s soul is sometime wont to bring him tidings, More than seven watchmen that sit on high on a watch-tower.
note: Trusting your own inner judgement in decisions

tags.when_helps: Someone torn between others' advice who needs to trust their own inner counsel.

display_text: And make the counsel of your heart to stand; For there is none more faithful to you than it. For a man’s soul is sometime wont to bring him tidings, More than seven watchmen that sit on high on a watch-tower.
plain: Hold firm to what your own heart advises, because nothing is more faithful to you. A person's soul can sometimes tell them more than seven watchmen sitting high on a tower.
core_idea: Trust the counsel of your own heart

text: Let reason be the beginning of every work, And let counsel go before every action.
note: Thinking before acting; decisions

tags.when_helps: Someone about to act on impulse who could pause to think it through first.

display_text: Let reason be the beginning of every work, And let counsel go before every action.
plain: Let reasoning begin every task, and let advice come before every action.
core_idea: Think and take advice before acting

text: My son, prove your soul in your life, And see what is evil for it, and give not that to it. For all things are not profitable for all men, Neither has every soul pleasure in every thing.
note: Knowing what is good for you; self-knowledge

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone learning which pleasures harm them and choosing not to indulge them.

display_text: My son, prove your soul in your life, And see what is evil for it, and give not that to it. For all things are not profitable for all men, Neither has every soul pleasure in every thing.
plain: Test your soul throughout your life, notice what is bad for it, and don't give it that. Not everything is good for everyone, and not everyone enjoys the same things.
core_idea: Learn what harms you and avoid it

text: My son, let your tears fall over the dead, And as one that suffers grievously begin lamentation; And wind up his body according to his due, And neglect not his burial. Make bitter weeping, and make passionate wailing, And let your mourning be according to his desert, For one day or two, lest you be evil spoken of: And so be comforted for your sorrow.
note: Permission to mourn a death fully

tags.when_helps: Someone newly bereaved who needs permission to mourn fully and then to be comforted.

display_text: My son, let your tears fall over the dead, And as one that suffers grievously begin lamentation; And wind up his body according to his due, And neglect not his burial. Make bitter weeping, and make passionate wailing, And let your mourning be according to his desert, For one day or two, lest you be evil spoken of: And so be comforted for your sorrow.
plain: Let your tears fall for the dead and lament deeply; prepare the body and don't neglect the burial. Mourn bitterly as the person deserves, for a day or two, and then be comforted in your sorrow.
core_idea: Mourn fully, then let yourself be comforted

plain_judge.issue: Drops the stated motive for mourning: so you are not evil spoken of.

text: Give not your heart to sorrow: Put it away, remembering the last end: Forget it not, for there is no returning again: Him you shall not profit, and you will hurt yourself. Remember the sentence upon him; for so also shall your be; Yesterday for me, and today for you. When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest; And be comforted for him, when his spirit departs from him.
note: Grief that lingers too long; letting the dead rest

keywords: yesterday for me, today for you
tags.when_helps: Someone whose grief has gone on long and is hurting them, encouraged to let the dead rest.

display_text: Give not your heart to sorrow: Put it away, remembering the last end: Forget it not, for there is no returning again: Him you shall not profit, and you will hurt yourself. Remember the sentence upon him; for so also shall yours be; Yesterday for me, and today for you. When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest; And be comforted for him, when his spirit departs from him.
plain: Don't give your heart to sorrow; remember your own end. The dead won't return, and grief harms you without helping them. Their fate will be yours: yesterday me, today you. Let their memory rest, and be comforted.
core_idea: Don't drown in grief; the dead are at rest

text: There is wrath, and jealousy, and trouble, and disquiet, And fear of death, and anger, and strife; And in the time of rest upon his bed His night sleep does change his knowledge. A little or nothing is his resting, And afterward in his sleep, as in a day of keeping watch, He is troubled in the vision of his heart, As one that has escaped from the front of battle. In the very time of his deliverance he awakens, And marvels that the fear is nothing.
note: Night anxiety and sleepless fear that proves empty

tags.when_helps: Someone whose worries chase them into sleepless or troubled nights, who may find the fear was nothing.

display_text: There is wrath, and jealousy, and trouble, and disquiet, And fear of death, and anger, and strife; And in the time of rest upon his bed His night sleep does change his knowledge. A little or nothing is his resting, And afterward in his sleep, as in a day of keeping watch, He is troubled in the vision of his heart, As one that has escaped from the front of battle. In the very time of his deliverance he awakens, And marvels that the fear is nothing.
plain: People live with anger, jealousy, trouble, fear of death and strife. Even in bed their rest is short; in sleep they are troubled as if fleeing a battle, then wake amazed the fear was nothing.
core_idea: Anxiety haunts even our sleep, then proves empty

text: The life of one that labores, and is contented, shall be made sweet; And he that finds a treasure is above both.
note: Contentment in honest work

tags.when_helps: Someone working hard for modest return, reminded that contentment makes such a life sweet.

display_text: The life of one that labors, and is contented, shall be made sweet; And he that finds a treasure is above both.
plain: The life of someone who works and is content will be sweet, but finding a treasure is better than both.
core_idea: Contented work makes life sweet

text: Wine and music rejoice the heart; And the love of wisdom is above both.
note: Pleasure versus the deeper joy of wisdom

tags.when_helps: Someone enjoying life's pleasures who might value the love of wisdom even more.

display_text: Wine and music rejoice the heart; And the love of wisdom is above both.
plain: Wine and music gladden the heart, but the love of wisdom is better than both.
core_idea: Love of wisdom beats wine and music

text: Don’t be afraid of the sentence of death; Remember those who have been before you, and that come after: This is the sentence from the Lord over all flesh. And why do you refuse, when it is the good pleasure of the Most High? Whether it be ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years, There is no inquisition of life in the grave.
note: Fear of death; mortality shared by all

tags.when_helps: Someone afraid of their own death who could find steadiness in its being shared by everyone.

display_text: Don’t be afraid of the sentence of death; Remember those who have been before you, and that come after: This is the sentence from the Lord over all flesh. And why do you refuse, when it is the good pleasure of the Most High? Whether it be ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years, There is no inquisition of life in the grave.
plain: Don't fear the sentence of death; it is the Lord's decree for everyone before and after you, so why resist it? Whether you live ten, a hundred or a thousand years, the grave doesn't ask.
core_idea: Death comes to all; don't fear it

plain_judge.issue: Folds 'good pleasure of the Most High' into decree; 'grave doesn't ask' loosens the meaning.

text: Have regard to your name; For it continueth with you longer than a thousand great treasures of gold. A good life has its number of days; And a good name continueth forever.
note: Reputation and legacy outlasting wealth

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to trade their good name for wealth, reminded which lasts longer.

display_text: Have regard to your name; For it continueth with you longer than a thousand great treasures of gold. A good life has its number of days; And a good name continueth forever.
plain: Take care of your reputation; it stays with you longer than a thousand fortunes in gold. A good life lasts a limited number of days, but a good name lasts forever.
core_idea: A good name outlasts life and gold

text: My children, keep instruction in peace: But wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seen, What profit is in them both? Better is a man that hides his foolishness Than a man that hides his wisdom.
note: Sharing your gifts rather than hiding them

tags.when_helps: Someone who holds back what they know out of shyness, urged to share it.

display_text: My children, keep instruction in peace: But wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seen, What profit is in them both? Better is a man that hides his foolishness Than a man that hides his wisdom.
plain: Keep what you have been taught, but hidden wisdom and buried treasure are of no use to anyone. Better someone who hides their foolishness than someone who hides their wisdom.
core_idea: Hidden wisdom is useless; share it

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'in peace' from keeping instruction.

text: A mist coming speedily is the healing of all things; A dew coming after heat shall bring cheerfulness.
note: Relief arriving after a hard, scorching time

tags.when_helps: Someone worn out by a hard stretch who needs a gentle image of coming relief.

display_text: A mist coming speedily is the healing of all things; A dew coming after heat shall bring cheerfulness.
plain: A mist that comes quickly heals everything, and dew that falls after the heat brings cheer.
core_idea: Relief after heat brings healing and cheer

text: We may say many things, yet shall we not attain; And the sum of our words is, He is all.
note: Limits of words before the divine; humility

tags.when_helps: Someone at the limits of words before the divine.

display_text: We may say many things, yet shall we not attain; And the sum of our words is, He is all.
plain: We can say many things and still fall short; the sum of all our words is that he, God, is everything.
core_idea: Words fall short; God is all

text: My soul drew near even to death, And my life was near to the grave beneath. They compassed me on every side, And there was none to help me. I was looking for the succour of men, And it was not. And I remembered your mercy, O Lord, And your working which has been from everlasting, How you deliver those who wait for you, And save them out of the hand of the enemies.
note: Feeling abandoned by everyone; finding hope in prayer

tags.when_helps: Someone near the edge with no one to help, reminded that crying out to God has brought deliverance before.

display_text: My soul drew near even to death, And my life was near to the grave beneath. They compassed me on every side, And there was none to help me. I was looking for the succour of men, And it was not. And I remembered your mercy, O Lord, And your working which has been from everlasting, How you deliver those who wait for you, And save them out of the hand of the enemies.
plain: The speaker was near death, surrounded, with no one to help and no human aid coming. Then he remembered the Lord's mercy and his age-old works, how he rescues those who wait for him.
core_idea: With no help left, remember God's mercy

text: When I was yet young, Or ever I went abroad, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer. Before the temple I asked for her, And I will seek her out even to the end. From her flower as from the ripening grape my heart delighted in her: My foot trod in uprightness, From my youth I tracked her out. I bowed down my ear a little, and received her, And found for myself much instruction.
note: A lifelong search for wisdom

keywords: from her flower as from the ripening grape
tags.when_helps: Someone drawn to a lifelong search for wisdom who finds delight in pursuing it.

display_text: When I was yet young, Or ever I went abroad, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer. Before the temple I asked for her, And I will seek her out even to the end. From her flower as from the ripening grape my heart delighted in her: My foot trod in uprightness, From my youth I tracked her out. I bowed down my ear a little, and received her, And found for myself much instruction.
plain: While still young, the speaker openly sought wisdom in prayer before the temple and will seek her to the end. He delighted in her, followed her uprightly from youth, listened a little and learned much.
core_idea: Seek wisdom from youth to the end

text: Work your work before the time comes, And in his time he will give you your reward.
note: Doing your work now; patience for reward

tags.when_helps: Someone unsure whether their effort will pay off, urged to do the work now and trust the reward.

display_text: Work your work before the time comes, And in his time he will give you your reward.
plain: Do your work before the time comes, and in his own time God will reward you.
core_idea: Do your work; reward comes in God's time

text: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.
note: not rushing love before its time

tags.when_helps: Someone eager to rush into romance, counselled to let love unfold in its own time.

display_text: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.
plain: The speaker begs the women of Jerusalem, by the deer of the field, not to stir up or awaken love until love itself is ready.
core_idea: Don't awaken love before its time

text: My beloved spoke, and said to me, “Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away. For, behold, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone. The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land. The fig tree ripens her green figs. The vines are in blossom. They give out their fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.”
note: a hard season ending, love and renewal

tags.when_helps: Someone in love or emerging from a hard season, ready to feel spring and renewal.

display_text: My beloved spoke, and said to me, “Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away. For, behold, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone. The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land. The fig tree ripens her green figs. The vines are in blossom. They give out their fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.”
plain: Her beloved calls her to rise and come away with him: winter and rain are over, flowers are out, birds are singing, figs are ripening and the vines are in fragrant blossom.
core_idea: Winter is past; love calls you to come away

text: By night on my bed, I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him. I will get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
note: longing for an absent loved one

tags.when_helps: Someone lying awake searching for a loved one they cannot reach.

display_text: By night on my bed, I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him. I will get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
plain: At night in bed she looked for the one she loves and couldn't find him. She resolves to get up and search the city's streets and squares for him, but still she doesn't find him.
core_idea: Searching for a loved one and not finding

text: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine.
note: mutual belonging in love

tags.when_helps: Someone treasuring a mutual, secure love with a partner.

display_text: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine.
plain: I belong to the one I love, and the one I love belongs to me.
core_idea: Lovers belong wholly to each other

text: Set me as a seal on your heart, as a seal on your arm; for love is strong as death. Jealousy is as cruel as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a very flame of Yahweh. Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.
note: the strength of love; love can't be bought

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling the full force of love and wanting words for how unquenchable and priceless it is.

display_text: Set me as a seal on your heart, as a seal on your arm; for love is strong as death. Jealousy is as cruel as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a very flame of Yahweh. Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.
plain: Keep me as a seal on your heart and arm, for love is as strong as death, its passion a blazing flame of God. No flood can drown love, and anyone trying to buy it with wealth would be scorned.
core_idea: Love is strong as death and can't be bought

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'jealousy is as cruel as Sheol'.

text: And now we follow you with all our heart, we fear you, and seek your face. Put us not to shame: but deal with us after your kindness, and according to the multitude of your mercy.
note: Shame and guilt; asking for mercy and a fresh start

tags.when_helps: A believer who fears disgrace and wants to commit wholeheartedly while asking for mercy.

display_text: And now we follow you with all our heart, we fear you, and seek your face. Put us not to shame: but deal with us after your kindness, and according to the multitude of your mercy.
plain: A prayer to God: we follow you wholeheartedly, revere you and seek your face. Don't let us be shamed, but treat us with your kindness and your great mercy.
core_idea: We follow you; deal with us in mercy

display_text: O give thanks to the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endures forever.
plain: Give thanks to the Lord, because he is good and his mercy lasts forever.
core_idea: Give thanks; God's mercy lasts forever

text: To the pure, all things are pure; but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but both their mind and their conscience are defiled.
note: how our inner state colours what we see

keywords: to the pure all things are pure
tags.when_helps: Someone who sees corruption everywhere and needs to consider how their own mind colours what they see.

display_text: To the pure, all things are pure; but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but both their mind and their conscience are defiled.
plain: To people who are pure, everything is pure; but to those who are corrupted and don't believe, nothing is pure, because their very minds and consciences are corrupted.
core_idea: To the pure, all things are pure

text: Don’t despise your mother. Honor her all the days of your life, and do that which is pleasing to her, and don’t grieve her. Remember, my child, that she has seen many dangers for you, when you were in her womb.
note: honoring and caring for one's mother

situations: caring for a sick or ageing relative
tags.when_helps: Someone with a strained or neglected relationship with their mother, reconsidering what they owe her.

display_text: Don’t despise your mother. Honor her all the days of your life, and do that which is pleasing to her, and don’t grieve her. Remember, my child, that she has seen many dangers for you, when you were in her womb.
plain: Tobit tells his child not to look down on their mother but to honour and please her and not grieve her all her life, remembering the dangers she went through for them while pregnant.
core_idea: Honour your mother all her days

text: Give alms from your possessions. When you give alms, don’t let your eye be envious. Don’t turn away your face from any poor man, and the face of God won’t be turned away from you. As your possessions are, give alms of it according to your abundance. If you have little, don’t be afraid to give alms according to that little; for you lay up a good treasure for yourself against the day of necessity; because alms-giving delivers from death, and doesn’t allow you to come into darkness.
note: generosity, even when you have little

tags.when_helps: Someone worried about money who hesitates to give, wondering whether a small gift is worth anything.

display_text: Give alms from your possessions. When you give alms, don’t let your eye be envious. Don’t turn away your face from any poor man, and the face of God won’t be turned away from you. As your possessions are, give alms of it according to your abundance. plain: Give to the poor from what you own, without begrudging it, and God won't turn from you. Give much if you have much, and a little without fear if you have little; giving protects from death and darkness.
core_idea: Give to the poor from whatever you have

plain_judge.issue: Drops giving as treasure laid up against the day of necessity.

text: And what you yourself hate, do to no man.
note: treating others as you wish to be treated

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to treat another person badly, needing a simple test for how to act.

display_text: And what you yourself hate, do to no man.
plain: Don't do to anyone what you yourself hate.
core_idea: Don't do to others what you hate

text: Ask counsel of every man who is wise, and don’t despise any counsel that is profitable.
note: seeking good advice when making decisions

tags.when_helps: Someone facing a decision alone and reluctant to ask others for advice.

display_text: Ask counsel of every man who is wise, and don’t despise any counsel that is profitable.
plain: Ask advice from every wise person, and don't scorn any useful counsel.
core_idea: Seek advice from the wise

text: And fear not, my child, because we are made poor. You have much wealth, if you fear God, and depart from all sin, and do that which is pleasing in his sight.”
note: facing poverty; true wealth is goodness

tags.when_helps: A believer frightened by sudden poverty, needing to hear that their real wealth lies elsewhere.

display_text: And fear not, my child, because we are made poor. You have much wealth, if you fear God, and depart from all sin, and do that which is pleasing in his sight.
plain: Tobit tells his child not to fear because they have become poor: you have great wealth if you revere God, turn away from all sin and do what pleases him.
core_idea: Fearing God is true wealth, even in poverty

text: Don’t be greedy to add money to money; but let it be as refuse compared to our child. For what the Lord has given us to live is enough for us.”
note: contentment; family matters more than money

tags.when_helps: A parent tempted to chase money at the cost of their family, reminded that what they have is enough.

display_text: Don’t be greedy to add money to money; but let it be as refuse compared to our child. For what the Lord has given us to live is enough for us.
plain: Don't be greedy to pile up money; let it be rubbish compared to our child. What the Lord has given us to live on is enough.
core_idea: What God gives is enough; people matter more

text: Do good, and evil won’t find you. Good is prayer with fasting, alms, and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold.
note: integrity over wealth; generosity

tags.when_helps: Someone torn between gain and goodness who needs a reminder that a little honestly held beats much.

display_text: Do good, and evil won’t find you. Good is prayer with fasting, alms, and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold.
plain: Do good and evil won't find you. Prayer with fasting, giving and righteousness are good. A little gained honestly is better than much gained wrongly, and giving to the poor is better than hoarding gold.
core_idea: A little with goodness beats much without

text: Beware then of unprofitable murmuring, And refrain your tongue from backbiting; Because no secret utterance will go on its way void, And a mouth that belies destroys a soul.
note: Gossip, complaining and the harm of careless words

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to grumble or gossip about others who needs a warning to hold their tongue.

display_text: Beware then of unprofitable murmuring, And refrain your tongue from backbiting; Because no secret utterance will go on its way void, And a mouth that belies destroys a soul.
plain: Beware of pointless grumbling and keep your tongue from backbiting, because no secret word goes without effect, and a lying mouth destroys the soul.
core_idea: Grumbling and lies harm your own soul

text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, And no torment will touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died; And their departure was accounted to be their hurt, And their journeying away from us to be their ruin: But they are in peace.
note: Grief for the dead; consolation that they are at peace

tags.when_helps: A believer mourning someone good who needs to trust they are now at peace.

display_text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, And no torment will touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died; And their departure was accounted to be their hurt, And their journeying away from us to be their ruin: But they are in peace.
plain: The souls of the righteous are in God's hand and no torment will touch them. To foolish eyes they seemed to die, and their leaving looked like disaster and ruin, but they are at peace.
core_idea: The righteous dead are at peace in God's hand

text: But a righteous man, though he die before his time, will be at rest. (For honorable old age is not that which stands in length of time, Nor is its measure given by number of years: But understanding is gray hairs to men, And an unspotted life is ripe old age.)
note: Grief over early death; a life measured by quality

tags.when_helps: Someone grieving a person who died young, consoled that a life's worth is not measured in years.

display_text: But a righteous man, though he die before his time, will be at rest. (For honorable old age is not that which stands in length of time, Nor is its measure given by number of years: But understanding is gray hairs to men, And an unspotted life is ripe old age.)
plain: A righteous person who dies young will be at rest. Honourable old age isn't measured by length of time or number of years; understanding is a person's grey hair, and a blameless life is ripe old age.
core_idea: A good life, not long years, is true old age

text: Wisdom is radiant and fades not away; And easily is she saw those who love her, And found of those who seek her. She forestalleth those who desire to know her, making herself first known. note: Seeking wisdom; wisdom is near to those who look

tags.when_helps: Someone searching for wisdom who is told it is near to those who seek it.

display_text: Wisdom is radiant and fades not away; And easily is she saw those who love her, And found of those who seek her. She forestalleth those who desire to know her, making herself first known. He that rises up early to seek her will have no toil, For he will find her sitting at his gates. For to think upon her is perfectness of understanding, And he that watches for her sake will quickly be free from care.
plain: Wisdom is radiant and never fades; those who love and seek her find her easily, as she shows herself first. Whoever rises early finds her at the door; thinking of her frees you from worry.

text: I myself also am mortal, like to all, And am sprung from one born of the earth, the man first formed, And in the womb of a mother was I moulded into flesh in the time of ten months, Being compacted in blood of the seed of man and pleasure that came with sleep. And I also, when I was born, drew in the common air, And fell upon the kindred earth, Uttering, like all, for my first voice, the selfsame wail: In swaddling clothes was I nursed, and with watchful cares. For no king had any other first beginning; But all men have one entrance into life, and a like departure.
note: Humility; shared mortality of the great and small

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling either above or below others who is reminded all share the same birth and death.

display_text: I myself also am mortal, like to all, And am sprung from one born of the earth, the man first formed, And in the womb of a mother was I moulded into flesh in the time of ten months, Being compacted in blood of the seed of man and pleasure that came with sleep. And I also, when I was born, drew in the common air, And fell upon the kindred earth, Uttering, like all, for my first voice, the selfsame wail: In swaddling clothes was I nursed, and with watchful cares. For no king had any other first beginning; But all men have one entrance into life, and a like departure.
plain: The king says he is mortal like everyone: formed in a womb, born breathing the same air, giving the same first cry, nursed with care. No king begins differently; all enter and leave life alike.
core_idea: Kings and all people share one birth and death

text: For what man will know the counsel of God? Or who will conceive what the Lord willeth? For the thoughts of mortals are timorous, And our plans are prone to fail. For a corruptible body weighs down the soul, And the earthy frame lies heavy on a mind that is full of cares. And hardly do we divine the things that are on earth, And the things that are close at hand we find with labor; But the things that are in the heavens who ever yet traced out?
note: Uncertainty, failed plans and the limits of understanding

keywords: our plans are prone to fail
tags.when_helps: Someone anxious that their plans may fail who can rest in the limits of human understanding.

display_text: For what man will know the counsel of God? Or who will conceive what the Lord willeth? For the thoughts of mortals are timorous, And our plans are prone to fail. plain: Who can know God's plan or will? Human thoughts are timid and our plans fail; the body weighs down the soul and the worried mind. We barely grasp earthly things, so who has traced heavenly ones?
core_idea: Human minds can't fathom God's plan

text: For you love all things that are, And abhor none of the things which you did make; For never would you have formed anything if you did hate it. And how would anything have endured, except you had willed it? Or that which was not called by you, how would it have been preserved? But you spare all things, because they are your, O Soverign Lord, you lover of men’s lives; For your incorruptible spirit is in all things.
note: Feeling unloved or worthless; everything that exists is loved

keywords: you love all things that are
tags.when_helps: A believer who feels unloved or unworthy, reminded that God loves all that exists.

display_text: For you love all things that are, And abhor none of the things which you did make; For never would you have formed anything if you did hate it. plain: A prayer to God: you love everything that exists and hate nothing you made, or you wouldn't have made it. You spare all things because they are yours, Lord who loves life; your spirit is in everything.
core_idea: God loves everything he made; his spirit is in all

text: For wickedness, condemned by a witness within, is a coward thing, And, being pressed hard by conscience, always forecasts the worst lot: For fear is nothing else but a surrender of the help which reason offers; And from within the heart the expectation of them being less Maketh of greater account the ignorance of the cause that brings the torment.
note: Guilty conscience and fear; fear as abandoning reason

tags.when_helps: Someone whose guilty conscience feeds constant fear of the worst.

display_text: For wickedness, condemned by a witness within, is a coward thing, And, being pressed hard by conscience, always forecasts the worst lot: For fear is nothing else but a surrender of the help which reason offers; And from within the heart the expectation of them being less Maketh of greater account the ignorance of the cause that brings the torment.
plain: Wickedness, condemned by its own conscience, is cowardly and always expects the worst. Fear is simply giving up the help reason offers, and the less help we expect within, the more frightening the unknown becomes.
core_idea: Fear is abandoning the help of reason
